## Restart 1282 addendum — Project read and master-link store authority

Restart 1282 reread the complete current MenuList Firestore ruleset and traced
project reads and direct master linking from authenticated claims through
browser DAL queries, nested and legacy rule paths, linked-outlet server routes,
public consumers, and the broad tenant/store emulator. One P1 authorization
defect was confirmed and closed, so `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains `0`.

### AUDIT-PROJECT-CROSS-STORE-READ-AUTHORITY-001 — Project reads and direct links accepted tenant-only authority

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** `AUDIT-PROJECT-CROSS-STORE-READ-AUTHORITY-001`
  / P1 / Closed locally in restart 1282; QA Firestore-rules deployment blocked
  by missing Firebase CLI authentication.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** `firestore.rules` nested
  `projects/{tId}/{sId}/{projectId}` read, legacy flat-project read,
  `isValidNewMasterProjectReference`, and scoped identity helpers;
  `src/database/projects/index.ts::getProjectDataByStore`; project document and
  master-link authority; authenticated Firebase claims → project read/link →
  owner editor and linked-outlet menu consumers.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger:** project documents are produced by the existing
  scoped project DAL and server-linked-outlet writers. Any authenticated owner
  who knew a project path or supplied another same-tenant store to the browser
  DAL could trigger the read; a direct first-link update could target a master
  project in an unassigned same-tenant store.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** nested project reads and the browser query
  proved tenant membership only, legacy flat reads ignored store claims, and
  direct master-link validation proved only that the target existed in another
  store of the same tenant. Signed `storeIds` are the existing store authority,
  but these branches did not use them. Project access and link targets must
  require current store membership unless the caller has the explicit platform
  override.
- **Security/tenant/data/public/cache impact:** no cross-tenant path was found,
  but store-level authorization within a tenant was bypassable, exposing menu
  truth and permitting a direct linked relationship across an unauthorized
  store boundary. The repair changes admission only; it does not mutate legacy
  documents, public output, cache keys, or invalidation behavior.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** nested and legacy reads now require
  tenant-plus-store membership and nested reads also validate any present
  embedded project/tenant/store aliases against the path. A new master link
  requires access to the target master store. The browser DAL fails before a
  Firestore query when the session lacks that store. Existing platform access,
  own-store access, and exact mapped multi-store access remain supported.
- **Files changed:** `firestore.rules`,
  `src/database/projects/index.ts`,
  `scripts/verification/test-tenant-store-scoped-rules.ts`,
  `scripts/verification/verify-multi-location-boundary.js`,
  Multi-Outlet Firebase/test documentation, changelog, and this audit ledger.
- **Regression/validation/re-audit:** the real Firestore emulator proves
  own-store success, same-tenant unassigned-store denial, mapped multi-store
  success, foreign-tenant denial, platform override, conflicting embedded
  identity denial, and direct master-link denial/success under the respective
  single-/multi-store claims. `npm run test:tenant-store-scoped-rules`,
  `npm run verify:menu-project-editor-boundary`,
  `npm run verify:pricing-integrity-boundary`,
  `npm run verify:menulist-api-tenant-safety`,
  `npm run verify:multi-location-boundary`,
  `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false`, scoped ESLint, and
  `git diff --check` pass. The verifier's two stale backfill tokens were
  reconciled to the already-implemented transaction replacement contract
  without weakening its explicit old-merge rejection.
- **Deployment evidence:** the first `npx firebase ...` invocation could not
  resolve a package executable. The installed repository CLI was then invoked
  directly with
  `firebase deploy --project menulist-qa --config firebase.json --only firestore:rules --non-interactive`;
  it exited 1 before validation/upload with `Failed to authenticate, have you
  run firebase login?`. No hosted rule revision changed.

## Restart 1280 addendum — shared Creative Editor data-flow closure

Restart 1280 completed a clean line-by-line review of all 8,598 pre-edit lines
of `src/modules/creative-editor/CreativeEditor.tsx`, its complete smoke
verifier, runtime document schema, Fabric adapter/export boundaries, product
callbacks and maintained feature contracts. Document/page state, Fabric
serialization, browser drafts, native/legacy imports, raster sources, AI and
Design Cue operations, history, template save, clipboard and export flows were
traced forward and in reverse. Three P1 and five P2 defects were confirmed and
closed; `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains `0`.

### AUDIT-CREATIVE-EDITOR-STALE-IMAGE-REPLACEMENT-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P1 / closed locally /
  `CreativeEditor.tsx` (`replaceSelectedImageFile`); selected image + owner
  file → asynchronous `FileReader` → selected-layer source mutation.
- **Affected structure/producer/consumer/trigger:** raster `File` and
  `CreativeEditorElement.image`; the initiating selection produced the target,
  while the late callback consumed whichever layer/page was current.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** selection, page or document changes during
  file reading could replace a different image. The completion must remain
  bound to its initiating document, page and element.
- **Security/data/public/cache/backward impact:** wrong owner asset truth could
  enter later save/export; no tenant, Firebase or cache path changed. Valid
  same-layer replacements remain compatible.
- **Fix/tests/validation/closure:** document/page/element identity is captured
  before reading and rechecked before mutation. Raster size/type/signature
  checks run first. The Creative Editor smoke verifier, template registry,
  printable-assets and CampaignCue aggregates pass; closure was confirmed in
  restart 1280.

### AUDIT-CREATIVE-EDITOR-FABRIC-IMPORT-LIVE-MUTATION-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P1 / closed locally /
  `CreativeEditor.tsx` (`importFabricJson`); untrusted legacy JSON → Fabric
  deserialization → neutral document → live editor.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** legacy JSON loaded directly into the live
  canvas before neutral-schema validation. The old wrapper also passed a
  callback to Fabric 7 `loadFromJSON` as though it were completion, but Fabric
  7 defines that callback as a per-object reviver and returns the completion
  Promise. Empty input could hang and nonempty input could serialize after only
  the first revived object, while a rejected commit still left live canvas
  state replaced and could announce success.
- **Security/data/public/cache/backward impact:** malformed, partial or stale
  import content could become visible/exported owner truth. No tenant or
  persistence authority changed. Compatible legacy Fabric JSON remains
  supported.
- **Fix/tests/validation/closure:** imports fully await the Fabric 7 Promise in
  an isolated off-screen canvas, serialize/validate the neutral document, check
  revision ownership, commit only on success and dispose in `finally`. The
  verifier forbids the retired callback-completion pattern; Fabric 7 runtime,
  export and integration gates pass.

### AUDIT-CREATIVE-EDITOR-RASTER-IMPORT-BOUNDARY-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P1 / closed locally /
  `CreativeEditor.tsx` (`importJsonFile`, `importImageFile`,
  `replaceSelectedImageFile`, `isSafeFabricImportPayload`); owner file/JSON →
  image source → document/Fabric/export.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** file MIME metadata was trusted without
  content signatures; a newly introduced 12 MiB file admission conflicted with
  the authoritative 2,000,000-character persisted `src` bound; native/legacy
  JSON could carry unsafe data/SVG sources, and raw Fabric complexity was
  bounded only by the file size after deserialization began.
- **Security/data/public/cache/backward impact:** spoofed or oversized content
  could cross the editor boundary, and valid large input could fail only after
  expensive reading. No server upload or Firebase write occurs in the shared
  editor. Current raster files and curated adapter assets remain supported.
- **Fix/tests/validation/closure:** raster files are capped at 1.4 MB so base64
  stays within the persisted contract and must match PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF magic
  bytes. Native imports reject unsafe image sources; legacy Fabric payloads
  reject unsafe sources, more than 300 objects or more than 5,000 traversed
  nodes before deserialization. Focused and full product gates pass.

### AUDIT-CREATIVE-EDITOR-FABRIC-LOAD-ORDER-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P2 / closed locally /
  `CreativeEditor.tsx` (`loadDocument` and Fabric bootstrap); document/page/
  undo/import mutations → asynchronous Fabric object/image load → live canvas.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** overlapping loads had no ordering or
  generation ownership, so an older slow image/document could complete after a
  newer page and replace its selection/canvas. Bootstrap also captured the
  mount-time document instead of current ref truth.
- **Impact/fix:** loads now serialize through one queue, superseded generations
  cannot publish completion state, canvas identity is rechecked, bootstrap
  reads the current document, and teardown invalidates ownership. No persisted
  shape changes; the smoke/Fabric boundary passes.

### AUDIT-CREATIVE-EDITOR-MUTATION-SCHEMA-BYPASS-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P2 / closed locally /
  `CreativeEditor.tsx` (`commitDocument`, `updateSelected`,
  `syncDocumentFromCanvas`, `getLatestDocumentFromCanvas`); numeric/property/
  Fabric mutation → document/history/autosave/callback/export.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** HTML min/max attributes and TypeScript types
  were treated as enforcement. Cleared/programmatic inputs could produce zero,
  `NaN` or out-of-range values; live selected Fabric state was patched before
  any runtime schema check, and commits accepted the result.
- **Impact/fix/backward compatibility:** invalid runtime truth could enter
  history, autosave, product callbacks or export. Every commit now passes the
  authoritative schema; selected-layer candidates validate before Fabric
  mutation, and invalid Fabric serialization restores the last valid design.
  Valid documents and controls are unchanged.
- **Regression/validation:** source assertions lock both pre-Fabric and commit
  validation. Exact TypeScript, scoped ESLint, editor and product aggregates
  pass.

### AUDIT-CREATIVE-EDITOR-ASYNC-DESIGN-REVISION-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P2 / closed locally /
  `runAiToolAction`, `runDesignCueRequest`, `applyDesignCuePatchSet`; current
  document/selection → product callback/provider work → suggestion or applied
  document.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** React busy state was not an immediate lock,
  requests were not revision-owned, and Design Cue request/apply could overlap.
  A late result could describe or overwrite newer design truth.
- **Impact/fix:** immediate ref single-flight, mutual exclusion, operation
  generations and document-revision checks reject stale results; cancel,
  document replacement and unmount invalidate ownership. No provider, billing
  or persistence contract changed. Design Cue and CampaignCue gates pass.

### AUDIT-CREATIVE-EDITOR-HANDOFF-SINGLE-FLIGHT-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P2 / closed locally /
  `downloadExportBundle`, `runExport`, `saveTemplate`,
  `copyPngToClipboard`, `copyBase64ToClipboard`; owner action → browser
  download/clipboard or product template callback.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** repeated events before rerender could start
  duplicate expensive or external effects, and pending bundle resize
  completions were not invalidated before triggering downloads.
- **Impact/fix:** export, template and clipboard workflows have immediate
  single-flight ownership and lifecycle invalidation; every asynchronous bundle
  completion checks ownership before download. Valid single actions retain
  behavior. Export/Fabric/product gates pass.

### AUDIT-CREATIVE-EDITOR-RASTER-READINESS-CLASSIFICATION-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P2 / closed locally /
  `buildReadinessIssues`; validated local raster file → base64 image element →
  pre-download safety notice.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** all `data:` sources were labelled unsafe,
  including the exact PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF data URLs created by the approved file
  flow. Owners received a false source warning before valid downloads.
- **Public/data/cache impact/fix:** advisory download truth was incorrect but
  no data or cache mutation occurred. Readiness now accepts the bounded raster
  data-URL allowlist while arbitrary data schemes remain unsafe.
- **Regression/validation:** the smoke verifier locks the shared safe-source
  classifier and all editor/product gates pass.

No Firestore rule/index, Storage rule, Firebase Function or product-owned
persistence source changed, so no infrastructure deployment applies. This
restart closes the last runtime/support file but is not a full repository pass.
The regenerated manifest contains 8,512 in-scope files and 313 exclusions:
2,501 reviewed, 1,803 in-progress and 4,208 inventory-only. All 342
runtime/support files are now fingerprint-reviewed; the reverse catalog remains
282 collection families. Documentation links have zero broken links and the
same 62 established founder-media filename warnings.

## Restart 1279 addendum — MyCodex reader lifecycle and persistence

Restart 1279 re-read all 3,618 pre-edit lines of
`MyCodexClientContainer.tsx`, its complete current verifier and connected
static-reader/PWA contracts. Browser storage, document response, navigation,
speech, wake-lock, screenshot, clipboard and Markdown-render flows were traced
in both directions. Seven defects were confirmed and closed;
`consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains `0`.

### AUDIT-MYCODEX-SCROLL-PERSISTENCE-CAP-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / closed locally /
  `MyCodexClientContainer.tsx`; document scroll events → browser-local
  `mycodex:scroll-positions` → next-launch hydration/resume.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** hydration rejected records above
  `MAX_SCROLL_POSITION_DOCS = 200`, but runtime writes never pruned. Reading
  more than 200 documents therefore produced a record the next launch deleted
  in full. Write and read bounds must agree.
- **Data/persistence impact/fix:** browser-only resume state could be lost; no
  server/Firebase data was involved. Every write now sorts by `updatedAt` and
  retains the newest 200 entries before state and localStorage persistence.
- **Regression/validation:** the MyCodex verifier requires write-time pruning.
  PWA/auth aggregate, exact TypeScript, scoped ESLint and diff integrity pass.

### AUDIT-MYCODEX-AUDIO-PREPARATION-LIFECYCLE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / closed locally / favorite/read-later
  playback → bounded document API fetches → speech queue/global browser speech.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** asynchronous document preparation had no
  abort or generation ownership. A stop, replacement, navigation or unmount
  could occur before fetch completion, after which old content could begin
  speaking on the new page.
- **Data/public impact/fix:** wrong private documentation could be read aloud
  after the initiating context ended. Preparation now owns one abort controller
  and generation; all fetches carry its signal and every completion rechecks
  ownership before queue mutation or speech.
- **Regression/validation:** the verifier locks cancellation, fetch signal and
  stale-completion rejection.

### AUDIT-MYCODEX-WAKELOCK-REQUEST-LIFECYCLE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / closed locally / active speech →
  asynchronous Screen Wake Lock request → device display lifecycle.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** release/disable/stop could run while
  acquisition was pending; the late result then reactivated a lock. Concurrent
  acquisition attempts also lacked explicit single-flight ownership.
- **Impact/fix:** request generations now bind acquisition to current
  keep-awake state, one request may be in flight, and a stale acquired lock is
  immediately released without becoming UI truth. Release events alter state
  only for the current sentinel.
- **Regression/validation:** the verifier requires the generation rejection;
  exact TypeScript and lint pass.

### AUDIT-MYCODEX-SCREENSHOT-SINGLE-FLIGHT-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / closed locally / screenshot copy action →
  canvas export → clipboard/share/download.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** React `isCopyingScreenshot` was the only
  guard, so repeated events before rerender could launch parallel high-memory
  canvas and external handoff flows.
- **Impact/fix:** an immediate ref lock now claims the workflow before state
  changes and releases in `finally`. Rendering/export behavior is unchanged.
- **Regression/validation:** the verifier requires the synchronous lock.

### AUDIT-MYCODEX-CLIPBOARD-ACKNOWLEDGEMENT-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / closed locally / copy path/link/content →
  modern or legacy clipboard → owner success toast.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** `document.execCommand('copy')` can return
  `false`; callers ignored that boolean and announced success. Copy truth must
  be acknowledged by the browser.
- **Impact/fix:** a false legacy result now throws into the existing visible
  failure path. Modern Clipboard success and acknowledged legacy success remain
  compatible.
- **Regression/validation:** the verifier requires the exact success check and
  rejection path.

### AUDIT-MYCODEX-DOCUMENT-RESPONSE-SOURCE-PATH-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P3 / closed locally / private document API JSON
  → browser response projector → reader metadata/share/screenshot consumer.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** the body had a 5 MiB cap, but optional
  `sourcePath` accepted any string length while browser-local entries use a
  4,096-character contract.
- **Impact/fix:** the response projector now requires the same bounded
  nonempty source path when present. Markdown byte and server filesystem limits
  are unchanged.
- **Regression/validation:** exact TypeScript and the MyCodex aggregate pass.

### AUDIT-MYCODEX-MARKDOWN-BROAD-TYPE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P3 / closed locally / trusted private Markdown
  → ReactMarkdown AST/component props → alert/link/heading/table renderers.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** recursive transforms and every renderer
  used `any`, masking child/prop drift at the content-rendering boundary.
- **Impact/fix:** transforms use `ReactNode` plus narrowed React elements and
  the library `Components` contract. Runtime rendering is unchanged and broad
  any-valued child/renderer signatures are excluded by the verifier.
- **Regression/validation:** exact TypeScript, scoped lint and the MyCodex
  aggregate pass.

MyCodex remains static/private: no Firestore rule/index, Storage rule, Firebase
Function, billing persistence or deployment behavior changed.

## Restart 1278 addendum — Answerlattice embedded widget client

Restart 1278 completed a clean line-by-line review of all 2,014 pre-edit lines
of `src/app/widget/[apiKey]/WidgetClient.tsx` and the legacy dynamic-key page,
then reversed response, context, visitor, image, feedback, escalation,
guidance and credential transitions through their route and renderer
consumers. Five defects were confirmed and closed;
`consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains `0`.

### AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-WIDGET-KEY-STATE-REMOUNT-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P0 / closed locally /
  `src/app/widget/[apiKey]/page.tsx` and `WidgetClient.tsx`; legacy dynamic
  credential route → retained React state → tenant-scoped rendered answers,
  context, visitor and runtime tokens.
- **Affected structures/producer/consumer/trigger:** the route `apiKey` plus
  browser messages, product/visitor context and rendered conversation produced
  under that key. A client-side dynamic-parameter transition from key A to key
  B without destroying the client component triggered the defect.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** the page passed the key only as a prop, so
  React could preserve the component identity and tenant A state while the
  credential prop became tenant B. Server requests would reject a mismatched
  runtime token, but already-rendered answers and context could remain visible
  beneath the new tenant identity. Credential identity must own the complete
  browser state lifetime.
- **Security/tenant/data/public/cache impact:** cross-tenant rendered public
  truth was possible within a reused legacy route component. No Firestore
  read/write or shared cache crossed scope. The page now keys the client by the
  exact credential so any key transition destroys all old state before the new
  client mounts. The maintained key-free embed remains single-key and
  compatible.
- **Regression/validation/closure:** the widget answer-contract gate requires
  credential-keyed remount. Answer/escalation, guidance, config and runtime-
  truth gates, exact TypeScript, scoped ESLint and diff integrity pass. P0
  resets the full clean counter.

### AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-WIDGET-MUTATION-SINGLE-FLIGHT-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / closed locally / solved/unresolved and
  support-form UI events → feedback/escalation POSTs → durable history/ticket
  mutation.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** React loading/optimistic state was the only
  duplicate guard. Repeated events before rerender could issue parallel
  feedback or support requests. Server idempotency protects durable identity,
  but the browser must not create redundant mutation/provider work.
- **Impact/fix:** immediate ref-backed per-message feedback and global
  escalation locks now claim admission before each POST and release in
  `finally`. Existing retry and server idempotency contracts remain intact.
- **Regression/validation:** the answer-contract gate requires both synchronous
  locks and pre-fetch admission checks.

### AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-WIDGET-MUTATION-GENERATION-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / closed locally / in-flight feedback or
  escalation → clear/new-chat/unmount → late browser completion.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** late success or failure could update error,
  escalation or message state after the conversation that initiated it had
  been cleared. Async mutation state lacked conversation ownership.
- **Impact/fix:** clear and unmount advance a conversation generation. Every
  feedback/escalation completion must still match its captured generation
  before touching UI state.
- **Regression/validation:** the answer-contract gate requires generation
  capture and stale-completion rejection; focused and type/lint gates pass.

### AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-WIDGET-IMAGE-READ-RACE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / closed locally / file or clipboard image
  selection → asynchronous `FileReader` → preview/search request.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** readers were neither cancelled nor
  sequenced. An older large screenshot could finish after a newer selection or
  after removal/clear and silently become the image later sent to support.
- **Security/data impact/fix:** this was a same-user unintended-image
  disclosure and request-integrity risk. A generation plus retained reader now
  aborts/rejects obsolete completions across replacement, removal, clear and
  unmount. Starting a new selection also clears the prior preview.
- **Regression/validation:** the answer-contract gate locks reader abort and
  generation checks; image policy and server validation are unchanged.

### AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-WIDGET-BROAD-CONTEXT-TYPE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P3 / closed locally / parent messages →
  sanitized context/visitor/request bodies → widget route.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** multiple `Record<string, any>` contracts
  hid the exact admitted shape and permitted a dead `displayName` reader even
  though sanitization projects that value to `name`. This allowed compile-time
  drift at a public runtime boundary.
- **Impact/fix:** exact product-context, visitor, evidence-link, conversation
  and request-body types now match runtime projection. The impossible reader
  was removed and unknown parent-message entries are narrowed explicitly.
- **Regression/validation:** the answer-contract gate excludes broad
  any-valued records. Exact TypeScript confirms all producers/consumers agree.

No Firestore rule/index, Storage rule or Firebase Function source changed, so
no infrastructure deployment applies.

### AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-WIDGET-INVALID-INIT-POISON-001

## Restart 1276 addendum — Answerlattice onboarding browser acknowledgement

Restart 1276 applied the SecurityOS Answerlattice routing contract, validated
the registry/plan without treating mapped evidence as executed proof, and
completed a line-by-line review of all 801 lines of the public get-started
`OnboardingForm.tsx`. The client response, current plan configuration,
Razorpay checkout contract, provisioning behavior test and route success
producers were traced in both directions. Three defects were confirmed and
closed; `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains `0`.

### AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-ONBOARD-BILLING-ACK-PROJECTION-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / closed locally /
  `src/lib/answerlattice/onboardingResponse.ts` and
  `src/app/sites/answerlattice/get-started/OnboardingForm.tsx`; authenticated
  onboarding route response → browser paid-plan/widget-key success truth →
  checkout/dashboard consumer.
- **Affected structures/producer/consumer/trigger:** route-owned
  `workspaceCreated` response, current monthly Answerlattice plan registry,
  Razorpay subscription/checkout acknowledgement and one-time widget key.
  Any internally drifted, malformed, proxy-corrupted or unexpectedly shaped
  success response triggered the defect.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** the former predicate required only a
  positive finite amount, a known plan ID, non-empty strings and a checkout URL
  that passed host validation. It then retained the unprojected object. A wrong
  but positive amount, drifted plan name, arbitrary non-empty widget key or
  loosely shaped subscription identity could therefore be presented as paid
  workspace truth. Billing and credential acknowledgements must agree exactly
  with current canonical configuration before display.
- **Security/tenant/billing/data/public/cache impact:** no cross-tenant read or
  write was found and server-side provider/persistence authority is unchanged.
  The impact was incorrect financial/credential truth after a successful
  same-origin response. The new projector requires the exact current monthly
  plan/name and smallest-unit amount, exact `al_*` key or explicit rotation
  state, bounded provider subscription identity/status, and canonical
  exact-host checkout URL. It returns only those projected fields. Valid
  current and payment-pending recovery responses remain compatible.
- **Regression/validation/closure:** the provisioning behavior test accepts
  canonical new/recovered responses, canonicalizes the safe checkout URL, and
  rejects price drift, malformed keys and lookalike checkout hosts. The
  Answerlattice runtime-truth source gate locks each boundary. Focused test,
  exact TypeScript, scoped ESLint and diff integrity pass.

### AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-ONBOARD-CLIENT-SINGLE-FLIGHT-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / closed locally /
  `OnboardingForm.tsx` (`handleCreateAccount`); owner submit → provider-backed
  onboarding POST → provisional scope/provider subscription/finalization.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** the form disappeared only after React
  committed `step = creating`; rapid submit events before rerender could issue
  parallel provider-backed setup requests. Server request fingerprinting and
  recovery reduce durable duplication, but the browser must reject a duplicate
  before invoking an expensive billing workflow.
- **Impact/fix:** an immediate ref-backed lock now gates before the POST and is
  released through one `finally`. No route, transaction, provider, plan, or
  idempotency architecture changed.
- **Regression/validation:** the source gate requires lock creation, admission
  and cleanup; the onboarding behavior and runtime-truth gates pass.

### AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-ONBOARD-POSTCOMMIT-SESSION-REFRESH-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / closed locally /
  `OnboardingForm.tsx`; durable successful workspace/provider acknowledgement
  → NextAuth refresh → owner success screen.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** the client awaited `update()` without a
  timeout inside the same `try` that classified creation. A rejected or hung
  session refresh after route success either displayed a false creation
  failure or left the owner indefinitely on “Setting up,” encouraging retries
  of a provider-backed operation. Session refresh is secondary and cannot
  reinterpret durable success.
- **Impact/fix:** new and existing-account refreshes race a cleanup-owned
  3-second timeout. Failure is bounded/logged; a validated durable success
  still advances to the one-time key/payment screen. Provider and Firestore
  truth are not retried or rolled back.
- **Regression/validation:** the source gate requires the bound, diagnostic and
  timer cleanup. Focused behavior, runtime-truth, exact TypeScript, scoped
  ESLint and diff integrity pass.

No Firestore rule/index, Storage rule or Firebase Function source changed, so
no infrastructure deployment applies.

## Restart 1275 addendum — public create-menu preview response and request lifecycle

Restart 1275 completed a line-by-line review of all 1,104 lines of
`src/app/(website)/create-menu/PreviewClient.tsx`, then reversed its poll and
claim inputs through the authenticated route, canonical public-draft contract,
extracted-business-profile contract, session handoff and success consumer.
Four defects were confirmed and closed; `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains
`0`.

### AUDIT-PUBLIC-CREATE-MENU-PREVIEW-RESPONSE-PROJECTION-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / closed locally /
  `PreviewClient.tsx` and
  `src/lib/publicCreateMenu/previewDraftResponse.ts`; authenticated poll JSON →
  browser React state → public extracted-menu/profile preview and claim
  defaults.
- **Affected structure/producer/consumer/trigger:** `publicMenuDrafts`
  status/full response, canonical `PublicMenuDraftExtractedData` and
  `ExtractedBusinessProfile`, produced normally by the owner-bound poll route
  and consumed by category/item renderers and claim defaults. Malformed,
  legacy, proxy-corrupted, or unexpectedly shaped successful JSON triggered
  the defect.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** the client checked only the top-level
  `status`, cast the remaining object to `DraftData`, spread it into state and
  later invoked array/map operations and used returned colors. A completed
  response with object-shaped `categories`, invalid localized structures or an
  incoherent full DTO could crash the preview or display unvalidated truth.
  Browser state must be an exact runtime projection, and completed truth must
  contain a coherent normalized menu.
- **Security/tenant/data/public/cache/compatibility impact:** the route remains
  owner-bound and no cross-tenant read was found, but the failure could make
  incorrect public-review truth or a broken claim funnel. The new browser
  projector reuses the authoritative public-draft/profile normalizers, bounds
  scalar fields, admits only normalized colors and fails unknown statuses or a
  completed incoherent menu closed. Valid current and normalized legacy
  responses remain compatible. No persistence/cache contract changed.

  normalization, rejects malformed nested containers and unsafe colors, and
  rejects unknown status. The maintained source gate requires the projector
  and forbids the former `any` profile. Public Menu Entry, full extraction
  pipeline, data-flow regression, exact TypeScript, scoped ESLint and diff
  integrity gates pass.

### AUDIT-PUBLIC-CREATE-MENU-PREVIEW-POLL-LIFECYCLE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / closed locally /
  `PreviewClient.tsx` (`fetchDraft` and poll effect); draft/session/retry cycle
  → status/full fetch → React state.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** effect cleanup stopped future timers but did
  not cancel an already running request. A response from an obsolete draft,
  session, or retry cycle could still set loading/draft state after cleanup.
  Each poll lifecycle must own and abort its network work before it loses
  authority.
- **Impact/fix:** no server mutation or additional datastore contract changed.
  One effect-owned `AbortController` now reaches both status and completion
  fetches; cleanup aborts it, and aborted work cannot navigate, report a false
  connection failure or mutate current state.
- **Regression/validation:** the source gate locks controller creation, signal
  propagation, abort cleanup and current attempt ordering. Exact TypeScript,
  scoped ESLint and the Public Menu Entry gates pass.

### AUDIT-PUBLIC-CREATE-MENU-PREVIEW-CLAIM-SINGLE-FLIGHT-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / closed locally /
  `PreviewClient.tsx` (`handleClaim`); owner click → claim POST → idempotent
  project/store transaction → session handoff.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** the disabled button depended only on an
  asynchronous React state update. Two rapid events before rerender could
  start parallel claim requests. The server receipt remains durable
  idempotency authority, but the browser must not knowingly duplicate an
  expensive publish attempt.
- **Impact/fix:** an immediate ref-backed lock now gates the action before
  validation/fetch and is released in one `finally`. Server authorization,
  transaction and receipt behavior are unchanged.
- **Regression/validation:** the source gate requires the pre-request
  single-flight boundary; Public Menu Entry and extraction pipeline gates
  pass.

### AUDIT-PUBLIC-CREATE-MENU-PREVIEW-REFRESH-TIMER-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P3 / closed locally /
  `PreviewClient.tsx` (`handleClaim`); committed claim acknowledgement →
  bounded NextAuth refresh race → success navigation.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** the 3-second timeout used in
  `Promise.race` was not retained or cleared when session refresh settled
  early. Repeated claims/tests left unnecessary queued callbacks beyond their
  owning operation.
- **Impact/fix:** the timeout is now retained and cleared in `finally` without
  changing the non-blocking handoff or committed claim truth.
- **Regression/validation:** source gate, exact TypeScript, scoped ESLint and

No Firestore rule/index, Storage rule or Firebase Function source changed, so

## Restart 1273 addendum — public Highlights display lifecycle integrity

Restart 1273 completed line-by-line reviews of both
`src/app/screen/[token]/ScreenDisplay.tsx` and
`src/app/screen/[token]/MenuBoardDisplay.tsx`, then reverse-traced their
timers, browser storage, server-prop reconciliation, public screen mirror
listeners and zero-blank rendering contracts through the shared screen
content/reload utilities. Eight defects were confirmed and closed. They reset
`consecutiveCleanFullPasses` to `0`.

### AUDIT-DIGITAL-SCREEN-EMPTY-ROTATION-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P1 / closed locally /
  `src/app/screen/[token]/ScreenDisplay.tsx::advanceSlide`; public Screen
  Highlights state → slide interval → selected public slide.
- **Affected structure/producer/consumer/trigger:** `ScreenState.currentIndex`;
  the server/listener supplies `slides`, the interval produces the next index,
  and the Highlights renderer consumes it. An interval callback already queued
  when the slide list becomes empty was the trigger.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** the callback evaluated
  `(currentIndex + 1) % slides.length`; modulo zero produces `NaN`. When slides
  later returned, a non-empty list indexed by `NaN` bypassed the empty fallback
  while rendering no slide. Rotation must keep a valid bounded integer for
  every list transition.
- **Security/data/public/cache/compatibility impact:** no tenant authority,
  persisted document or cache key changed. A timing race could leave a public
  TV blank until reload, violating public truth availability. Normal rotation
  order is unchanged.
- **Fix/files/test/validation/closure:** empty lists reset the index to zero and
  non-empty rotation first normalizes the prior index. The Digital Screens
  verifier requires both guards. Focused Digital Screens, public-truth, exact
  TypeScript, scoped ESLint and diff-integrity validation close the finding in
  restart 1273.

### AUDIT-DIGITAL-SCREEN-FULLSCREEN-HINT-TIMER-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P3 / closed locally /
  `src/app/screen/[token]/ScreenDisplay.tsx` fullscreen-change effect; browser
  fullscreen state → recovery hint timer → public display overlay.
- **Affected structure/producer/consumer/trigger:** the browser event produced
  untracked ten-second timers and React consumed their delayed state writes.
  Repeated exit/entry events or unmount before settlement triggered stale
  callbacks.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** every fullscreen exit created a timer that
  was neither cleared on a later event nor on effect cleanup. An older callback
  could hide a newer hint and callbacks survived unmount. Exactly one owned
  timer must exist and be cleared on replacement, click and cleanup.
- **Security/data/public/cache/compatibility impact:** no security, persistence
  or cache impact. The defect caused stale public-display UI state and an
  avoidable post-unmount callback. Current recovery copy and ten-second
  duration remain unchanged.
- **Fix/files/test/validation/closure:** a timer ref now owns the timeout; all
  event, click and cleanup paths clear it. The source verifier locks ownership
  and cleanup, with the same validation set closing the finding in restart
  1273.

### AUDIT-DIGITAL-SCREEN-SEEN-STORAGE-READ-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P2 / closed locally /
  `src/app/screen/[token]/ScreenDisplay.tsx` daily-seen effect; TV browser
  storage → daily admission → `/api/screen/seen` operational signal.
- **Affected structure/producer/consumer/trigger:** the browser produces the
  `screen_seen_*` marker and the client effect consumes it before the bounded
  seen endpoint. Browsers that disable or throw on local storage triggered the
  failure.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** `localStorage.getItem()` was outside the
  existing failure boundary, so a `SecurityError` escaped the effect and could
  disrupt the public screen. The optional operational signal must never take
  display truth down.
- **Security/data/public/cache/compatibility impact:** no tenant identifier or
  endpoint authorization changed. Storage denial now emits only the existing
  bounded token/store context and permits a best-effort request; it may repeat
  on a later mount when the browser cannot retain the marker, but never marks a
  failed endpoint call as successful.
- **Fix/files/test/validation/closure:** the storage read is contained and logs
  `digital_screen_display_seen_storage_read_failed`; the response/storage-write
  promise retains its existing rejection diagnostic. The verifier locks the
  bounded failure code, and focused/broader validation closes the finding in
  restart 1273.

### AUDIT-DIGITAL-SCREEN-OFFLINE-CACHE-PROJECTION-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / closed locally /
  `screenContent.ts`, `ScreenDisplay.tsx` and `MenuBoardDisplay.tsx`; mutable
  token-scoped local storage → offline cache admission → public TV output.
- **Affected structures/producers/consumers/trigger:** JSON browser values
  claimed `ScreenSlide[]` or `MenuItemForSlide[]`; both display clients
  consumed them after checking only a version and array-like `length`.
  Malformed same-origin state or a cached owner poster past its truth deadline
  triggered the path.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** an object with `length` could pass cache
  admission and crash/blank array consumers, individual fields bypassed the
  public projectors, and an expired cached owner slide remained visible
  indefinitely while offline. Highlights also immediately replaced a valid
  offline cache during its first reconciliation effect whenever it differed
  from server fallback props. Browser persistence is input, not a TypeScript
  contract, and first-mount fallback must remain distinct from a later
  server-prop refresh.
- **Security/data/public/cache/compatibility impact:** token keys remain
  isolated and no persisted Firebase truth changes. The impact was malformed
  or withdrawn public content, including a stale offer. Current safe
  same-version cached entries retain their order/content after bounded
  normalization; expired or malformed entries fail closed.
- **Fix/files/test/validation/closure:** shared cache projectors snapshot real
  arrays without invoking accessors, bound all fields, rebuild future
  timestamps and omit expired slides. Both clients admit the normalized count
  only; Highlights skips reconciliation on the initial mount but applies later
  server truth. Lifecycle tests cover array-like data, incomplete items and
  expired/future posters; source gates lock both client calls.

### AUDIT-DIGITAL-SCREEN-RELOAD-ACKNOWLEDGEMENT-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / closed locally /
  `src/lib/screen/utils.ts` and both display listeners; public mirror revision
  → jittered guarded reload → fresh server-rendered public truth.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** jitter timers were unowned and every
  version event could create another. More importantly, the listener advanced
  its local version acknowledgement before the timer ran; if the 30-second
  reload guard suppressed that attempt, no later snapshot or timer retried, so
  the TV could retain stale public truth indefinitely.
- **Security/data/public/cache/compatibility impact:** reload guard keys remain
  token-specific and no datastore/cache contract changes. The defect could
  delay publication/unpublication and leave timers targeting a component that
  had unmounted. Jitter remains 0–60 seconds for fleet smoothing.
- **Fix/files/test/validation/closure:** guarded reload reports suppression;
  one cancellable scheduler retains a retry after the guard window, and each
  listener owns at most one scheduled content reload and cancels it on
  cleanup. A fake-clock/timer regression proves suppression followed by one
  successful retry.

### AUDIT-DIGITAL-SCREEN-PUBLIC-MIRROR-MISSING-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / closed locally /
  `ScreenDisplay.tsx` and `MenuBoardDisplay.tsx`; token-free
  `platformSummary/screen_{storeId}` snapshot → enable/revision admission →
  public display lifecycle.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** a non-existent listener snapshot performed
  no action. Mirror removal or partial cleanup could therefore leave the
  already rendered screen visible indefinitely. Missing or disabled
  authoritative state must force the public route to re-resolve.
- **Security/data/public/cache/compatibility impact:** no anonymous read scope
  or tenant identity changes. Missing/disabled truth now schedules an immediate
  guarded reload and retains retry if another recent reload owns the guard;
  valid enabled snapshots are unchanged.
- **Fix/test/validation/closure:** both listeners explicitly handle
  `!snapshot.exists()`, use the cleanup-owned immediate scheduler, and the
  Digital Screens source gate requires the fail-closed branch.

### AUDIT-MENUBOARD-SERVER-TRUTH-PAGINATION-RACE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / closed locally /
  `MenuBoardDisplay.tsx`; Next server props/menu projection → local display
  state → category pagination → public menu.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** React state was initialized once and never
  reconciled when a client-side route refresh preserved the component with new
  menu/version props. Separately, a queued callback from an old pagination
  interval closed over the old page count and could select a now-nonexistent
  page after the clamp effect, leaving an empty board. Current server truth and
  current page bounds must be authoritative.
- **Security/data/public/cache/compatibility impact:** no tenant or persistence
  change. The defects could show stale or blank public menu truth. Initial
  offline cache admission remains preserved, while later server revisions
  reset to page zero.
- **Fix/test/validation/closure:** an initial-truth ref distinguishes mount
  from later props, updates the content-version ref/items/page atomically, and
  queued pagination callbacks read the current total-page ref. The verifier
  locks both lifecycle guards.

### AUDIT-MENUBOARD-BROWSER-EFFECT-LIFECYCLE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / closed locally /
  `MenuBoardDisplay.tsx`; browser seen marker/fullscreen/token changes → public
  Menu Board effects.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** the Menu Board repeated the uncontained
  seen-marker read and untracked fullscreen timer found in Highlights, while
  listener/fallback/proactive reload effects could retain an old token across

## Restart 1272 addendum — shared runtime utility data-contract repair

Restart 1272 completed a line-by-line review of `src/utils/utils.ts` and traced
every live export to its callers. Seven defects were confirmed and closed.
They reset `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` to `0`.

### AUDIT-SHARED-DEEP-CLONE-CONTRACT-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P2 / closed locally /
  `src/utils/utils.ts::removeObjRef`; loaded project/store/user/menu structures
  → owner editor clone → local mutation/persistence DTO.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** the recursive `{}` assignment admitted
  `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype`, converted `Date` instances to
  empty objects, shallow-copied sets and recursed forever on cycles. A shared
  clone must preserve supported value semantics and cannot allow input keys to
  control the clone prototype.
- **Impact/compatibility:** no confirmed cross-tenant read; hostile or legacy
  shapes could change inherited values, lose timestamps, crash an editor or
  corrupt a later write. Firestore `Timestamp` identity remains preserved and
  normal object/array callers keep their existing returned shape.
- **Fix/test:** one cycle-aware clone projector skips unsafe keys, clones Date,
  set, array and object values, and retains the generic caller contract.
  `test-small-runtime-contracts.ts` covers prototype-key rejection, deep
  independence and Date preservation.

### AUDIT-DEEP-PATH-PROTOTYPE-POLLUTION-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P2 / closed locally /
  `src/utils/utils.ts::updateDeepPathValue`; owner form field key → nested user
  draft mutation.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** `__proto__.x` traversed the inherited
  prototype object and wrote into it. Empty path segments and arrays were also
  accepted as containers. Path segments must be explicit safe own-data keys.
- **Impact/compatibility:** current first-party callers use fixed field names,
  so no exploited path was confirmed; the exported helper nevertheless
  provided a concrete prototype-mutation path if a dynamic form key reached
  it. Valid existing paths retain in-place update behavior.
- **Fix/test:** empty and prototype-control segments now throw before mutation;
  nested containers are created with reflection over safe segments. Regression
  coverage proves normal nesting and hostile-path rejection.

### AUDIT-MEDIA-FILEREADER-SETTLEMENT-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P2 / closed locally /
  `blobToBase64` and `getCompressedImage`; owner-selected image → compressor →
  FileReader → preview/upload DTO.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** `blobToBase64` had no error handler, and an
  exception in the compressor success callback could leave the outer promise
  pending forever. Every media preparation attempt must settle.
- **Impact/compatibility:** an unreadable compressed blob could leave owner
  loading state indefinitely; no partial write occurs before this conversion.
- **Fix/test:** FileReader errors and non-string results reject; compression
  catches that rejection, emits the existing bounded
  `image_compression_failed` diagnostic and resolves `null`. A mocked reader
  regression proves rejection settlement.

### AUDIT-DATA-URL-SIZE-METADATA-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P2 / closed locally /
  `getBase64Length`; image/font/SVG data URL → asset size metadata and owner
  display.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** byte size subtracted a hard-coded PNG
  prefix and used an approximation for JPEG, GIF, WebP, font and text data
  URLs. Invalid/null compression output also threw. Metadata must reflect the
  actual payload independently of MIME.
- **Impact/compatibility:** stored/displayed asset sizes could be wrong and a
  failed compression could turn into a secondary exception. Persisted legacy
  size values need no migration because they are informational.
- **Fix/test:** exact base64 padding math, encoded-text byte measurement and
  malformed/null fail-closed handling now cover all current callers.

### AUDIT-UTILITY-INDEX-KEY-IGNORED-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P3 / closed locally /
  `getNewIndex`; knowledge-base list and requested ordering key → next index.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** sorting used the requested key but the
  return always read `lastItem.index`; non-default callers produced `NaN` or
  the wrong value. The key contract must be consistent end to end.
- **Fix/test:** the helper computes the maximum finite numeric value for the
  requested key and returns zero for empty/malformed sets; default callers are
  unchanged and custom-key coverage is present.

### AUDIT-THEME-MEDIA-QUERY-TRUTHINESS-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P3 / closed locally /
  `initialThemeHandler`; first browser visit → system theme preference → local
  theme persistence.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** the MediaQueryList object itself is always
  truthy, so a first-time light-mode user was stored as dark. The decision must
  read `.matches`.
- **Fix/test:** `.matches` now controls the initial value; a browser-global
  fixture proves a nonmatching query stores and returns light.

### AUDIT-JSON-RESPONSE-PROMISE-SETTLEMENT-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P3 / closed locally /
  `parseJSON`; fetch response → status/body projection.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** a manually nested promise did not forward
  `response.text()` or `JSON.parse()` rejection, and an empty body returned the
  string `"{}"` instead of an object. The exported response projector must
  settle with one consistent shape.
- **Fix/test:** the helper is an async function that naturally forwards read
  and parse failures and projects an empty body as `{}`; both cases have
  focused assertions.

### AUDIT-SPECIAL-MENU-TRANSLATION-PARTIAL-METADATA-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / closed locally / desktop Editor,
  Command Center, Projects, mobile project selector, special-menu screen,
  language manager and bulk actions; translated special-menu display name →
  project mutation → canonical project and summary persistence.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** every surface spread
  `(_specialMenu || {})` and added only `displayName`. When legacy or malformed
  input lacked `_specialMenu`, the code manufactured a partial object without
  required `baseProjectId`, mode, schedule or lifecycle status. Translation
  may update an existing special menu but must not invent its authority.
- **Security/data/public/cache/compatibility:** no tenant bypass. A partial
  object could corrupt special-menu activation/public truth and later
  scheduler assumptions. Existing complete metadata remains unchanged; legacy
  missing metadata is not silently synthesized and needs no migration.
- **Fix/test:** all eight mutation branches now require current complete
  `_specialMenu` truth before replacing its display name. The public-business-
  truth source gate asserts each desktop/mobile branch.

### AUDIT-EXTRACTED-LANGUAGE-PRIMARY-STATE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / closed locally /
  `Editor.tsx` translation loop; owner-added target language → extracted file
  language registry → translation/persistence.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** a newly appended language contained only
  code/name even though `ExtractedDataLanguage.isPrimary` is required. This
  produced a runtime shape that disagreed with every typed consumer.
- **Impact/fix/test:** no tenant impact; downstream primary-language selection
  could treat the entry inconsistently. New target entries now explicitly use

### AUDIT-NULLABLE-EDITOR-DRAFT-FALLBACK-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P2 / closed locally / role-details and
  tenant-details platform editors; drawer lifecycle → late field event → typed
  draft state.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** both handlers cloned nullable state and
  replaced a null result with `{}`, then assigned arbitrary fields as though
  the object were a complete `StoreRoleDataType` or `TenantDataType`. A field
  event after close could recreate an invalid draft, while the tenant add flow
  depended on that same accidental empty-object behavior instead of defining
  its required initial fields.
- **Impact/fix/test:** platform-only local-state integrity; no write occurs
  without later form submission, but required identity and authority fields
  could be absent. State is now accurately nullable, tenant creation starts
  from an explicit complete minimum draft, submit is null-guarded, and late
  events fail closed. Exact TypeScript proves every live caller respects the
  clone result.

  directly and keys POS registration from that same current value. The

### AUDIT-AL-RETENTION-ZERO-AND-INVALID-FROM-001 — Epoch zero silently became the current time

- **Finding/severity/status:** `AUDIT-AL-RETENTION-ZERO-AND-INVALID-FROM-001` / P2 / Closed locally in restart 1050.
- **Files/flow:** app and Answerlattice Functions `dataRetention.ts::toMillis`; explicit source timestamp → retention expiry/TTL field → cleanup scheduler.

- **Fix/compatibility/regression:** only nullish input defaults to now; all explicit values must project to a safe integer millisecond value. ### AUDIT-AUTH-SANITIZER-INHERITED-PROPERTIES-001 — Inherited fields entered sanitized auth records

- **Finding/severity/status:** `AUDIT-AUTH-SANITIZER-INHERITED-PROPERTIES-001` / P2 / Closed locally in restart 1051.
- **File/flow:** `src/lib/security/sanitizeObject.ts`; Firestore/auth user object → sanitized server user/session and phone/user DAL records.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** both sanitizers used `for...in`, which copies enumerable inherited fields. `removeKeys` also depended on every caller remembering the prototype-pollution key list. A non-plain or polluted input could therefore inject inherited identity, product or role-like fields into the sanitized record, and a throwing Proxy/accessor could abort authentication recovery.
- **Fix/regression:** one typed projector now enumerates own keys only, always removes the three dangerous keys, contains enumeration/property failures and defines copied values as ordinary own data properties. - **Finding/severity/status:** `AUDIT-LOCALIZATION-RUNTIME-CONTRACT-001` / P2 / Closed locally in restart 1051.

- **Observed/root cause/impact:** type guards admitted null text values and arbitrary array contents while claiming `Record<string,string>` and `Record<string,string[]>`. `Object.values`/indexed reads and `String(item)` could execute access or coercion hooks from corrupt persisted/local data, aborting public or owner rendering. The special-note resolver also traversed its unknown nested inputs directly.
- **Fix/compatibility/regression:** localization reads snapshot own entries with exception containment, validate every non-null legacy entry, accept only string list members, and operate from the safe snapshot. Strict exported type guards now match their declared types, while read/conversion helpers retain the established compatibility behavior of ignoring null legacy language slots. Special-note paths use safe nested reads. Tests cover valid/legacy values, false type-guard cases, throwing enumeration and coercion, and the store-note fallback; the complete global/public localization matrix passes.

## Restart 1128 addendum — public hours timezone parity trace

Restart 1128 changed direction to the canonical weekly-hours evaluator and
traced missing, malformed and valid store timezone metadata through owner
status, public menu, Official Business Page, Output Control, trust signals and
structured-data consumers. One P1 public-truth defect was confirmed and closed;
`consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains zero.

### AUDIT-PUBLIC-HOURS-TIMEZONE-FALLBACK-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/hours/hoursEngine.ts`, `src/lib/hours/hoursDiagnostics.ts`,
  `src/lib/obp/hoursStatus.ts` and the OBP today-hours path; persisted optional
  store timezone and weekly hours → store-local day/minute resolution → open,
  closed and next-change projections → owner/public consumers.
- **Observed behavior:** the shared localization contract defines `UTC` as its
  deterministic SSR fallback. The hours engine and most public consumers used
  that value when timezone metadata was missing, but both OBP status paths
  independently substituted `Asia/Kolkata`. A legacy store without timezone
  truth could therefore be open on the menu and closed on the OBP, or the
  reverse, near differing day/time boundaries. If an explicitly malformed
  timezone reached the engine, its catch branches used the server or browser
  local clock, so identical persisted truth could change by runtime host.
- **Expected/root cause/impact:** every consumer of the same store-hours truth
  must use the same deterministic timezone policy. Region-specific fallbacks
  had survived in the OBP adapters after the shared localization/runtime
  fallback became `UTC`, and error recovery had retained environment-local
  clock calls. This did not bypass tenant authorization or mutate persisted
  data, but it could publish contradictory current-business truth.
- **Fix/legacy/cache/Firebase:** engine resolution now imports the canonical
  localization fallback for both normal and error paths. Invalid-zone failures
  remain bounded and observable but retry against `UTC`, never the runtime
  local clock. Both OBP paths delegate the optional timezone unchanged to that
  engine. Existing valid store timezones remain authoritative; missing/invalid
  legacy values converge deterministically without a migration. No read,
  write, cache key/invalidation, persisted shape, rule/index, Storage or
  Function change applies.
- **Regression/validation:** the behavior suite uses an instant where UTC and
  India are on different weekdays and proves missing and malformed timezone
  parity through both `getStoreStatus()` and `getStoreOpenStatus()`. The

### AUDIT-AL-GOVERNANCE-IDENTITY-NORMALIZATION-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/answerlattice/governanceContracts.ts`; authenticated governance
  JSON or stored proposal → Zod decoding → document mutation/idempotency,
  evidence association and canonical output.
- **Observed/root cause:** identifier schemas called `trim()` before comparing
  against the shared normalizer. A request such as `" proposal_123 "` was
  therefore transformed into `proposal_123` and could act on that existing
  proposal; request IDs similarly aliased another idempotency key. Evidence

  transformation. Exact current IDs are unchanged. Malformed legacy stored
  identity fields fail closed with the established bounded invalid-document
  response rather than targeting a normalized neighbor.

  idempotency and evidence IDs while retaining valid merge, approval and
  stored-proposal behavior.

### AUDIT-AL-GOVERNANCE-CANONICAL-INVARIANTS-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/answerlattice/governanceContracts.ts`; owner canonical editor or
  direct governance request → proposal → approval → canonical answer scope,
  version truth and retrieval applicability.

  admitted duplicate entity/plan/role/state scope identifiers and

  some version/entity cases only after route validation, but duplicate
  optional applicability dimensions could persist into canonical truth.
  Separately, the handwritten TypeScript proposal contract represented a

  binding enforces `lastValidatedInVersion >= introducedInVersion` and

  server's independent candidate checks remain as defense in depth.
- **Regression:** focused tests pin duplicate optional scope rejection and
  both invalid version relationships; guided-procedure contracts retain valid
  structured procedure behavior.

## Restart 1121 addendum — linked-outlet resolver structure trace

Restart 1121 selected the unreviewed 553-line linked-outlet renderer and traced
master cache population/fetch, project-ID scope, master/outlet structure,

Pull API serialization and owner/public consumers. One P1 public-truth defect

### AUDIT-MULTI-OUTLET-RESOLVER-STRUCTURE-AUTHORITY-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/multiOutlet/resolveProject.ts`, the public Pull API behavior suite
  and multi-outlet implementation contract; cached/fetched master plus stored
  outlet project → overrides/local entity merge → resolved project → public
  menu/Pull API/owner editor.
- **Observed/root cause/security/data impact:** cache population did not prove
  that the supplied project matched its master-project key. The renderer
  documented single-file inheritance but accepted multi-file master/outlet
  projects, flattened all entities into file 1 and then preserved later outlet
  files, duplicating local entities. It accepted a linked project as another
  master, duplicate/unsafe IDs, malformed override maps and any store-only ID
  as local despite the governed `L_I_`/`L_C_` namespaces. Corrupt or legacy
  state could therefore manufacture incorrect public item/category/image/price
  truth or cross-wire an externally populated cache entry. Current callers
  were scope-aware, so no observed cross-tenant disclosure was established.
- **Fix/compatibility:** cache population now accepts only an exact normalized
  key/project identity. Linked resolution requires the cached/fetched master
  to match that identity, have no upstream master and exactly one file; outlet
  storage may contain at most one file. Master/store item and category IDs
  must be unique, trimmed, slash-free and non-dangerous; every store-only
  entity must use its governed local prefix. Present override maps must be
  plain objects, while missing legacy maps remain compatible and normalize to
  empty maps. Invalid structure emits bounded diagnostics and returns
  unresolved rather than merging.
- **Regression/validation:** the public Pull behavior suite proves mismatched
  cache identity is rejected and linked-master, multi-file master, multi-file
  outlet and unprefixed-local cases fail unresolved. Its valid inherited item,
  price, variant, allergen, decision-fact and language projection remains
  intact. Multi-location, complete public-business-truth, exact TypeScript,
  focused lint and diff hygiene pass.

### AUDIT-IMAGE-BATCH-ITEM-IDENTITY-AMBIGUITY-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/ai/imageBatchProjectSelection.ts` and its focused regression suite;
  generated image result selected by item ID → transaction-current project or
  outlet/master project → persisted `item.images`/outlet override → public
  menu.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the batch protocol intentionally carries an
  item ID but no source file ID. The projector scanned every file and appended
  the same selected image to every matching item; its matched-ID set collapsed

  therefore publish a generated photo on multiple unrelated items.

  requires exactly one. Zero matches retain the existing missing-item failure;
  multiple standalone/local/master matches now fail with a stable ambiguous
  target error before the transaction writes. Normal globally unique item IDs,
  idempotent same-URL append, linked local precedence and inherited override
  behavior remain unchanged.

  inherited master duplicates fail closed. The image-batch selection suite,
  complete AI-accounting aggregate, multi-location source gate, exact
  TypeScript, focused ESLint and diff hygiene pass.

Restart 1118 restarted from the remaining mobile `item.images` writers and
traced edit/add input through local projection, linked-outlet override policy,

### AUDIT-MOBILE-ITEM-IMAGE-UPLOAD-TARGET-RACE-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/components/mobile/screens/MobileMenuScreen.tsx`,
  `src/lib/media/itemImageAssociationBoundary.ts` and the embedded-owner
  regression suite; owner data-URL photo → prepared Storage upload → delayed
  completion → exact project/file/item image truth → public menu.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** background completion re-read whichever
  project happened to be current, scanned every file by item ID alone and
  replaced every match. Navigation, duplicate item IDs or two overlapping
  edits could therefore attach an older photo to another project/file/item or
  overwrite newer image state. The input also used an unsafe cast. No tenant
  disclosure was observed, but the delayed write could corrupt owner and
  public menu truth.
- **Fix/compatibility:** each upload captures canonical project/file/item
  identity, exact prior-image snapshot and a per-target revision. Completion
  requires the same project, unique file/item, unchanged image state and
  current revision before immutable replacement. Superseded, navigated-away
  or otherwise stale uploads are rejected and their just-created Storage
  objects are deleted. The upload DTO is precisely typed. Existing non-data
  image and successful background behavior remains intact.
- **Regression/validation:** behavioral tests prove exact replacement does not
  cross a duplicate ID, source state remains immutable and a completion with
  stale prior-image state fails closed. Source contracts pin project/file/item
  correlation, revision fencing and stale-object cleanup. The 60-check owner
  capability suite, exact root TypeScript, focused ESLint and diff hygiene
  pass.

### AUDIT-MOBILE-LINKED-OUTLET-IMAGE-UPLOAD-OVERRIDE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/components/mobile/screens/MobileMenuScreen.tsx`; linked-outlet inherited
  item photo edit → outlet policy → Storage → resolved item and persisted
  `overrides.items` image truth.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the linked-outlet branch defined an image
  change as only a non-data URL. A data-URL selection therefore bypassed the
  `imageOverride` permission check, was excluded from the override projection,
  and returned before starting background upload. The UI could acknowledge
  the edit although the photo was never published; if later completion were
  introduced independently, the same branch would have bypassed policy.
- **Fix/compatibility:** any supplied image value now passes the image-override
  policy before mutation. Direct URLs/deletion retain synchronous projection;
  permitted data URLs start the same exact-target background upload before
  the branch returns, and successful completion flows through the existing
  linked-override persistence projection. Exact file identity also scopes the
  resolved display update.
- **Regression/validation:** source contracts pin policy admission for both

Restart 1116 restarted forward from the public-media owner entry point through
camera/device intake, browser preparation, item selection, immutable Storage

### AUDIT-ITEM-PHOTO-PREPARATION-SELECTION-RACE-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/components/templates/main-app/projects/editorView/ImageUploadModal.tsx`,
  `src/components/shared/media/ItemPhotoCaptureAssist.tsx`,

  `scripts/verification/verify-embedded-owner-capabilities.ts`; owner selects
  item → camera/device photo → asynchronous preparation → draft image list →
  final item save.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** preparation completion had no relationship to
  the item selection that started it. If item A preparation was slow and the
  owner selected item B, A's prepared photo entered B's draft. An item-ID-only
  check would also become true again after A → B → A. The capture component
  retained the prior item's preview/readiness state across those changes. A
  normal owner interaction could therefore publish the wrong photo as public
  menu truth.
- **Fix/regression/cache/backward compatibility:** every preparation captures
  an item-selection revision and is discarded unless both item and revision
  remain current. Item changes remount the camera component, stopping the old
  stream and clearing preview/feedback. Behavior tests prove unchanged,
  A → B and A → B → A settlement. No persisted schema or cache key changed;
  accepted saves retain the existing project/public-cache invalidation path.

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /

  the desktop/mobile editor target handoffs,

  suite; prepared browser image → exact editor target → Storage upload →
  project document item image metadata → public menu consumer.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** final association ignored
  `selectedItem.fileId` and updated the first item with a matching ID across all
  files. Direct/select UI also reduced identity to item ID, so duplicated or

  objects and appended browser `Blob` plus the full prepared-canvas payload to
  the Firestore-bound project shape; those values are transient and not valid
  project truth. The general path also lacked the shared 20-image ceiling.
  Outcomes included wrong-item public media, rejected project persistence
  after a successful immutable Storage upload and divergent batch/manual

  exact serialized file/item tuple; direct desktop/mobile edit handoffs carry

### AUDIT-BOOKING-RESPONSE-EXPECTATION-INFERENCE-001

  `src/lib/public-truth-tools/bookingInquiryReadinessReport.ts`; owner-entered
  action sentence and selections → booking/inquiry readiness rows → public
  report and setup handoff.

  accepted generic tokens outside the fact they claimed to prove.
  Response-expectation accepted bare `hours`, `today`, `tomorrow`, `available`
  and `slot`; confirmation accepted bare `slot`; fallback accepted a primary

  during our opening hours” therefore proved response and confirmation, while

  business reply/respond/callback/contact/confirm statement, a bounded
  response-time phrase, or an explicit availability-confirmation statement.

  an alternative/failure/help cue; location requires actual location,
  directions, service-area or locality phrasing. Separate owner checkboxes are
  unchanged, as are true statements such as “we reply within one hour.”

  text keeps hours present while response and confirmation remain unclear, and
  that a primary call does not prove fallback or location context. The focused
  booking verifier, exact TypeScript and scoped ESLint pass.

## Restart 1114 addendum — type-first Answerlattice proof contracts

Restart 1114 restarted type-first from remaining executable shared-runtime
contracts. It traced the Answer Tests case/result schemas through deterministic
evaluation, run construction, summary compaction/persistence, retained-run
normalization, Activation proof projection and owner display. One P2 producer
contract defect was confirmed and closed; `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains
zero.

### AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-ANSWER-TEST-RESULT-BOUNDS-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/answerlattice/answerTestEvaluation.ts`,
  `src/lib/answerlattice/answerTestContracts.ts`,
  `src/lib/answerlattice/answerTestServer.ts`,
  `scripts/verification/test-answerlattice-founder-support-controls.ts`,
  `scripts/verification/verify-answerlattice-runtime-truth.js` and Founder
  Support Controls implementation/test documentation; admitted test case +
  resolved answer + elapsed duration → deterministic evaluator → retained
  Answer Test run → compact Firestore summary → Activation/owner proof.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the evaluator appended one failure for every
  independent assertion without applying the authoritative result schema's
  limit. A valid case can produce 21 failures, and a missing-specific-reference
  message can exceed 240 characters. `Math.max(0, Math.floor(durationMs))`
  also preserves `NaN` and positive infinity. The exported producer therefore
  could return a value that its declared persisted result schema rejects; the
  write path compacts for byte size but does not re-parse a newly produced run.
  A later legacy normalizer would truncate the row, causing producer/reader
  evidence drift.
- **Fix/regression:** the evaluator now retains the first 20 deterministic
  failures, bounds each to 240 characters, and converts negative/non-finite
  duration to zero while capping finite duration to a safe integer. Pass/fail
  continues to derive from the complete raw failure set. A maximal valid case
  simultaneously fails source, critical authority, answer/FAQ identity,
  confidence, eight required phrases, eight forbidden phrases and specific
  citations; the regression proves the result remains failed, contains exactly
  20 bounded messages, normalizes infinite duration, and parses through
  `AnswerlatticeAnswerTestCaseResultSchema`.

### AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-PROPOSAL-IMPACT-RESPONSE-INVARIANTS-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/answerlattice/proposalImpactContracts.ts`,
  `src/app/api/answerlattice/answer-tests/proposal-impact/route.ts`,
  `src/lib/answerlattice/proposalImpactClient.ts`,
  `scripts/verification/test-answerlattice-founder-support-controls.ts`,
  `scripts/verification/verify-answerlattice-runtime-truth.js` and Founder
  Support Controls implementation/test documentation; selected linked cases →
  current/proposed evaluation pairs → derived counts/proof → strict API
  response → bounded browser parser → owner preview.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the shared response schema bounded individual
  fields but did not reconcile them. A structurally valid response could claim
  counts, truncation, evaluated totals or current/proposed proof statuses that
  contradicted its comparison rows. The route currently builds those fields
  correctly, but the browser treats schema success as server-response
  authority, so the runtime contract did not independently protect owner
  decision truth from producer drift.
- **Fix/regression:** schema refinement now derives comparison length, all four
  classification counts, truncation state and both proof statuses from the
  admitted rows, and rejects evaluated counts above linked counts. Tests prove
  the valid empty response remains accepted while contradictory count and
  truncation state fails closed. The source verifier pins the derived-field
  invariants.

### AUDIT-PRODUCTION-ENV-FAILFAST-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/env/validateEnv.ts`, `src/instrumentation.ts`,
  `scripts/verification/test-configuration-safety.ts` and
  `scripts/verification/verify-configuration-safety.js`; server
  instrumentation → environment contract evaluation → bounded diagnostic →
  production runtime admission.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** `runEnvValidation()` described its
  non-Vercel production branch as a hard error, but only logged and returned.
  A production Node server could therefore start with missing required
  Firebase, NextAuth, Admin or model configuration and fail later through
  partial auth/data/provider paths. Its Vercel detection also differed from the
  validator by ignoring `VERCEL_ENV`.
- **Fix/regression:** non-Vercel production now throws a generic error after
  the bounded diagnostic, without exposing missing names or values. Runtime and
  validation use the same `VERCEL`/`VERCEL_ENV` detection. The deliberate
  Vercel log-only static-build exception remains. Behavioral tests clear and
  restore the relevant process environment, prove both branches, and the
  source verifier pins the fail-fast statement. `npm run
  verify:configuration-safety`, focused ESLint and exact root TypeScript pass.

### AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-PUBLIC-RICH-TEXT-URL-ADMISSION-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/answerlattice/publicRichText.ts`,
  `scripts/verification/test-answerlattice-knowledge-map.ts`,
  `scripts/verification/verify-answerlattice-knowledge-map.js`,
  `scripts/verification/verify-answerlattice-runtime-truth.js` and the
  Knowledge Map implementation/test documentation; published TipTap JSON →
  fixed-tag server renderer → hosted-help HTML → browser navigation or image
  request.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the public renderer treated any value
  beginning with one slash as a same-site URL. Browser URL parsing normalizes
  `/\attacker.example/path` to an external origin, so published rich text could
  create an attacker-controlled navigation or image request. Absolute HTTP(S)
  URLs containing credentials were also retained. Prefix-only scheme checks
  did not model the browser's URL parser.
- **Fix/regression:** root-relative values are now parsed against a fixed
  non-routable same-site base and must retain that origin. Absolute values are
  parsed, allowlisted by protocol, and must contain no username or password;
  controls and backslashes fail closed. Links retain the intended HTTP(S),
  mail and telephone schemes, while images retain HTTP(S) only. Focused
  behavior tests prove valid internal/external values still render and
  backslash/credential variants are absent. The Knowledge Map and runtime
  source verifiers pin the parser, credential, and unsafe-character guards.

  same-site paths or credential-free HTTPS URLs; every other value rejects
  before script creation. Runtime-summary tests cover accepted production and
  relative values plus rejected protocol-relative, HTTP, data, JavaScript and
  credential-bearing cases. The package build, focused lint, behavioral test
  and Answerlattice runtime source verifier pass.

Restart 1111 began public-output-first with Answerlattice JSON-LD and public
page registry consumers, then reverse-traced every browser producer that could
feed the consented marketing-event sink and the explicit failure-report sink.
The structured-data slice was consistent. Two P1 context-disclosure defects and
