`consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains zero.

### AUDIT-PUBLIC-MARKETING-CLICK-CONTEXT-LEAK-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/components/website/resources/ResourceTrackedLink.tsx`,
  `src/components/website/resources/ArticleSection.tsx`,
  `src/components/website/WebsiteMarketingClickTracker.tsx`,
  `src/lib/website/publicAnalyticsContext.ts` and
  `src/lib/website/plausible.ts`; consented public click/copy event → browser
  context and destination → shared Google event projection → analytics vendor.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** after Restart 1110 minimized resource page
  views, active resource-link clicks still emitted raw referrer and hostname,
  query-bearing entry pages, arbitrary UTM text and raw destinations. Checklist
  copies emitted the full current URL. Delegated website CTA tracking emitted
  full internal/external anchor URLs; a WhatsApp target could therefore expose
  its phone/path/query content. Resource `eventProps` were spread last and
  could overwrite reserved safe fields.
- **Fix/regression:** link, copy and delegated click producers now reuse the
  shared URL/path/referrer-group/attribution boundary. Caller properties are
  projected before reserved fields. The central Google parameter projector is
  defense in depth: it removes raw `referrer` and `referrer_host`, strips
  URL/query/fragment context for destination/link/target keys, admits path-only
  page/entry keys and exact compact attribution tokens. External destinations
  retain origin only.

### AUDIT-FAILURE-DIAGNOSTIC-URL-CONTEXT-LEAK-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/components/shared/debug/ErrorReportButton.tsx` and
  `src/lib/runtime/runtimeDiagnostics.ts`; explicit failure-screen report →
  runtime diagnostics → sanitized logger/Sentry or user-copied support detail.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the explicit report payload included the full
  current `window.location.href` and raw `document.referrer`. The generic log
  sanitizer bounds strings but does not remove arbitrary URL queries,
  fragments or external paths, so reset tokens, private report hashes or
  referrer path details could enter monitoring or copied support data.
- **Fix/regression:** the runtime diagnostic URL boundary retains origin/path
  for the current origin, external origin only, and rejects non-HTTP and
  credential-bearing values. Query strings and fragments never enter the
  retained location/referrer fields.

### AUDIT-FAILURE-DIAGNOSTIC-ERROR-GETTER-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /

  failure report assembly → monitoring/copy fallback.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** diagnostic assembly read `error.digest` and
  `error.name` directly after the rest of the retained error had already moved
  to descriptor-safe projection. A throwing accessor or hostile Proxy could
  break the fallback while it was reporting the original failure.
- **Fix/regression:** digest and name now use the established bounded,
  own-descriptor helpers; direct optional-chain property reads are source-gated
  out.

## Restart 1109 addendum — SecurityOS evidence and runtime registry contracts

Restart 1109 changed direction to newly inventoried configuration/evidence
data and its internal security-registry consumer. Two P2 truth/reliability
defects and one P3 date-validation defect were confirmed and closed;
`consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains zero.

### AUDIT-SECURITYOS-EVIDENCE-EXECUTION-POLICY-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `packages/security-os/evidence/verifier-evidence.json` and
  `packages/security-os/scripts/lib/security-os-audit.ts`; approved evidence
  record → operator/agent command selection and safety decision.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** MenuList's Storage aggregate was declared
  `local-read-only` even though its nested npm command launches a Firebase
  Storage emulator. The Answerlattice dependency-security verifier was
  declared network-free even though it invokes `npm audit` against the package
  registry. The registry checked only that a top-level npm script existed, so
  inaccurate execution/network declarations still passed.
- **Fix/regression:** Storage evidence is now `firebase-emulator` with its
  existing local-emulator-only network policy; the dependency audit explicitly
  declares read-only package-registry access. Registry validation recursively
  resolves nested npm scripts for emulator use and inspects the registered
  dependency verifier for package-audit invocation. Mismatched declarations
  are errors. The internal registry runtime itself remains network- and
  command-execution-free.

### AUDIT-SECURITYOS-RUNTIME-SCHEMA-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `packages/security-os/schemas/security-os-schema.ts` and
  `packages/security-os/scripts/lib/security-os-audit.ts`; tracked JSON
  registry files → typed audit loops → reported security coverage/evidence.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** TypeScript interfaces were treated as runtime
  contracts through unchecked generic `JSON.parse` casts. Missing arrays,
  extra fields or wrong scalar shapes could crash the audit or flow into
  misleading checks instead of producing a controlled integrity failure.
- **Fix/regression:** strict Zod schemas now validate every manifest/evidence
  level, enum, literal boundary flag and required field before typed use.
  Read/parse and shape failures return bounded audit errors with zero claimed
  coverage. A narrow type bridge follows successful complete schema admission
  because this repository's Zod/compiler mode otherwise infers object
  properties as optional.

### AUDIT-SECURITYOS-CALENDAR-DATE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P3 / Closed locally /
  `packages/security-os/scripts/lib/security-os-audit.ts`; manifest/evidence
  `updatedAt` → current-registry integrity result.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the date check combined a shape regex with
  `Date.parse`, which normalizes impossible dates such as `2026-02-31`.
  Invalid audit currency metadata could therefore pass.
- **Fix/regression:** exact UTC year/month/day round-trip validation now rejects
  impossible days and invalid months while preserving valid ISO dates.

The SecurityOS package source, product profiles, complete manifest/evidence
data, registry CLI, source verifier, agent metadata/workflow and synchronized

## Restart 1108 addendum — Shared update and Business Copy runtime contracts

Restart 1108 changed direction to unreconciled compact type/schema boundaries,
then traced each active shallow-update consumer into its protected writer and
the Business Copy coverage result into desktop/mobile owner surfaces. Three P2
active defects and one P3 dormant utility defect were confirmed and closed;
`consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains zero.

### AUDIT-SHARED-OBJECT-DIFFERENCE-PROTOTYPE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/utils/deepMerge.ts::getObjectDifferance`; owner/platform form state →
  shallow changed-field projection → staff, tenant and Answerlattice article
  writer.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the untyped helper assigned every
  `Object.keys(updated)` value into `{}`. A JSON-owned `__proto__` key mutated
  the result prototype instead of becoming a normal field, while inherited
  original values and accessor/Proxy reads could affect or abort the mutation
  decision. This shared helper sits before tenant/persistence-sensitive
  writers even though those writers enforce their own downstream scope and
  shape contracts.
- **Fix/regression:** the now-generic projector compares enumerable own data
  fields only, rejects prototype-mutating keys, never executes accessors,
  contains enumeration failure and defines admitted values as ordinary own
  properties. Focused tests cover JSON prototype keys, inherited tenant-like
  fields, accessors and hostile Proxies. Staff scope/role, tenant lifecycle and
  Answerlattice article/ID gates remain green.

### AUDIT-DORMANT-DEEP-MERGE-CONTRACT-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P3 / Closed locally /
  `src/utils/deepMerge.ts::default`; generic object input → merged object.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** no active first-party callsite was found, but
  the exported utility was untyped, copied executable/prototype-sensitive
  properties, and silently dropped `considerArray` during nested recursion.
  Any future reuse would therefore expose a concrete unsafe and internally
  inconsistent contract.
- **Fix/regression:** merge inputs are unknown at runtime; only enumerable own
  data fields enter a fresh ordinary object, unsafe keys and hostile
  enumeration fail closed, and the array policy is preserved recursively.
  Nested array, pollution, accessor and Proxy cases pass.

### AUDIT-BUSINESS-COPY-COVERAGE-RUNTIME-SHAPE-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/services/ai/businessCopy/fieldConfig.ts`,
  `translationCoverageCore.ts` and `translationCoverage.ts`; persisted store
  copy/language fields → shared coverage and repair-gap calculation →
  desktop/mobile owner settings and AI translation repair.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the private localized-text guard claimed
  `Record<string,string>` while admitting legacy null entries and directly
  enumerated/indexed unknown persisted objects. Field readers likewise used
  optional chaining over unvalidated nested records. Malformed accessors or
  Proxies could execute or abort owner rendering/repair decisions, and the
  compile-time guard did not describe runtime reality.
- **Fix/regression:** coverage now snapshots enumerable own data descriptors,
  explicitly accepts string/null/undefined legacy entries, rejects accessors
  and malformed values, and resolves candidates from the contained snapshot.
  Field and keyword reads use contained own-data paths. Valid legacy,
  multilingual, null-gap, inherited, accessor and hostile-Proxy behavior
  passes with the Business Copy output and AI-accounting aggregates.

### AUDIT-BUSINESS-COPY-METADATA-UPDATE-PROJECTION-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/services/ai/businessCopy/metadata.ts::getBusinessCopyFieldKeysFromUpdate`;
  owner business-details update → manual-override metadata.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** broad `any`, optional chaining and `in`
  admitted inherited fields, executed nested accessors and threw for primitive
  or hostile inputs. Manual-override metadata could therefore be false,
  missing or abort its containing update-side workflow.
- **Fix/regression:** the detector now accepts `unknown` and admits only
  contained own data fields at the root and nested public/PWA records.
  Inherited, primitive and hostile-Proxy cases fail closed while all supported
  field keys retain their established order.

Focused hostile suites, all directly related writer/lifecycle gates, the
Business Copy output test, full AI-accounting aggregate, focused ESLint, exact
Node 22 TypeScript and diff hygiene pass. No Firestore rule/index,
Storage-rule or Firebase Function source changed, so no infrastructure
deployment applies.

  warning and text values and directly traversed unknown records. Attacker or

  and access failures; allowlist and bounded-text admission accept strings
  only; warnings are string-only, bounded and capped. Hostile accessors,

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/signaldesk/csvImport.ts`; uploaded CSV text → normalized target
  import rows → source-policy import transaction and target/contact authority.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the parser declared
  `SignalDeskTargetImportRow[]` while returning unchecked URLs, email, phone
  and Instagram values. Callers could therefore receive a compile-time-valid

### AUDIT-SIGNALDESK-AI-CRITIC-VERDICT-001

  `src/lib/signaldesk/aiProvider.ts`; Gemini critic response → volume/direct AI
  review decision → persisted child-run result and founder review.

  for `revise`. Provider response text is also read through a contained scalar
  boundary instead of a broad response cast/coercion.

### AUDIT-SIGNALDESK-SOURCE-QUALITY-DISTINCT-ACTIVATION-001

  unrelated window, a valid source run could lose all related targets and

  authority, strictly projects at most the import contract's 50 targets, and
  counts durable verified activation once per target through the shared
  activation predicate. This also removes its unrelated global outcome window
  and repeated-event sensitivity.

  outcome-set implementation and rejected the safer run-scoped durable-target

## Restart 1104 addendum — Compact authorization and mutation inputs

Restart 1104 changed to unreviewed compact shared-runtime boundaries feeding
authorization, reseller billing mutations and owner-referral acquisition.
Two P1 and one P2 defects were confirmed and closed;
`consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains zero.

### AUDIT-ROLE-ACTIVE-TYPE-AND-DUPLICATE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/permissions/hasPermission.ts`; persisted store roles plus session
  role ID → server/UI effective permission projection → protected owner/staff
  actions.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** role activation used truthiness, malformed
  role collections could throw, and the first of duplicate active definitions
  silently won. A persisted `"true"` activation or ambiguous duplicate could
  therefore grant authority, while corrupt collections produced availability
  failures rather than denial. Permission resolution now requires an array
  containing exactly one matching role whose `active` field is boolean
  `true`; every malformed or ambiguous case returns the complete denied map.
  Blank-only role IDs are no longer reported as valid.

### AUDIT-RESELLER-MUTATION-NUMERIC-COERCION-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/validation/resellerSchemas.ts`; authenticated reseller JSON body →
  onboarding/renewal/location-capacity billing scope and quantities →
  Auth/Firestore/payment state.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** `z.coerce.number()` converted arrays,
  booleans and numeric strings at a security- and billing-sensitive boundary.
  This admitted shapes outside the TypeScript/runtime contract before
  authorization, idempotency fingerprints and monetary calculations. All JSON
  numeric fields now require actual finite Zod numbers and integers where
  applicable; mutation objects are strict, and public business/email strings
  are trimmed before downstream identity and persistence use. Existing
  desktop/mobile producers already send numeric values.

### AUDIT-OWNER-REFERRAL-TOKEN-CANONICAL-ENCODING-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/ownerReferral/ownerReferralTokenServer.ts`; encrypted invite token
  fragment/cookie → capture validation → tenant/store referral attribution.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** Node's permissive Base64URL decoder accepted
  alternate padded or non-canonical representations of authenticated token
  segments. The token boundary now admits only nonempty canonical Base64URL
  for the secret, IV, ciphertext, tag and token ID, requires the exact random
  token-ID byte length, and accepts positive scope/time values only as actual
  numbers.

Validation passed the focused hostile boundary suite, owner-referral source
and real Firestore emulator suites, reseller dashboard/source/unit and real
onboarding-billing emulator suites, the complete auth/security failure matrix,
the MenuList API tenant-safety aggregate, exact Node 22 TypeScript, focused

Function source changed, so no infrastructure deployment applies.

## Restart 1103 addendum — Provider clients and media references

Restart 1103 changed to provider/client-boundary review across Google Analytics
server access, AI reference-image loading, Gemini key rotation and the
Answerlattice Firebase client/admin initialization surfaces. Three P1 defects
were confirmed and closed; `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains zero.

### AUDIT-GA-PRIVATE-KEY-ESCAPE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/analytics/server/index.ts`; governed environment credential →
  Google Analytics client → protected owner analytics reports.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** private-key normalization replaced literal
  newline characters with themselves rather than converting escaped `\\n`
  sequences. Standard single-line environment storage therefore produced an
  invalid credential and made analytics unavailable. A dedicated normalizer
  now converts escaped newlines while preserving already multiline keys.
  Provider error-code inspection is also exception-contained.

### AUDIT-AI-REFERENCE-IMAGE-SIGNATURE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/apiUtils/index.ts`; tenant/store-scoped Firebase Storage or inline
  image reference → bounded server fetch/Base64 → Gemini image edit/generation.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** response/data-URL MIME was allowlisted but
  bytes were not correlated to the declared type; inline Base64 admitted
  arbitrary whitespace/characters. Mislabeled content could cross the provider
  boundary as an image. Both fetched and inline bytes now pass the strict
  existing JPEG/PNG/WebP magic-byte contract, inline Base64 is canonical and
  decoded size remains capped before provider use.

### AUDIT-APP-AI-KEY-CONCURRENT-ATTRIBUTION-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/google/genAi/keyManager.ts` plus the retry range in
  `src/lib/google/genAi/aiGateway.ts`; concurrent MenuList/SignalDesk/
  Answerlattice provider requests → key selection → delayed success/rate-limit
  feedback → rotation/cooldown.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the app key manager attributed completion
  through mutable `currentIndex`. A concurrent request could rotate that
  cursor before an earlier request completed, causing the wrong key to be
  cooled down or reset. Feedback now carries the exact client that served the
  attempt, matching the already-correct Functions implementation; rotation
  advances only when the limited client is still current.

The Answerlattice Firebase Admin/client initializers and the modular Firebase
Admin compatibility surface were reviewed fully with no new confirmed defect;
their explicit shared/separate project checks and configured-null build
boundary remain intact. Validation passed the new provider client suite,

aggregate, complete AI accounting, exact Node 22 TypeScript, full `src` ESLint
and diff hygiene. No Firebase Function/rule/index/Storage-rule source changed,

## Restart 1100 addendum — Mutation acknowledgements and staff credential sharing

Restart 1100 changed direction to authorization/acknowledgement-first review
across owner route permission requirements, multi-outlet mutation responses,
staff login sharing and scheduler-hour normalization. Two P1 and two P2
defects were confirmed and closed; `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains zero.
The permission and scheduler utilities produced no new confirmed defect in
their current calling contexts.

### AUDIT-OUTLET-ACTION-RESPONSE-IDENTITY-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/multiOutlet/outletActionResponseGuards.ts` and desktop/mobile
  location consumers; protected create/rename/deactivate mutation →
  successful JSON acknowledgement → tenant store-list state.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** rename and deactivate acknowledgements were
  checked only for broad field types. They were not correlated to the outlet
  ID submitted by the active request, and rename was not correlated to the
  submitted slug. A stale, crossed or otherwise mismatched successful response
  could therefore update the wrong outlet in local owner state or present a
  success for a different rename.
- **Fix/regression:** rename and deactivate guards now accept the request's
  expected identity and fail closed unless the response exactly matches it.
  Desktop and mobile callers bind the acknowledgement before any local
  mutation or success message. Focused tests exercise mismatched IDs/slugs;
  both multi-location and public-business-truth aggregates pass.

### AUDIT-OUTLET-ACTION-RESPONSE-SHAPE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/multiOutlet/outletActionResponseGuards.ts`; mutation response JSON →
  typed create/rename/deactivate owner state.
- **Observed/fix:** finite fractional, negative and unsafe numeric IDs or
  quantities passed; arbitrary records passed as an `OutletPolicy`; slugs and
  prior-slug arrays were unbounded. The boundary now requires canonical
  positive safe-integer identities/quantities, canonical bounded outlet slugs,
  all governed boolean policy fields, a nonblank tenant name and a capped
  prior-slug chain.

### AUDIT-STAFF-SHARE-SIGNIN-HOST-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/staffManagement/shareLoginDetails.ts`; one-time staff ID/passcode →
  clipboard/native/WhatsApp share → staff sign-in.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the credential message derived its sign-in
  destination from `window.location.origin`. Rendering the owner surface
  through an unexpected host could therefore embed that host in a sensitive
  credential handoff, and server rendering used a divergent relative path.
- **Fix/regression:** outside explicit local-development hosts, the message now
  uses the governed `SIGNIN_URL` single source of truth on both server and
  client. Local localhost/LAN development retains its current-origin route.
  The focused suite pins deterministic text and WhatsApp output.

### AUDIT-STAFF-SHARE-LINE-INJECTION-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/staffManagement/shareLoginDetails.ts`; staff/product/sign-in
  strings → human-readable credential message.
- **Observed/fix:** embedded control characters/newlines were retained, so a
  malformed display value could introduce a second `Passcode` or `Sign in`
  line and make the credential handoff ambiguous. Every line value is now
  control-free, whitespace-collapsed and bounded before message/title
  construction; the four-line contract is regression-tested.

Validation passed both new focused suites, multi-location, the complete public
business truth aggregate, exact Node 22 TypeScript, full `src` ESLint and diff
hygiene. No Firebase rule/index, Storage rule or Function source changed.

## Restart 1098 addendum — Slug, shortcut, location and phone identity

Restart 1098 switched to identity-first review across project slug
reservation/allocation, PWA shortcut construction, persisted external-location
bindings and app/Functions phone normalization. One P1 and three P2 defects
were confirmed and closed; `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains zero.

### AUDIT-PHONE-DIAL-PREFIX-COLLISION-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/phone/phoneNumber.ts`, `functions/src/utils/phoneNumber.ts`; owner,
  persisted or public phone fields → normalized E.164/username → OTP, public
  call/WhatsApp and notification delivery.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** any national number beginning with its
  country's dial digits was treated as already international. An Indian
  10-digit mobile beginning `91` therefore remained only 10 digits instead of
  receiving `+91`, sending OTP/WhatsApp delivery toward the wrong destination.
  Dial stripping could also turn an invalid 16-digit `+` input into a valid
  looking 15-digit output.
- **Fix/regression:** only explicit `+`/`00` input or a bounded unprefixed
  legacy number longer than 10 digits is treated as international. Root local
  projection and both app/Functions delivery digits agree; original explicit
  international input is capped at 15 digits before stripping. Unknown scalar
  conversion hooks are not executed.

### AUDIT-PROJECT-SLUG-UNKNOWN-TRAVERSAL-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/menu/projectSlugOwnership.ts`; current/deleted project summaries →
  slug collision/reservation → public menu URL allocation.
- **Observed/fix:** `Object.entries`, summary fields, previous-slug arrays and
  Date methods trusted unknown persisted structures. Accessor/Proxy/Date-proxy
  failures aborted transactions instead of preserving URL authority. Own-data
  reads and capped previous-slug/project traversal are contained; ambiguous
  current ownership fails closed as claimed, while malformed timestamp values
  remain non-reservations under the existing retention policy.

### AUDIT-PWA-SHORTCUT-URL-ACCESS-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/pwa/shortcutsBuilder.ts`; manifest shortcut inputs and language →
  public shortcut URLs and launch attribution.
- **Observed/fix:** direct info getters could abort manifest generation and
  string concatenation placed `entry_source` after a URL fragment or duplicated
  an old value. Inputs are now contained own strings, the menu shortcut admits
  only a same-origin absolute path, and URL parsing replaces attribution before
  preserving the fragment.

### AUDIT-EXTERNAL-LOCATION-IDENTITY-ACCESS-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/public-truth-tools/externalLocationIdentity.ts`; owner Maps link or
  grounded Maps/GBP evidence → persisted owner-confirmed provider binding.
- **Observed/fix:** candidate/binding fields and grounding-source slices used
  direct reads and traversal, so malformed provider output or persisted data
  could abort confirmation/normalization. Every field is now own-data-only and
  the first eight sources are snapshotted with exception containment; provider,
  source, resolution, ID, URI and timestamp correlation remains unchanged.

Focused behavior suites, complete public-customer delivery, menu-project
editor, public-business-truth, MenuList Functions build, exact Node 22 root
TypeScript, focused ESLint and diff hygiene pass. Two stale source assertions
were updated to require the new path/own-field slug boundaries. Because the

  rejects invalid sizes outside 1–4,096, URLs over 4,096 characters, invalid
  natural dimensions and decoded images above 100 million pixels, retaining
  its graceful null fallback.

## Restart 1096 addendum — Shared input, URL and identifier admission

Restart 1096 continued from external media into the generic input-security
module, then re-read the compact PWA icon, prepared-media and image-quality
boundaries and their active consumers. Two P2 and three P3 defects were
confirmed and closed; `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains zero.

### AUDIT-GENERIC-NUMERIC-ID-SAFE-INTEGER-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/security/inputValidation.ts`; request numeric tenant/store ID →
  generic Zod boundary → downstream scoped operation.
- **Observed/fix:** digit strings were transformed with `Number` and only
  checked as positive, so an oversized string became positive `Infinity`;
  fractional numeric IDs and noncanonical leading-zero strings also passed.
  Admission now requires a canonical positive safe integer.

### AUDIT-GENERIC-URL-HOST-BOUNDARY-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally / same module; external

- **Observed/root cause/impact:** `hostname.endsWith(domain)` admitted

  classifier are rejected; allowlists match only the exact host or a

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P3 / Closed locally / generic file metadata →

- **Observed/fix:** the schema accepted zero, negative and fractional byte

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P3 / Closed locally / generic query object →
  sanitized Firestore scalar filters.
- **Observed/fix:** the helper used broad `any`, retained `NaN`/infinities and
  built a normal object whose `__proto__` key did not have ordinary data-key
  semantics. It now consumes/returns unknown scalar records, retains finite

- **Observed/fix:** the error promised Firestore's 1,500-byte limit but checked

## Restart 1095 addendum — Upload bytes and Base64 image identity

Restart 1095 continued external-file-input-first through the server upload
validator used by public Create Menu, the shared browser/generated-image magic
byte boundary, signature definitions and active consumers. Two P1 upload
admission defects and two P2 image-contract defects were confirmed and closed;
`consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains zero.

### AUDIT-SERVER-FILE-ACTUAL-SIZE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/security/fileValidation.ts`; public multipart image/PDF metadata
  plus uploaded bytes → Create Menu extraction admission.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the validator enforced only the untrusted
  claimed size. A caller could submit a larger buffer or Blob under a smaller
  claim, bypassing the governed per-type byte limit before extraction.
- **Fix/regression:** claimed size must be a positive safe integer, Blob size
  is checked before materialization, and the resulting byte length must exactly
  equal the claim and remain within the type limit. Mismatch, empty,
  non-finite and oversized content fail before downstream work.

### AUDIT-SERVER-WEBP-RIFF-IDENTITY-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally / same server validator;
  uploaded bytes → MIME identity → public menu extraction.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** generic type detection returned WebP for any
  RIFF container because the shared signature begins with `RIFF`. WAV and other
  RIFF payloads could therefore pass a claimed `image/webp` check.
- **Fix/regression:** WebP admission now requires both `RIFF` and `WEBP` at
  offset eight. A WAV-shaped RIFF regression is rejected while valid JPEG,
  PNG and WebP signatures remain admitted.

### AUDIT-IMAGE-BASE64-SIZE-MIME-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/security/magicBytesValidator.ts`; browser/generated Base64 image,
  declared MIME and byte count → media preparation, upload and AI cache/output.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** decoded bytes were materialized and checked
  without reconciling their real length to the claimed size; invalid numeric
  sizes were admitted, data-URL MIME could disagree with the expected type,
  and unpadded Base64 length used rounding that overcounted a one-byte payload.
- **Fix/regression:** Base64 syntax is validated before decode, decoded length
  is exact (including padded/unpadded input) and must equal a positive integer
  claim, data-URL MIME must match, and invalid/fractional/non-finite sizes fail.

### AUDIT-IMAGE-JPG-ALIAS-CONTRACT-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally / same image boundary;
  accepted `image/jpg` input → shared JPEG signature lookup.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the public allowlist advertised
  `image/jpg`, but signatures are keyed only by canonical `image/jpeg`, so
  valid files using the supported alias always failed.
- **Fix/regression:** image MIME identity is normalized once and `image/jpg`
  maps to `image/jpeg` before allowlist, data-URL and signature comparison.

Validation passed the focused file-boundary behavior suite, all 371 Menu
Extraction source assertions, AI accounting hardening, exact root TypeScript,
focused ESLint and diff hygiene. No Firestore rule/index, Storage rule or
Firebase Function source changed, so no infrastructure deployment applies.

## Restart 1094 addendum — Generic webhook signature and source admission

Restart 1094 continued external-input-first through the inventory-only generic
webhook validator, signature wrappers, provider detection and IP allowlists.
The live Razorpay payment route remains on its separately audited dedicated
validator; this helper is currently dormant but executable first-party

### AUDIT-GENERIC-WEBHOOK-CIDR-ALLOWLIST-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/security/webhookValidation.ts`; trusted request IP plus provider
  allowlist → webhook source admission.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the public function and examples promised
  CIDR support, and every Razorpay allowlist entry is a `/27`, but the
  implementation performed exact string equality only. No real Razorpay IP
  could ever pass those maintained entries, making the defense unusable and
  encouraging callers to bypass it.
- **Fix/regression:** strict canonical IPv4 parsing and unsigned prefix masks
  now support `/0` through `/32`; exact normalized IPv4/IPv6 entries remain
  supported. Ambiguous comma-separated forwarded lists, whitespace, leading
  zeroes, malformed prefixes and non-IPv4 CIDR fail closed. Tests pin both
  edges of the two current Razorpay ranges and adjacent rejection.

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally / same helper; GitHub-style
  prefixed signature → HMAC comparison.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** a configured prefix was stripped when
  present, but absence did not fail. A raw digest without required `sha256=`
  therefore validated successfully, weakening the exported provider contract.
- **Fix/regression:** a configured prefix is mandatory and mismatch is a
  bounded diagnostic plus false result. Correct GitHub, Razorpay and Shopify
  encodings, body tampering, missing prefix, wrong length and missing secret
  are covered.

### AUDIT-GENERIC-WEBHOOK-WEAK-HASH-CONTRACT-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P3 / Closed locally / generic HMAC algorithm
  type → future webhook integrations.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the exported type advertised SHA-1 and MD5 as
  supported choices despite the repository security posture and no active
  compatibility consumer. This was a concrete future misuse path in shared
  security infrastructure.
- **Fix:** the compile-time contract now admits only SHA-256 and SHA-512;
  existing provider wrappers are unchanged.

## Restart 1093 addendum — Cross-runtime outbound network target admission

Restart 1093 changed direction to external-input-first and traced root app URL
validation, Answerlattice public-page discovery, Menu Link Import checks and
Answerlattice Functions integration delivery through URL parsing, DNS
resolution, address admission, redirect handling, pinned socket lookup,
remote-address verification, response type/encoding/length checks and bounded

### AUDIT-SERVER-NETWORK-IPV6-CLASSIFICATION-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P0 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/security/serverNetworkTarget.ts`,
  `functions-answerlattice/src/utils/networkTarget.ts` and the new
  cross-runtime regression; public/provider URL → DNS/literal address →
  outbound root or Functions request.
- **Observed/root cause/security impact:** both generic server guards used
  prefix checks for only `fc`, `fd`, `fe80:` and dotted
  `::ffff:<IPv4>`. Valid link-local addresses across the rest of `fe80::/10`,
  multicast, hexadecimal IPv4-mapped loopback, documentation/special
  assignments and malformed colon addresses could be classified as public.
  Root public-page intake and Functions integrations could therefore pass an
  internal/non-global IPv6 target through their pre-request SSRF gate.
- **Fix/regression:** both runtimes now parse exact eight-segment IPv6,
  including compressed, zone and dotted-IPv4 forms, and fail closed on
  malformed input. Unspecified/loopback, unique-local, full link-local,
  multicast, IPv4-compatible/mapped, IETF special, documentation, 6to4 and
  non-global-unicast ranges are blocked. Missing IPv4 special/documentation/
  benchmarking ranges were aligned at the same boundary. The cross-runtime
  suite proves identical rejection for 13 IPv4 and 14 IPv6 adversarial forms
  while retaining public `8.8.8.8` and `2001:4860:4860::8888`.

`boundedPublicTextFetch.ts` was fully reread and produced no additional
confirmed defect: every redirect is reparsed and DNS-resolved, the selected
address is pinned through the request lookup callback, the connected remote
address is checked again, credentials/nonstandard ports/non-text or encoded
responses are rejected, and streamed bytes are capped. Validation passed the

## Restart 1092 addendum — Digital Screen transaction authority and token identity

Restart 1092 restarted at the authenticated owner mutation entry point and
traced session actor/scope, permission admission, transaction-current
store/tenant truth, canonical summary/private-control/public-mirror writes,
owner response serialization and mutation retry identity. One P0
cross-tenant race, one P1 setup failure and two P2 limiter/idempotency defects
were confirmed and closed; `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains zero.

### AUDIT-DIGITAL-SCREEN-MANAGEMENT-SCOPE-RACE-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P0 / Closed locally /
  `screenManagementServer.ts`, the management route/source gate and new Admin
  emulator; authenticated owner permission read → transaction → campaigns
  summary, private control and public mirror.
- **Observed/root cause/security impact:** permission admission read current
  store ownership before the transaction, but the transaction read only the
  screen summary/control. If a store moved from tenant A to tenant B between
  those steps, tenant A's already-authorized request could still mutate every
  screen document and write a private control row naming tenant A.
- **Fix/regression:** the same transaction now reads the authoritative store
  and tenant and applies exact alias/document/lifecycle admission before any
  screen read-modify-write. The credential-isolated Admin emulator initializes
  a valid screen, reassigns the store, then proves tenant A receives
  `digital_screen_scope_changed` and the summary, control and public mirror
  remain byte-stable.

### AUDIT-DIGITAL-SCREEN-TOKEN-GENERATOR-CONTRACT-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `privateScreenControl.ts`; owner initialization → generated bearer token →
  canonical route/control validator and owner response.
- **Observed/root cause/public impact:** the generator returned unrestricted
  Base64URL, which sometimes contains `-` or `_`; every maintained screen token
  validator accepts alphanumeric characters only. Initialization therefore
  succeeded or threw `digital_screen_owner_state_invalid` based on random
  output. The new emulator exposed this by passing once and then failing on a
  later independent execution.
- **Fix/regression:** generation uses rejection sampling over the same
  cryptographic 16-byte source until its 22-character Base64URL encoding is
  entirely alphanumeric. This preserves validator/URL compatibility and full
  entropy without lossy replacement. Each lifecycle run validates 128
  generated tokens, and the Admin emulator passed three independent runs.

### AUDIT-DIGITAL-SCREEN-MANAGEMENT-RATE-SCOPE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/app/api/digital-screens/route.ts`; authenticated session → pre-Firestore
  mutation limiter.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the limiter selected the first truthy user
  alias, fell back to email/`unknown`, stored the raw identity in the key and
  omitted tenant/store. Contradictory aliases or tenant switches could share
  or evade the intended write budget and expose raw identity to the limiter
  backend.
- **Fix/regression:** the existing exact session actor projector must succeed;
  actor, tenant and store are independently hashed into the key before the
  permission read. The feature source gate pins all three dimensions.

### AUDIT-DIGITAL-SCREEN-SLIDE-IDEMPOTENCY-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `screenManagementServer.ts` and expected-error contracts; `add_slide`
  request/retry → transaction-current pinned-slide state.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** an existing slide ID made every later
  `add_slide` a silent success, even when image, caption or expiry differed.
  A caller could therefore receive success for content that was not persisted.
- **Fix/regression:** exact same-content replay remains a no-write success;
  reuse with different content returns the bounded 409 stale-state response.
  The Admin emulator proves the conflicting image/caption case and lifecycle
  tests pin its client response.

Validation passed three independent management Admin emulator executions, the
complete Digital Screens aggregate including direct rules and Admin emulator
coverage, MenuList API tenant safety and its three children, exact root
TypeScript, focused ESLint and diff hygiene. `publicScreenState.ts`,
`slideGenerator.ts` and all current write/response branches were fully reread;

## Restart 1091 addendum — Digital Screen project-to-public projection

Restart 1091 restarted from raw Firestore project documents and traced
localized menu fields, category/item ordering, availability, prices, tags and
images into the public Digital Screen menu projection and owner health
surfaces. One P1 public-truth defect and two P2 malformed/legacy-state defects
were confirmed and closed; `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains zero.

### AUDIT-DIGITAL-SCREEN-PROJECT-AVAILABILITY-COERCION-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/screen/screenContent.ts`; persisted extracted menu item →
  `MenuItemForSlide` → evergreen/menu-board public TV output.
- **Observed/root cause/public impact:** availability used
  `item.available !== false` and bestseller used `item.isBestSeller || false`.
  Malformed or legacy strings such as `"false"` and `"true"` therefore became
  publicly available/promoted truth. A menu item explicitly carrying invalid
  availability state could remain visible on a customer-facing TV.
- **Fix/regression:** missing availability retains the established legacy
  default of available, but only the booleans `true` and `false` are admitted;
  any present malformed value fails unavailable. Bestseller admission now
  requires exact boolean `true`. The lifecycle regression proves string
  lookalikes cannot select public truth.

### AUDIT-DIGITAL-SCREEN-PROJECT-TRAVERSAL-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally / same projector; unknown
  Firestore project/localized fields → bounded normalized screen DTO.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** localized text used direct property access
  and `Object.values`, arrays were traversed directly, order fields were passed
  to `Number()`, and category IDs became ordinary object keys. Accessors,
  Proxies or coercion hooks could execute/throw during public SSR; a
  prototype-like category ID could mutate the category lookup object; and
  malformed projects had no file/category/item inspection bound.
- **Fix/regression:** own data descriptors are the only accepted field source,
  array snapshots skip accessors and contain Proxy failures, ordering accepts
  only nonnegative safe integers/canonical decimal strings, category lookup is
  a `Map`, and file/category/item inspection is bounded. A malformed project
  returns an empty projection. Tests cover inherited/accessor text, indexed
  tag accessors, a prototype-like category ID, throwing coercion hooks and a
  throwing project Proxy.

### AUDIT-DIGITAL-SCREEN-FUTURE-HEALTH-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/screen/screenHealth.ts`; persisted server seen timestamp → desktop,
  mobile and Output Center owner health copy.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the health projector clamped every negative
  age to zero, so a materially future-dated corrupt/legacy timestamp appeared
  as `Seen recently` / `Seen just now`. This hid invalid operational state
  behind a healthy owner signal.
- **Fix/regression:** up to five minutes of clock skew remains recent; a
  timestamp further in the future now returns the existing `Check TV` stale
  state with bounded `TV time needs checking` detail. The lifecycle suite pins
  the future-hour case.

Digital Screens aggregate including its real Firestore rules emulator, exact

## Restart 1090 addendum — Digital Screen malformed-state totality

Restart 1090 continued from the compact Digital Screen runtime boundary and
traced persisted browser-cache metadata plus owner/display timestamps into
offline admission, expiry, health and lifecycle consumers. Two P2 malformed
state defects were confirmed and closed; `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains
zero.

### AUDIT-DIGITAL-SCREEN-OFFLINE-CACHE-COERCION-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/screen/screenRuntime.ts`; browser cache metadata and server content
  version → offline-cache admission → public Digital Screen display.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** cache admission repeatedly passed explicitly
  unknown values to `Number()`. This could execute caller-controlled
  `valueOf`/`toString` hooks and admitted noncanonical values such as booleans
  or zero-padded numeric strings as valid cache metadata. A corrupt or
  attacker-influenced browser cache could therefore select stale display data
  through a weaker contract than the persisted content-version boundary.
- **Fix/regression:** one noncoercing scalar parser now admits only nonnegative
  safe-integer numbers or canonical decimal strings. The current server
  version must also be a nonnegative safe integer, and cache entry count must
  be positive. Lifecycle tests prove a throwing coercion hook is never
  executed and noncanonical scalar forms fail closed.

### AUDIT-DIGITAL-SCREEN-TIMESTAMP-TOTALITY-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/screen/screenTimestamp.ts`; Firestore/serialized/browser timestamp
  forms → display expiry and owner health/seen projections.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the exported `unknown`-to-`Date | null`
  normalizer directly evaluated `instanceof`, `Array.isArray` and timestamp
  properties outside complete exception containment. Date Proxies, revoked
  Proxies or throwing `seconds` getters could therefore escape the supposedly
  total boundary and abort display or owner rendering.
- **Fix/regression:** every classification/property/method read is now inside
  one fail-closed exception boundary. Date validation invokes the intrinsic
  `Date.prototype.getTime` and returns a fresh finite Date, rejecting Date
  Proxies without calling their traps as date values. Focused tests cover a
  throwing seconds getter, ordinary Date Proxy and revoked Date Proxy.

Validation passed `npm run test:screen-timestamp`, `npm run
test:digital-screens:lifecycle`, the complete `npm run
verify:digital-screens-boundary` aggregate including its real Firestore rules
emulator, exact root `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false`, focused ESLint and
`git diff --check`. No Firestore rule/index, Storage rule or Firebase Function
source changed in this restart, so no infrastructure deployment applies.

Restart 1089 restarted from the public-menu UI analytics entry point and
traced menu view, alias switch, language adoption, item view/tap, third-party
pixel and shared analytics writer flows. One P1 identity-attribution defect and

### AUDIT-PUBLIC-MENU-ANALYTICS-SCOPE-ALIAS-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `clientWebsite/AnalyticsContext.tsx`; server-projected store →
  tenant/store analytics scope → public event writer/diagnostics.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the context independently used

### AUDIT-PUBLIC-MENU-LANGUAGE-SCOPE-TRANSITION-001

  tenant/store/project/language props → ten-second dwell timer → language
  adoption event.

  project changes. If the provider instance transitioned from business A in
  English to business B in Hindi, the new business could receive a false
  English-to-Hindi adoption event after dwell. This polluted owner analytics

### AUDIT-RETIRED-SCREEN-SERVICE-WORKER-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `public/screen-sw.js` and the Digital Screens gate; historical root-scope
  worker registration → activation/fetch interception → public screen/API/
  image cache → Digital Screen truth.
- **Observed/root cause/public/cache impact:** active registration code and
  current docs say the standalone worker is retired, but its publicly served
  script still installed a live cache-first handler for screen pages,
  `/api/screen/*` and all images. A surviving historical registration could
  therefore serve expired screen/API truth and cache error responses outside
  the current server-cache/content-version contract. Its activation also
  enumerated and deleted every cache whose name was not its own, crossing
  owner/customer product cache boundaries.

  tombstone so existing registrations can update. It intercepts no fetches;
  install activates immediately, activation deletes only

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `public/sw-customer.js` and the Customer App gate; customer/custom-domain
  worker activation → Cache Storage cleanup → current offline fallback and
  unrelated same-origin application caches.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** activation deleted every cache other than the
  current customer offline cache. On a verified custom domain this could erase
  caches owned by a prior or parallel same-origin application, not merely
  retired MenuList workers. Menu content was not exposed, but the cleanup
  exceeded MenuList cache authority and could destroy unrelated offline state.
- **Fix/compatibility/regression:** cleanup now admits only exact retired
  MenuList cache names and the known Serwist/Workbox precache prefixes. The
  frozen `/offline`-only customer cache and network-first navigation behavior
  are unchanged. The Customer App gate rejects the former broad filter and
  requires the owned-cache classifier.

## Restart 1082 addendum — Public navigation source attribution

Restart 1082 traced OBP menu cards and external links through URL
normalization, analytics source attribution, tracking settlement and browser
navigation. One P3 malformed-URL logic defect was confirmed and closed;
`consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains zero.

### AUDIT-ANALYTICS-SOURCE-FALLBACK-FRAGMENT-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P3 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/analytics/sourceAttribution.ts` and `OBPMenuCTA.tsx`; public
  menu/share/QR/OBP URL → `entry_source` projection → native navigation and
  analytics.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** normal URL parsing correctly inserted the
  source before a fragment. On parse failure, however, both shared and OBP
  fallback code manually appended `?` or `&` to the end of the original text.
  If that text contained a fragment, the parameter landed inside the fragment,
  was not sent as a query, and navigation was mutated despite attribution
  remaining absent.
- **Fix/compatibility:** parse failure still emits the existing bounded,
  capped diagnostic but now returns the original URL byte-for-byte. Valid
  absolute and relative URLs retain exact query replacement and fragment
  preservation.
- **Regression/validation:** the analytics browser suite pins relative and
  absolute fragment ordering plus byte-identical malformed fallback. The full
  public-business-truth aggregate, exact TypeScript, focused ESLint and diff
  hygiene pass.

`OBPMenuCTA` and `OBPExternalLinks` were fully reread. Their remaining behavior
correctly normalizes public destinations, reconciles real and placeholder
actions, preserves native alternate/blank navigation, bounds tracking wait to
800 ms and propagates secondary-card analytics failures to the shared
navigation handler. Concurrent first-party additions expanded the regenerated
snapshot during this restart to 8,587 in-scope files and 420 exclusions: 1,778
reviewed, 1,869 in-progress and 4,940 inventory-only. No additional defect or
Firebase change was found.

### AUDIT-CUSTOMER-APP-INVALID-SCOPE-EVENT-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `CustomerAppController.tsx` and its PWA source gate; OBP/menu tenant-store

  and diff hygiene pass.

## Restart 1079 addendum — OBP localization and public-truth source gates

### AUDIT-OBP-I18N-UNKNOWN-TRAVERSAL-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/app/client/obp/i18n.ts`; committed locale dictionary plus runtime
  interpolation values → brand/outlet OBP headings, status, actions, photos
  and customer facts.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** dotted dictionary lookup used ordinary
  property access against broad `Record<string, any>` values. A key such as
  `constructor.name` traversed the object prototype and returned `Object`.
  Interpolation also read values normally and called broad `String(value)`, so
  a malformed getter or conversion object could execute or throw while

  data descriptors, contain descriptor failures, cap dotted paths, and
  serialize only finite numbers, booleans and strings. Accessors, inherited
  properties, objects and non-finite numbers resolve to the established empty
  placeholder behavior. Current locale fallback and valid scalar
  interpolation remain unchanged.
- **Regression:** `test-obp-i18n-boundary.ts` covers current and unknown
  locales, missing/prototype paths, finite scalar output, non-finite values,
  inherited values and a throwing getter that remains uncalled. It is a child
  of the Official Business Page aggregate.

  single-command package string, preventing registration of a behavioral child
  gate. Concurrent Digital Screen cache work also changed store revalidation

  behavior commands, pins the current options-bearing store cache call and

  The concurrent verifier update for the removed browser invalidation module

## Restart 1078 addendum — Registration email-domain boundary

Restart 1078 restarted from the authentication intake boundary and traced
email text through syntax checks, canonical domain extraction, reserved-domain
policy, the 71,743-entry disposable-domain artifact, registration consumers
and the Auth/Onboarding aggregate. Two P2 validation defects and one P3
maintenance-integrity defect were confirmed and closed. The repository-wide
validation replay then exposed and closed one separate P2 compile defect in
the concurrently changed Digital Screen status header. Because this restart
found defects, `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains zero.

### AUDIT-DISPOSABLE-EMAIL-SUBDOMAIN-BYPASS-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/validation/disposableEmailDomains.ts`; registration email →
  disposable-domain policy → account admission.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** disposable detection performed one exact Set
  lookup. An address on a subdomain such as `user@sub.mailinator.com` bypassed
  the parent disposable-service entry. This weakened registration abuse
  controls but did not establish tenant access or persisted-data disclosure.
- **Fix/compatibility:** email extraction now requires exactly one `@` with
  nonempty local and domain parts. Detection checks the canonical domain and
  each bounded parent suffix, so disposable service subdomains are rejected
  while unrelated sibling domains remain unaffected. Imported JSON values are
  admitted only after scalar, length, dot and canonical-character validation;
  the established fallback Set remains available if the validated artifact is
  empty.
- **Regression:** `test-email-domain-validation.ts` pins exact and subdomain
  disposable detection and validates all 71,743 committed artifact entries
  for uniqueness, lowercase normalization and bounded canonical structure.

### AUDIT-EMAIL-DOMAIN-SUBSTRING-SYNTAX-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/validation/emailDomainValidator.ts`; registration email →
  syntax/reserved-domain validation → account admission and owner error.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** reserved tokens were checked with
  `domain.includes(...)`, so legitimate permanent domains containing `test`
  or `local` (for example `contest.com` or `locality.org`) were rejected.
  Conversely, general validation did not enforce DNS label length, leading or
  trailing hyphens, total-domain length, local-part length or a nonnumeric
  top-level label.
- **Fix/compatibility:** reserved values now match only the exact domain or a
  subdomain. Domain admission enforces 63-character labels, 253-character
  total length, canonical label edges, a top-level label containing a letter,
  a 64-character local part and a 254-character total email. Existing
  lowercase normalization, disposable blocking and owner-facing result shape
  are unchanged.
- **Regression:** the focused suite covers legitimate token-containing
  domains, reserved exact/subdomain values, invalid labels, numeric TLDs,
  local/domain/email bounds, multiple separators and a valid punycode label.

### AUDIT-DIGITAL-SCREEN-ICON-EXPORT-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `DigitalScreenSettings/index.tsx`; current screen heartbeat → owner Settings
  health summary.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** concurrent health-state UI work imported
  `LuCircleAlert`, which the repository's pinned `react-icons/lu` package does
  not export. Exact TypeScript therefore failed and the affected application
  source could not build.
- **Fix/regression:** the stale-state branch now uses the package's verified
  `LuAlertCircle` export; no screen state, persistence, tenant, cache or
  customer behavior changed. Exact root TypeScript and focused ESLint pass.

### AUDIT-DISPOSABLE-DOMAIN-UPDATE-ATOMICITY-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P3 / Closed locally /
  `scripts/update-disposable-email-domains.ts`, the disposable-domain source
  comment and active security guide; upstream domain artifact → committed
  registration policy data.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the only documented regeneration path used
  `curl -s ... -o` directly against the authoritative file. An HTTP failure,
  truncated body, invalid JSON, duplicate/unsorted list or structurally invalid
  upstream entry could replace or truncate registration policy data before
  validation. This was a maintenance-time integrity risk rather than a
  currently malformed artifact.
- **Fix/regression:** the repository command downloads with an HTTP status,
  timeout and five-megabyte bound; validates JSON, minimum population, exact
  scalar normalization, domain structure, strict ordering and uniqueness; then
  writes a unique temporary file and atomically renames it. Failure removes
  the temporary file and preserves the current artifact. The focused test
  exercises the validator against the entire committed list plus undersized,
  duplicate and noncanonical variants. The command was not run against the
  network during this audit because no source-list refresh was requested.

run verify:auth-onboarding-flow` aggregate and all of its set-claims,

## Restart 1073 addendum — Monitoring inspection and alternate-envelope privacy

Restart 1073 restarted from the smallest remaining runtime inventory and
traced browser console capture, the central secure logger, shared Sentry event
sanitization, client/server/Edge initialization, tracing transactions and
error-sampled Replay delivery. Two defects were confirmed and closed locally,
so `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains zero.

### AUDIT-MONITORING-UNKNOWN-INSPECTION-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/security/secureLogger.ts`,
  `src/lib/monitoring/sentryShared.ts`,
  `src/lib/debug/clientConsoleBuffer.ts`,
  `src/lib/localLogs/localLogsTracker.ts`; arbitrary runtime failure/context →
  bounded console, support-ticket or Sentry diagnostic.
- **Observed/root cause:** the central logger and Sentry sanitizer used direct
  enumeration, array traversal, broad string conversion and JSON
  serialization on unknown values. Getters, Proxies, `toJSON`, `valueOf` or
  `toString` could execute or throw while the application was already handling
  a failure. The console wrapper could therefore replace a normal console call
  with an exception; monitoring could lose the original failure or inspect
  unintended values.
- **Security/data/cache/public impact:** attacker-controlled or malformed
  diagnostic context could cause an availability/observability failure and
  execute conversion hooks. No tenant datastore, cache or public-truth write
  occurs in this flow, and no confirmed cross-tenant read was observed.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** sanitizers now inspect capped own enumerable
  data descriptors, skip accessors/symbols, contain Proxy failures, traverse
  arrays by bounded own numeric descriptors, never stringify non-scalar
  unknown values, and make sensitive-data inspection fail closed. Error
  presence/length metadata and valid scalar/log context remain compatible.
- **Regression/validation:** the behavior suite proves getters and `toJSON`
  remain uncalled, broken own-key/prototype Proxies cannot throw, sensitive
  inspection fails closed, and the installed browser console buffer preserves
  a safe bounded snapshot. Global observability, the full Auth/Security Failure
  Matrix and its children, exact TypeScript, focused ESLint and diff hygiene
  pass.

### AUDIT-SENTRY-ALTERNATE-ENVELOPE-PRIVACY-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `instrumentation-client.ts`, `sentry.server.config.ts`,
  `sentry.edge.config.ts`; browser/server telemetry → Sentry transaction and
  Replay envelopes.
- **Observed/root cause/privacy impact:** `beforeSend` sanitized ordinary error
  events, but tracing transactions use `beforeSendTransaction`, and Replay
  custom performance/network/navigation frames use a separate recording
  envelope. Consequently sampled span descriptions and Replay URLs could
  bypass the established path/identifier minimizer even while Replay DOM text,
  inputs and media were masked.
- **Fix:** all three runtimes now sanitize tracing transactions explicitly.
  Client Replay explicitly disables network body capture, keeps its network
  detail allowlist empty, and drops every SDK custom recording frame; masked
  DOM recording remains available for sampled errors. This prevents custom
  navigation/resource/request URLs from leaving through Replay without
  disabling the useful masked visual failure trace.
- **Regression/validation:** both observability source gates now pin the
  separate transaction hooks and Replay deny-by-default options. The same full
  validation matrix listed above passes. No Firebase source or infrastructure
  changed, and no deploy applies.

Restart 1071 switched product-boundary-first to the previously inventory-only

### AUDIT-CC-PRODUCTION-SHARED-FIREBASE-001

  `NODE_ENV=production` honored them. A stale or mistaken preview/production

  for MenuList or another accessible project could initialize the named Admin

## Restart 1070 addendum — Image-provider logging privacy

Restart 1070 switched to observability/privacy-first review of the previously
inventory-only image-operation logging helper and all three active image
generation/editing consumers. One P2 active logging defect and one P3 dormant
logging contract were confirmed and closed locally.

### AUDIT-IMAGE-PROVIDER-USAGE-METADATA-LEAK-001

- **Severity/status/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `FLOW-AI-IMAGE-PROVIDER-LOGGING`; authenticated image generation/editing →
  Gemini response → local operational/AI accounting summaries.
- **Observed/root cause/privacy/reliability impact:** the response helper
  returned the provider's complete unknown `usageMetadata` object. Current
  token-count fields were expected, but any present or future provider detail,
  nested arrays or private metadata was persisted to logs without an allowlist.
  It also asserted the external response shape and traversed every candidate
  and part, so hostile accessors or unexpectedly large responses could break or
  amplify failure logging.
- **Fix:** unknown properties are read through contained `Reflect` access;
  candidate/part inspection is capped at 100 by 100; only counts and five
  non-negative safe-integer usage totals are returned:
  `cachedContentTokenCount`, `candidatesTokenCount`, `promptTokenCount`,
  `thoughtsTokenCount` and `totalTokenCount`. Image bytes, text, prompt-token
  detail arrays and all other provider fields are excluded. Active callers keep
  the same summary envelope.
- **Regression:** the pure suite proves valid counts, private/detail exclusion,
  malformed/proxy containment, no conversion hooks and the inspection cap.
  The AI Accounting source aggregate now requires the allowlist and forbids the
  raw metadata projection.

### AUDIT-DORMANT-RAW-IMAGE-CONFIG-LOGGER-001

- **Severity/status/file:** P3 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/ai/imageOperationLogging.ts`.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** two exported helpers had no runtime consumer
  but advertised a “sanitized” generation-config logger that spread every
  non-image field, including raw prompts and future arbitrary owner/provider
  values, while retaining uploaded image names and IDs. Existing verifiers
  explicitly forbid using that helper in accounting and route logs. The
  dormant unsafe API and its image projector were removed, preventing later
  accidental reactivation.

Validation passed the new behavioral suite, the full 3,000-plus-assertion AI
Accounting source verifier, focused ESLint, exact root TypeScript and diff
hygiene. The AI Image Generation spec now records the exact logging allowlist
and inspection cap. No Firebase/Storage rule, index or Function source changed,
so no infrastructure deployment applies. New findings keep
`consecutiveCleanFullPasses` at zero. The new regression file brings the
regenerated scope to 8,382 files plus 310 exclusions: 1,767 reviewed, 1,838
in-progress and 4,777 inventory-only. The reverse catalog remains 282
collection families.

## Restart 1069 addendum — Platform alert recipient and diagnostic boundaries

Restart 1069 switched type-first to the previously inventory-only owner email
and WhatsApp channels, then traced both app and Functions platform-alert
producers into their provider calls. Both channel adapters were completely
reviewed without a new defect. The upstream platform delivery mirrors exposed
one P2 recipient-boundary defect and one P3 diagnostic-boundary defect, both
closed locally.

### AUDIT-PLATFORM-ALERT-EMAIL-RECIPIENT-LIST-001

- **Severity/status/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `FLOW-OPS-PLATFORM-ALERT-DELIVERY`; internal alert classification → configured
  platform recipient → app or Functions SMTP provider → founder operations
  mailbox.
- **Files/producer/consumer:** `src/lib/ops/platformNotificationDelivery.ts`
  and `functions/src/monitoring/platformNotificationDelivery.ts` consume
  `PLATFORM_ALERT_EMAIL_TO` with `INTERNAL_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL` fallback and
  feed the existing generic SMTP adapters. The new byte-identical app/Functions
  contract lives in `src/data/shared/platformNotificationRecipient.ts` and
  `functions/src/sharedData/platformNotificationRecipient.ts`.
- **Observed/root cause/security impact:** the declared configuration contract
  describes one platform mailbox, but the raw environment string was passed to
  Nodemailer. Comma/semicolon recipient lists and provider display-name syntax
  were therefore not rejected at the platform boundary. A configuration error
  could fan tenant/store operational alerts to additional mailboxes, creating a
  confidentiality and alert-routing failure.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** the first configured environment value is
  admitted only when it is one primitive, control-free, delimiter-free,
  syntactically valid mailbox of at most 254 characters. Invalid override
  values fail closed rather than silently falling through to another mailbox.
  Valid existing single addresses are unchanged. The generic owner-notification
  email channel remains reusable for already validated owner recipients.
- **Tests/docs:** the pure parity suite proves valid trimming and rejects
  lists, semicolon lists, display names, header injection, malformed,
  oversized and non-string input without executing conversion hooks. It also
  proves both runtime contracts are byte-identical. Ops delivery and deployment
  docs now state the one-mailbox rule.

### AUDIT-PLATFORM-DELIVERY-DIAGNOSTIC-COERCION-001

- **Severity/status/file:** P3 / Closed locally /
  `functions/src/monitoring/platformNotificationDelivery.ts`; alert/provider
  result → bounded failure diagnostics.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the helper accepted `unknown` but called
  `String(value)`. A malformed runtime value with a conversion hook could throw
  while the code was already reporting a provider failure, hiding the original
  delivery outcome. The helper now admits strings, finite numbers and booleans
  only and otherwise records an absent value.

Founder Growth writer and acquisition contract. It reverse-traced

### AUDIT-FOUNDER-GROWTH-PERSISTED-ATTRIBUTION-001

- **Severity/status/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `FLOW-FOUNDER-GROWTH-ATTRIBUTION`; public create-menu attribution → persisted
  draft → draft/claim lifecycle call → source/stage Founder Growth counters →

  draft marker and `platformSummary/founderMonitorGrowth`; the platform-only
  Founder Monitor consumes the bounded counters. No tenant/store/customer
  identity is stored in the aggregate.

  recorded and permanently increment the wrong source bucket, preventing a

  map are independently normalized and must match in source, medium and
  campaign before any marker or counter changes. Missing, malformed or
  mismatched persisted truth fails closed. Current drafts already persist the

  cache or public DTO change is required.

  best-effort so telemetry cannot block onboarding. The existing one draft read,

  no extra read/write or retained event document was added. Bounded diagnostics
  still exclude attribution and owner identifiers.

  supplies a conflicting public-surface attribution and proves both
  `recorded:false` and absence of a marker. Existing six-way concurrency tests
  still prove exactly one marker/counter effect for matching draft and claim
  events.

### AUDIT-GROWTH-ATTRIBUTION-UNKNOWN-COERCION-001

- **Severity/status/file:** P2 / Closed locally /

  query/form/persisted attribution → fixed acquisition combination.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** `String(unknown)` normalized the three fields.
  Malformed boundary or legacy values could execute conversion hooks or be
  admitted through an object string representation before the allowlist.
  Depending on the caller, a thrown hook could turn optional telemetry or a
  public create/claim request into a generic failure.
- **Fix/regression:** primary and legacy `utm_*` fields now admit primitive
  strings only, with primary-string precedence and the same exact combination
  allowlist. The emulator invokes normalization with a source object whose

## Restart 1067 addendum — Public analytics delivery idempotency

Restart 1067 switched to failure/concurrency-first review of the browser
analytics queue, public tracking route and Admin daily-analytics writer. It
followed a queued snapshot through persistence, cross-tab recovery, HTTP retry,
route validation, transactional increment, client rules and retention. One P1
owner/public-truth defect was confirmed and closed locally.

### AUDIT-PUBLIC-ANALYTICS-DELIVERY-IDEMPOTENCY-001

- **Severity/status/flow:** P1 / Closed locally / `FLOW-ANALYTICS-PUBLIC-TRACK`;
  browser menu event → tenant/store/project/date-scoped local queue → public
  analytics route → Admin daily aggregate → owner analytics and operational
  consumers.
- **Files/functions:** `src/lib/analytics/queueBoundary.ts`
  (`normalizeAnalyticsQueueEntry`), `src/database/analytics/index.ts`
  (`queueEvents`, `flushQueue`),
  `src/app/api/public/analytics/track/route.ts` (`analyticsPayloadSchema`,
  `POST`) and `src/lib/analytics/serverWrite.ts`
  (`writeValidatedDailyAnalytics`).
- **Affected structure/producers/consumers:** persisted browser queue snapshots
  and daily `analytics` documents produced by public-menu clients; consumed by
  analytics aggregation, owner dashboards, settlement and decision-support
  paths. A new Admin-only `analyticsDeliveryReceipts` receipt structure is
  keyed by an opaque hash of canonical scope plus a 32-character delivery ID.
- **Trigger/observed behavior:** after Firestore committed a daily increment,
  any lost HTTP acknowledgement, browser retry, page restoration or
  cross-tab recovery resent the same snapshot. The prior Admin writer used an
  atomic increment but had no delivery receipt, so every retry incremented the
  same event counts again.
- **Expected/root cause:** an exact queued delivery must have at-most-once
  aggregate effect even though transport remains at-least-once. The queue had
  retry metadata but no stable delivery identity, and the server had no
  transactional replay guard.
- **Security/tenant/data/public/cache impact:** the public route still derives
  and validates tenant/store/project ownership independently; the delivery ID
  is not accepted as scope. The defect did not expose another tenant, but it
  could overstate menu views, searches, item views and downstream owner truth.
  No cache stores the mutation response. Replays could distort settlement and
  decision inputs until later correction.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** each new snapshot receives a random lowercase
  alphanumeric 32-character ID; retries preserve it, successful acknowledgement
  rotates it for events merged while a send is in flight, legacy stored
  snapshots receive a deterministic compatible ID, and malformed present IDs
  fail closed. The Admin transaction reads the exact receipt, returns
  `duplicate` without touching the daily document on replay, or atomically
  increments and creates the receipt. Receipts expire after 72 hours through a
  native TTL field override. Firestore rules explicitly deny every client read
  and write. Existing daily documents require no migration.
- **Side effects/error/idempotency/observability:** the daily increment and
  receipt creation share one Firestore transaction, so neither can commit
  alone. Retryable HTTP failures retain the same snapshot identity; nonretryable
  input remains rejected. Receipt payloads contain canonical IDs and expiry,
  not request content or user identity. The existing bounded route/logger error
  behavior remains unchanged.
- **Regression/validation:** the browser suite proves identity persistence,
  legacy normalization, malformed-ID rejection and post-ack rotation. The real
  Admin Firestore emulator proves two distinct concurrent deliveries aggregate
  and an exact delivery replay returns `duplicate` without a second increment.
  The rules emulator proves public, assigned-store and platform clients cannot
  read or write receipts. `npm run verify:analytics-write-boundary`,
  `npm run verify:menulist-api-tenant-safety`, `npm run
  verify:doc-npm-scripts`, exact root TypeScript and `git diff --check` pass.
- **Deployment evidence:** this restart changes `firestore.rules` and
  `firestore.indexes.json`. The smallest required QA deployment,
  `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules,firestore:indexes --project
  menulist-qa --config firebase.json`, exited 1 with `Failed to authenticate,
  have you run firebase login?`. Source, emulator and index-JSON proof is
  complete, but rules and TTL are not remotely deployed or verified from this
  workspace.
- **Closure:** locally closed in re-audit pass 1067. The new finding resets
  `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` to zero.

Coverage regeneration found 8,378 in-scope files and 310 explicit exclusions:
1,757 are reviewed, 1,836 are in-progress and 4,785 remain inventory-only.
The reverse catalog now resolves 282 Firestore collection families, including
the new receipt family. The shared 4,000-line ruleset, index registry, package
manifest, aggregate verifier and long Firebase documentation retain
conservative partial-review status; focused changes do not constitute complete
current-file review.

## Restart 1066 addendum — Analytics business-day settlement truth

Restart 1066 switched to type-first review of the app/Functions business-day
mirrors and followed configured close time through analytics keys, scheduler
cycles, owner dashboard fallback and nightly settlement. One P1 owner-truth
defect and one P2 input-contract defect were confirmed and closed.

### AUDIT-ANALYTICS-WRAPPED-SETTLEMENT-DATE-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/analytics/businessDay.ts` and
  `functions/src/utils/businessDay.ts`; store close time + timezone →
  settlement cutoff → latest settled business date → dashboard reads,
  correction/aggregation and owner action baselines.
- **Observed/root cause/public/data impact:** when close time plus the governed
  150-minute buffer crossed midnight (for example, 23:00 → 01:30), the cycle
  helper already represented the correct settlement date, but the latest-date
  helper subtracted two dates instead of one. Before cutoff it could report
  three calendar dates back; after cutoff it remained one date behind. Late
  closing businesses therefore read stale settled truth and could attach owner
  actions to the wrong baseline.
- **Fix/regression:** latest settled truth is always the business date
  immediately preceding the settlement cycle key; midnight wrap is already
  encoded by the cycle calculation. A shared app/Functions regression pins
  23:00 close at 01:29/01:30 and the normal 03:00 close at 05:29/05:30.

### AUDIT-BUSINESS-DAY-TIME-COERCION-001

- **Severity/status/files/flow:** P2 / Closed locally / the same app/Functions
  mirrors; persisted/onboarding close-time/category input → normalized
  analytics policy.
- **Observed/root cause/data impact:** `String(value)` broadly coerced unknown
  time/business-type values, and an invalid caller-provided fallback could be
  emitted unchanged into persistence/scheduling. The boundary now admits
  primitive strings only, never runs conversion hooks, validates both primary
  and fallback values and returns the governed 03:00 default if both are
  invalid.

Validation passed the new app/Functions parity test, Functions TypeScript
build, Analytics Write aggregate and both of its real Firestore emulators, the
complete Analytics Settlement emulator, focused ESLint, exact root TypeScript,
dependency freeze, documentation script references and diff hygiene.

--project menulist-qa --config firebase.json`—exited 1 with `Failed to
