## Restart 1065 addendum — Transaction replay and external DNS projection

Restart 1065 began datastore-first from unreviewed compact writers and response
projectors. It traced owner action acknowledgements through the Analytics
transaction and public/provider DNS guidance through the Vercel response
normalizer. Two P2 source defects and one P3 verifier-parity defect were
confirmed and closed.

### AUDIT-OWNER-ACTION-RECEIPT-REPLAY-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/analytics/ownerActionReceiptTransaction.ts`; authenticated owner
  action → deterministic receipt ID → Analytics dashboard transaction →
  desktop/mobile acknowledgement and later outcome tracking.
- **Observed/root cause/data impact:** the deterministic receipt ID prevented a
  second map slot but did not provide idempotent replay. A duplicate request
  rebuilt and rewrote `markedDoneAt`, actor, baseline and `modifiedOn`; after
  the source action rolled out of the current plan, the same already-committed
  request returned 409 rather than its receipt. This made acknowledgement-loss
  retries produce a second write or a false failure.
- **Fix/regression:** inside the transaction, an existing exact receipt now
  replays before current-action validation and performs no write; an
  identity-conflicting persisted receipt fails closed. The real Firestore
  emulator removes the action after the initial commit, replays the same
  request, verifies byte-equivalent receipt truth and proves `modifiedOn`
  remains unchanged. Concurrent new receipts still serialize at the 20-row cap.

### AUDIT-VERCEL-DNS-RANK-COERCION-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/domains/vercelDnsRecords.ts`; bounded Vercel provider JSON → ranked
  DNS recommendations → desktop/mobile custom-domain setup instructions.
- **Observed/root cause/public impact:** broad `any` plus `Number(rank)` treated
  malformed empty-string/null-like ranks as zero and could execute an unknown
  conversion hook. A malformed provider row could therefore outrank valid
  guidance and display the wrong A record to an owner.
- **Fix/regression:** provider objects are admitted from `unknown`; rank accepts
  only a finite non-negative number or canonical non-negative integer string.
  Invalid rows cannot outrank valid guidance or execute conversion hooks.
  Apex/subdomain selection, verification records and deduplication remain
  unchanged.

### AUDIT-VERCEL-DNS-RANK-VERIFIER-PARITY-001

- **Severity/status/file:** P3 / Closed locally /
  `scripts/verification/verify-custom-domain-boundary.js`.

## Restart 1064 addendum — Shared request admission and dormant security contracts

Restart 1064 traced declared and streamed request sizes through the shared
bounded-body reader and its MenuList, Answerlattice, SignalDesk, CampaignCue,
billing, screen and public route consumers. It also completed the compact App
Check module and repository-wide consumer traces for two dormant security/rate
contracts. One P2 and three P3 defects were confirmed and closed.

### AUDIT-BOUNDED-REQUEST-CONTENT-LENGTH-GRAMMAR-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/security/boundedRequestBody.ts`; untrusted HTTP headers and body
  stream → shared JSON/text/form-data admission → protected/public route
  validation and side effects.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** `Number(content-length)` admitted exponent,
  signed and fractional syntax even though HTTP content length is a decimal
  digit sequence; it also admitted integers beyond JavaScript's exact range.
  The actual stream remained byte-bounded, so this was not a size-limit bypass,
  but declared-size preflight and its before-rate-limit ordering could behave
  inconsistently for malformed requests. Invalid configured limits were also
  not rejected explicitly.
- **Fix/regression:** the boundary requires digit-only syntax and an exactly
  representable non-negative safe integer, rejects malformed declarations with
  400, retains 413 for valid oversized declarations and throws immediately for
  invalid `maxBytes` configuration. The focused test pins exponent, sign,
  fraction, duplicate-style, unsafe-integer, leading-zero, exact-limit and
  oversized behavior.

### AUDIT-DORMANT-RAW-SECURITY-CONTEXT-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P3 / Closed locally /
  removed `src/lib/security/securityContext.ts`; session/request metadata →
  security diagnostics.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the orphaned exported helper assembled raw
  email, user, tenant, store, forwarded-IP, user-agent, error and attempted
  payload data, directly contradicting the active bounded-diagnostics contract.
  Repository-wide import tracing found no runtime consumer, so removal closes
  the latent PII-log path without changing active logging behavior.

### AUDIT-DORMANT-GENERIC-RATE-TIERS-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P3 / Closed locally /
  removed `src/lib/rateLimit/tiers.ts`; generic subscription label → request
  limit, upgrade suggestion and display price.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** this unused alternate contract embedded
  ungoverned generic plan prices and entitlement limits outside the
  authoritative billing/rate-limit systems. No first-party runtime or verifier
  imported it. Removing it prevents a future consumer from silently selecting
  fabricated billing semantics.

### AUDIT-APP-CHECK-DEBUG-WINDOW-ANY-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P3 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/firebase/appCheck.ts`; development App Check environment value →
  Firebase SDK debug-token bootstrap.
- **Observed/fix:** a broad `window as any` assertion erased the only supported
  debug-token value contract. A narrow `Window` intersection now admits only
  the Firebase SDK's boolean-or-string debug token while preserving the
  development-only and explicit-environment gates.

## Restart 1061 addendum — Unattended screen reload recovery

Restart 1061 followed browser-persisted timing state into the unattended
digital-screen reload path. One P2 defect was confirmed and closed.

### AUDIT-SCREEN-RELOAD-FUTURE-TIMESTAMP-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/screen/utils.ts`; local reload timestamp plus content/offline/timer
  trigger → guarded customer screen reload.
- **Observed/root cause/reliability impact:** the guard parsed arbitrary storage
  text with `parseInt` and suppressed reload whenever `now - stored < 30s`.
  A corrupt or manually future-dated value therefore produced a negative
  duration and could suppress recovery until that future time; prefix strings
  such as a valid timestamp plus junk were also admitted.
- **Fix/regression:** a pure boundary now admits only a canonical positive
  integer timestamp no later than the current safe integer time. Only a real
  reload within the 30-second window suppresses another reload. Future,
  negative and suffix-mutated values fail open to recovery and are replaced
  with the current timestamp. Lifecycle tests pin all cases.
- **Validation:** the full Digital Screens source gate, timestamp and
  seen-scope suites, Firestore rules emulator, focused lint, exact TypeScript
  and diff hygiene pass.

## Restart 1060 addendum — Tenant-partitioned owner selection and deletion boundaries

Restart 1060 traced tenant-switch-sensitive browser state from storage keys
back through the shared desktop/mobile project selector. Two P1 defects were
confirmed and closed.

### AUDIT-OWNER-PROJECT-SELECTION-SCOPE-CANONICALIZATION-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/projects/projectSelection.ts`; session tenant/store identity →
  persisted owner project selection → desktop/mobile selected project.
- **Observed/root cause/tenant impact:** tenant and store scopes were converted
  with broad `String()` and concatenated with `:`. Noncanonical string scopes
  could therefore contain the delimiter and make two different pairs share one
  browser key (for example tenant `1`, store `2:3` versus tenant `1:2`, store
  `3`). Whitespace-mutated aliases also created separate stale partitions.
- **Fix/regression:** both identity dimensions now reuse the canonical positive
  numeric Firestore document-ID boundary; invalid, ambiguous, zero, whitespace
  and delimiter-bearing scopes fail closed and cannot read or write scoped
  browser state. Regression tests prove the collision key is never created.

### AUDIT-DELETED-PROJECT-RESELECTION-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally / same selector; persisted
  preferred project ID plus current project list → owner active project.
- **Observed/root cause/public-truth impact:** after failing to find a preferred
  ID among nondeleted projects, the selector searched the original list and
  could reselect a deleted project. If every project was deleted, its fallback
  also selected one of those deleted records.
- **Fix/regression:** deletion is now an absolute admission boundary. Preferred
  IDs are resolved only within nondeleted projects, and an all-deleted list
  returns `null`. Tests cover both a stale deleted preference beside an active
  project and an all-deleted list.

## Restart 1055 addendum — Date-range termination, translation bounds and multilingual normalization

Restart 1055 switched to public text, analytics range and shared runtime
utility contracts. Two P1, three P2 and one P3 defects were confirmed and
closed; the discovery of defects resets convergence and
`consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains `0`.

### AUDIT-ANALYTICS-DATE-RANGE-VALIDATION-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/analytics/dateKey.ts`; analytics calendar inputs → dashboard query
  ranges, settlement keys, receipts and public event admission.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** date keys were split and passed to `Date`
  without syntax/calendar validation. Invalid keys could normalize to another
  day; worse, `getAnalyticsDateRange()` could repeatedly transform a malformed
  key into `NaN-NaN-NaN` while its lexical loop condition remained true,
  creating a non-terminating server/client loop.
- **Fix/regression:** exact `YYYY-MM-DD` keys must round-trip to a real UTC
  calendar date; offsets must be bounded safe integers; ranges are calculated
  arithmetically, return empty when reversed and reject more than 3,660 days.
  Small runtime tests cover leap-boundary traversal, impossible/malformed
  dates, reversed and oversized ranges and non-finite offsets.

### AUDIT-AL-TRANSLATION-SOURCE-BOUNDARY-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/answerlattice/articleTranslationServer.ts`; persisted editor JSON →
  source fingerprint/provider translation input/draft.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** recursive editor traversal had no cycle, node
  or output bound and read unknown nodes directly. Cyclic or deeply/oversized
  persisted content could overflow the stack or create unbounded provider
  input before the already strict provider-response validator ran.
- **Fix/regression:** source traversal now contains every read/array
  iteration, tracks visited objects, caps nodes at 10,000 and source text at
  12,000 characters, while preserving stable paragraph separation and hashes.
  Multi-language contracts cover cyclic content, a hostile node Proxy,
  oversized text and a hostile article record.

### AUDIT-PUBLIC-HOURS-PROTOTYPE-COLLISION-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/localization/publicHoursText.ts`; persisted hours text → localized
  customer menu/OBP status.
- **Observed/fix:** exact-label lookup used `exactLabels[value]`; a legitimate
  unknown string such as `toString` resolved an inherited object method rather
  than remaining text. Lookup now requires an own label key, and the regression
  proves prototype names remain ordinary public text.

### AUDIT-EXTRACTION-NAME-RUNTIME-ACCESS-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/extraction/normalize.ts`; extracted/legacy localized names → menu
  comparison and matching.
- **Observed/fix:** compile-time `Record<string,string>` assumptions allowed a
  non-string primary/fallback value or hostile localized container to reach

### AUDIT-EXTRACTION-NAME-UNICODE-LOSS-001

### AUDIT-PROJECT-DOCUMENT-EMBEDDED-SCOPE-FAIL-OPEN-001 — Malformed present scope fields were treated as absent

- **Finding/severity/status:** `AUDIT-PROJECT-DOCUMENT-EMBEDDED-SCOPE-FAIL-OPEN-001` / P1 / Closed locally in restart 1053.
- **File/flow:** `src/lib/menu/projectDocumentScope.ts`; session/path tenant-store-project identity + persisted project document → project DAL and project/outlet mutation authorization.
- **Observed/root cause/security impact:** the helper normalized embedded aliases and filtered invalid results before comparison. A present `tId`, `tenantId`, `sId`, `storeId` or `projectId` containing a slash, whitespace, leading zero, null or other invalid value disappeared from the candidate list and the document passed as if it contained no embedded identity. Path reads remained session-scoped, so no direct cross-tenant disclosure was observed, but a security guard explicitly intended to reject contradictory persisted authority failed open and could let corrupted scope metadata continue into downstream project operations.
- **Fix/compatibility:** tenant/store scope accepts only canonical positive safe-integer IDs; project IDs remain trimmed slash-free strings correlated to both scope ends. Every own embedded alias, when present, must normalize and exactly match. Absent legacy fields remain supported; inherited properties are not Firestore document fields; enumeration/getter failures reject.
- **Regression/validation:** focused tests cover valid current/legacy aliases, wrong IDs, invalid/slashed/null/leading-zero values, inherited pollution, throwing accessors and invalid path scope. The complete menu-project-editor boundary and its mutation/upload/time-slot children pass.

### AUDIT-PLATFORM-BLOCK-STATE-INSPECTION-001 — Critical block checks could throw instead of failing closed

- **Finding/severity/status:** `AUDIT-PLATFORM-BLOCK-STATE-INSPECTION-001` / P1 / Closed locally in restart 1053.
- **File/flow:** `src/lib/platform/entityBlock.ts`; persisted user/tenant/store block fields → auth, session, billing, staff, public truth, multi-outlet and mutation eligibility.
- **Observed/root cause/security impact:** broad `any` and direct optional-chain access meant a throwing/malformed object could abort block evaluation across a widely shared authorization primitive. Most server paths would deny through an exception, but public filters could fail as availability errors and the helper had no explicit fail-closed contract.
- **Fix/regression:** top-level `blocked`, `tenantBlocked`, `blockDetails` and nested `blocked` are inspected through contained reads. Any access failure now returns blocked; valid explicit true/false behavior is unchanged. The focused runtime test proves malformed input fails closed, and the platform entity-block verifier was updated to require this safer implementation rather than its former optional-chain tokens.

### AUDIT-AL-SEARCH-HISTORY-TIMESTAMP-COERCION-001 — Retained interaction admission executed unknown values

- **Finding/severity/status:** `AUDIT-AL-SEARCH-HISTORY-TIMESTAMP-COERCION-001` / P2 / Closed locally in restart 1053.

Separately, `getStoreContextName` deliberately called child helpers with an empty fallback, but those helpers forcibly substituted `Business` and `Store`, manufacturing `Business - Store` and preventing the caller's localized fallback from ever being used.

### AUDIT-OBA-ANALYTICS-PERIOD-PRECEDENCE-001 — Generic phrases overrode explicit analytics periods

- **Finding/severity/status:** `AUDIT-OBA-ANALYTICS-PERIOD-PRECEDENCE-001` / P2 / Closed locally in restart 1052.
- **File/flow:** `src/lib/ownerBusinessAssistant/server/analyticsPeriodResolver.ts`; owner question → compact analytics period → assistant facts/answer.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** `today` matched the generic phrase `so far` before specific entries, so “this month so far” returned today's data. Synonyms were also checked before unsupported custom-date detection, so a question containing both “last month” and “from June 1 to June 5” silently returned all of last month instead of refusing the unsupported range.
- **Expected/root cause/impact:** explicit custom dates must fail closed, explicit named periods must beat generic language, and “so far” alone may retain the established today fallback. The resolver now checks custom dates first, resolves named periods next, then treats a remaining `so far` as today. This changes no analytics documents, cache identity, tenant scope or provider behavior.
- **Regression/validation:** the existing hardening verifier now pins named-period-over-generic and custom-date-over-synonym cases in addition to its normal last-month and custom-range coverage. The full Owner Business Assistant aggregate, exact TypeScript, lint and diff hygiene pass.

### AUDIT-DORMANT-STYLE-UTILITY-COERCION-001 — Exported CSS helpers used broad executable coercion

- **Finding/severity/status:** `AUDIT-DORMANT-STYLE-UTILITY-COERCION-001` / P3 / Closed locally in restart 1052.
- **File/flow:** `src/utils/getColorsValue.ts`; legacy exported gradient/dimension helpers. Repository-wide search found no active first-party runtime consumer.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** broad `any` values were interpolated, mapped and passed to `.includes`/`.split`; a finite numeric style value threw and arbitrary objects could execute conversion hooks. This was a dormant concrete failure path, not a current owner/public surface regression.
- **Fix/regression:** gradient configuration and return values are exact types; only nonblank string colors/type/direction are serialized. CSS dimensions accept finite numbers or an exact numeric `%`/`px` string and otherwise return the established zero-pixel fallback without coercion. Focused tests cover normal gradient, number, percentage and a throwing conversion object.

### AUDIT-PRINT-CANVAS-RESOURCE-BOUNDS-001

  `src/lib/menu-kit/platformAttribution.ts`; persisted/public labels and brand
  presentation → QR, Menu Kit, printable assets and physical surfaces.
- **Observed/root cause/reliability impact:** text fitting decremented an
  unchecked font size two points at a time and truncation removed one character

  monopolize the browser; non-finite widths/logo heights also propagated into

  unchanged.

  one-million-character label stay within bounded measurement counts and
  non-finite logo geometry normalizes deterministically. Menu Card Export,
  exact TypeScript, scoped ESLint and dependency freeze pass.

## Restart 1159 addendum — Share payloads, public print assets and menu-link SSRF

Restart 1159 moved from browser-local public report serialization through the
public print/share renderers and then into the server-side menu-link network

### AUDIT-MENU-LINK-IPV6-LINK-LOCAL-SSRF-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P0 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/menu-link-import/sourceAcquisition.ts`; authenticated owner or
  signed-in public-create-menu URL input → URL/DNS/IP admission → pinned HTTP
  request or isolated renderer → private extraction artifact.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** both protected menu-link routes send
  owner-controlled URLs to the shared acquisition helper. Its IPv6 guard
  rejected only strings beginning `fe80:` even though link-local space is the
  complete `fe80::/10` range. Literal targets such as `fe90::1`, `fea0::1` and
  `febf::1` therefore passed pre-fetch admission and could reach the pinned
  network client.
- **Expected/root cause/security impact:** no loopback, private, link-local,
  site-local, multicast or metadata-class endpoint may be fetched. The helper
  now parses the first IPv6 hextet and applies the correct `fe80::/10` mask;
  deprecated non-public `fec0::/10` site-local space is also rejected. DNS
  rebinding protection, redirect revalidation, credential/protocol rejection,
  byte/time limits and Chrome hostname pinning remain unchanged.
- **Regression/validation:** a focused executable suite proves representative
  `fe80`, `fe90`, `fea0`, `febf` and `fec0` literals fail with `UNSAFE_IP`
  before any request. The test, scoped ESLint and exact TypeScript pass. The
  test is registered in the Menu Extraction aggregate.

The complete shareable-report module produced no new finding: encoded and
decoded payload sizes, check/boundary/job cardinality, canonical timestamp and
display strings, exact visible-row summary reconciliation, derived setup
jobs, required report limits, base64/JSON failure containment and same-origin
next actions are enforced before rendering. The complete print/share types,
registry, report builder and SVG renderer also produced no new finding:
owner-entered URLs and phone values are admitted before QR/action projection,
SVG copy is escaped, dimensions are fixed and rendering is browser-local.

no infrastructure deployment applies.

### AUDIT-FORMATTER-NONFINITE-FINANCIAL-TRUTH-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/utils/formatters.ts`; persisted/calculated monetary or duration scalar
  → shared localized formatter → owner/platform/mobile display.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** `formatInrPaise(Number.NaN)` used
  `(paise || 0)` and therefore displayed malformed financial state as a real
  zero amount. Other currency/INR/duration functions admitted `NaN`,
  infinities, or an invalid currency code, producing misleading `NaN`/infinity
  labels or throwing during render. Missing and malformed values must never be

  read models produce the scalars; desktop/mobile financial summaries consume
  them. A malformed legacy/API value, failed arithmetic, overflow, or invalid
  currency code triggered the issue. Tenant scope, persistence, billing

  incorrect or failed owner/operator presentation.

  processing-time formatters reject non-finite numbers; currency construction
  is contained and returns the established missing-value marker for invalid
  codes. Valid finite values, including zero and negative adjustments, retain
  their previous formatting. The existing deliberate undefined-paise fallback
  remains zero for aggregate displays.

## Restart 1247 addendum — Shared date and timezone conversion boundary

Restart 1247 reverse-traced the shared date utility from owner scheduling,
special-menu, temporary-status, billing/transaction, CampaignCue, and public
display consumers back through Firestore/API timestamp conversion and
timezone-local form serialization. One P2 defect was confirmed and closed;
`consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains `0`.

### AUDIT-DATETIME-HOSTILE-TIMESTAMP-DST-GAP-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/utils/dateTime/index.tsx` (`toDate`,
  `fromNativeDateInputValue`, `fromNativeDateTimeInputValue`);
  Firestore/API/date-form input → normalized instant → owner mutation or
  localized display.
- **Affected structure/producer/consumer/trigger:** `DateLike`, serialized
  Firestore timestamps, method-bearing timestamp compatibility values, and
  native `datetime-local` strings produced by owner forms and consumed by
  scheduling/public-state writers and date presentation helpers. A hostile
  accessor/proxy, a `toDate()` result that was not a valid `Date`, malformed
  seconds/nanoseconds, or a timezone-local wall time inside a daylight-saving
  gap triggered the defect.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** the normalizer read `toDate` and serialized
  fields through unchecked property access and returned the method result
  without validating it. Formatting could therefore execute hostile accessors
  or throw on a non-Date. The timezone converter also accepted syntactically
  valid but nonexistent wall times and silently shifted them to a different
  local time. Timestamp conversion must be total and a local form value must
  round-trip to the same local date/time before it is persisted.
- **Security/tenant/data/public/cache impact:** no tenant identity, cache key,
  or authorization changed. Malformed persisted/client state could crash
  owner/public presentation, while a DST-gap schedule could persist the wrong
  publication/status instant.
- **Fix/backward compatibility/files changed:** date conversion now inspects
  only data descriptors, bounds prototype lookup, contains proxy/method
  failures, validates returned `Date` objects, and requires finite seconds plus
  integer nanoseconds in Firestore range. Native date/date-time conversion now
  verifies the computed instant maps back to the exact requested wall time.
  Valid current `Date`, Firebase `Timestamp`, admin-style prototype method,
  ISO/epoch, and serialized timestamp inputs remain supported.
- **Regression/validation/closure:** the localization behavior suite proves
  epoch-zero and serialized timestamps, rejects out-of-range nanoseconds and
  non-Date method results, proves accessor and Proxy traps cannot escape or
  execute, and rejects the `2026-03-08 02:30` New York DST gap. The complete
  Global Localization aggregate and exact TypeScript pass. An initially
  attempted `test:global-localization-boundary` package-script alias exited nonzero because
  no such package script exists; the repository-authoritative command is
  `npm run verify:global-localization-boundary`, which ran the focused test and
  all registered localization checks successfully.

No Firestore rule/index, Storage rule or Firebase Function source changed, so
no infrastructure deployment applies.

## Restart 1245 addendum — Asset Factory and SecurityOS planning boundaries

Restart 1245 traced the internal Website Asset Operating System from slot and
manifest declarations through source hashing, brief generation, output
admission, approval review, and public-file ownership checks. It also reviewed
the read-only SecurityOS evidence-plan selector from its schema-validated
registry through product and bundle filtering to terminal output. One P2
repository-integrity defect was confirmed and closed;
`consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains `0`.

### AUDIT-ASSET-FACTORY-PATH-CONTAINMENT-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `packages/asset-factory/scripts/lib/asset-runtime.ts`
  (`fromRepoPath`, `getAssetBriefPath`) and
  `packages/asset-factory/scripts/generate-brief.ts` (`buildBrief`,
  `writeBrief`); Asset slot/manifest declaration → internal brief generation
  → repository filesystem.
- **Affected structure/producer/consumer/trigger:** a manifest
  `AssetManifestEntry.brief` or repository-relative Asset Factory path produced
  by tracked internal configuration and consumed by Asset Factory readers and
  writers; a malformed `../`/absolute path or a brief path that did not match
  its slot triggered the defect.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** `fromRepoPath` used `path.join` without
  proving repository containment, and brief generation trusted the manifest
  output path. A malformed tracked entry could read outside the repository or
  make `assets:brief` overwrite unrelated runtime source. All Asset Factory
  paths must remain in the repository, and generated briefs must be written
  only to the exact governed `packages/asset-factory/briefs/{slot}.md` path.
- **Security/tenant/data/public/cache impact:** no tenant, Firebase, billing,
  cache, or public-runtime authority was involved. The defect was confined to
  a developer-run internal generator, but it could corrupt first-party source
  or consume unintended local files before review.
- **Fix/backward compatibility/files changed:** repository paths are resolved
  and rejected when outside `REPO_ROOT`; slot IDs must be path-safe; a
  manifest brief path, when present, must exactly match its slot-derived
  destination. All current slots and manifest entries already follow that
  contract, so no supported output path changed.
- **Regression/validation/closure:** the new
  `scripts/verification/test-asset-factory-runtime-boundary.ts` rejects parent
  traversal, absolute external paths, runtime-source brief redirection, and
  traversal-bearing slot IDs while accepting the current governed path. It is
  registered in `npm run verify:asset-factory`. The complete aggregate passes:
  focused boundary test, Asset audit with 0 errors/0 warnings, and Asset review
  with 0 blocked/founder-review/warning items. Thirteen source fingerprints
  were relocked individually only after their current source changes and six
  representative outputs were inspected; no binary was regenerated.

The SecurityOS planner remains read-only: evidence JSON is schema-validated,
unknown products/bundles and cross-product selection fail closed, every
referenced evidence ID must exist, and the CLI only prints commands and
execution/network policy. No evidence command is executed by the planner.
No Firestore rule/index, Storage rule or Firebase Function source changed, so
no infrastructure deployment applies.

### AUDIT-STORES-SUMMARY-BACKFILL-MERGE-RACE-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `functions/src/triggers/operations.ts`
  (`replaceStoresSummaryIfUnchanged`, `backfillStoresSummary`); current
  platform authority → bounded canonical store scan → complete summary
  projection → `platformSummary/storesSummary` → analytics, scheduling,
  retention, billing and owner location consumers.
- **Observed behavior:** the backfill built a complete replacement `stores`
  map but persisted it through `set(..., { merge: true })`. Firestore recursively
  merged that nested map, so a store absent from the canonical scan could
  survive as a stale summary key. Simply switching to an exact field
  replacement would also have allowed a concurrent onboarding, billing or
  scheduler summary mutation to be overwritten after the initial scan.
- **Expected/root cause/data/public/cache impact:** a full backfill must remove
  orphaned summary entries and must not erase a newer legitimate mutation.
  The prior write mode treated replacement data as a patch and had no
  optimistic fence. Stale rows could continue driving cross-store scheduled
  work, analytics/retention scans and owner location summaries. The collection
  is platform-private; no direct public DTO or cache write occurs here.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** the callable captures the summary document
  update time before scanning canonical stores. A final transaction re-reads
  that exact document, aborts if its version/existence changed, and replaces
  the complete `stores` field while preserving unrelated top-level metadata.
  Concurrent summary writers conflict or change the version and require an
  explicit safe retry. Existing bounded store count, payload-size check,
  identity validation, projection defaults and current platform authority
  remain unchanged.
- **Regression/validation/deployment:** the real Firestore emulator starts
  with an orphaned store key, proves exact removal and top-level metadata
  preservation, preserves same-tenant billing/enrichment fields, rejects
  foreign-tenant derived fields, then inserts a concurrent summary mutation and
  proves the stale replacement aborts. Functions build, MenuList tenant-safety,
  exact root TypeScript, root lint, dependency freeze, documentation links,
  focused ESLint and `git diff --check` pass. `npm run build` also passes and
  retains the repository's existing Sass `@import` deprecation warnings plus
  bounded build-time Firebase project-mismatch/key-availability diagnostics.
  The required narrow MenuList QA deployment covers
  `functions:backfillStoresSummary`; Firebase CLI authentication is unavailable,
  so the attempt stopped before upload and no remote revision changed. Closure
  was confirmed locally in restart 1171.

### AUDIT-MENU-KIT-GENERATED-TEXT-OVERFLOW-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/menu-kit/canvasPrimitives.ts`,
  `src/lib/menu-kit/templates/deliveryBagTemplate.ts`,
  `takeawayCardTemplate.ts` and `googleMapsTemplate.ts`; canonical store name,
  short public link and Menu Kit branding → browser Canvas/QR rendering →
  owner-downloaded public PNG.
- **Observed/root cause:** Delivery Bag and Takeaway Card shortened a measured
  label and only then appended an unmeasured ellipsis, so the final text could
  still overflow. Google Maps split only on spaces, drew an overlong single
  word outside its right column, silently discarded every line after the
  third, and drew an unbounded short link.
- **Expected/data/public impact:** generated public identity must remain inside
  the declared print/social layout for valid but long business names and
  links. The defect did not mutate authoritative store/menu data, but it could
  create clipped or misleading owner-distributed artifacts.
- **Fix/compatibility:** the existing bounded text primitive now provides
  measured whitespace normalization, finite width/line admission, hard-word
  truncation and an ellipsized final line. All three affected templates use
  the shared measured helpers for store names and links. Ordinary current
  names retain identical text; long values now degrade visibly and within the
  assigned region.
- **Regression/validation:** the pure canvas suite proves three-line overflow,
  a hostile unbroken word and invalid line limits. The aggregate source gate
  locks each renderer to the shared helper. Menu Card Export and all child
  print suites, exact TypeScript and scoped ESLint pass.

### AUDIT-MENU-KIT-CANONICAL-QR-HANDOFF-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/menu-kit/menuKitGenerator.ts`; caller-supplied public menu URL →
  HTTPS/credential validation and canonicalization → per-surface UTM
  projection → every generated QR code.
- **Observed/root cause:** `prepareMenuKitInput()` computed the canonical
  validated URL but returned a prepared object containing the original
  request string. A whitespace-padded URL therefore passed HTTPS validation
  while every printable/social QR encoded the padded value. The boundary
  proved one value and consumed another.
- **Expected/public/cache/security impact:** QR artifacts must encode the exact
  canonical HTTPS value that passed validation. The defect could produce
  non-opening or scanner-dependent public artifacts; it did not change the
  destination host, persisted menu truth, tenant scope or caches.
- **Fix/regression:** prepared input now overwrites `menuUrl` with
  `validatedUrl` before UTM projection or template execution. The URL suite
  already proves whitespace normalization and rejects HTTP, credentials,
  JavaScript and network-path input; both aggregate source gates now lock the
  canonical handoff. Existing canonical URLs are byte-equivalent.

The remaining four renderers in this batch already use shared truncation or
static bounded copy, scan-safe four-module QR margins, neutral QR panels,
bounded logo geometry and plan-governed MenuList attribution. No Firestore,
Storage, cache, provider, Function, rule/index or deployment behavior changed.

### AUDIT-GLOBAL-ERROR-DIGEST-ACCESSOR-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/app/global-error.tsx`; thrown root error → global error boundary effect
  → bounded runtime failure diagnostic → owner/customer recovery UI.
- **Affected structure/producer/consumer/trigger:** Next.js supplies an
  `Error` with an optional digest. The boundary directly evaluated
  `error?.digest` twice before delegating to the bounded logger. An Error-like
  object with a throwing digest getter, descriptor trap or malformed Proxy
  could therefore throw while the application was already rendering its
  last-resort fallback.
- **Observed/root cause:** the diagnostic-report button correctly used the
  descriptor-safe bounded-field helper, but the root boundary independently
  trusted property access. This created divergent admission for the same
  digest and could replace a recoverable application failure with a broken
  global error screen.
- **Expected/impact:** the last-resort fallback must not invoke unknown error
  accessors. Digest presence and bounded metadata must derive from one
  contained descriptor-safe read. No raw error text is rendered, and no
  persistence, tenant, cache, billing or public-business truth is involved.
- **Fix/regression/validation:** the effect now reads the digest once through
  `getBoundedErrorStringField()` and uses only that admitted value. Both the
  focused global-failure verifier and the broader auth/security matrix reject
  direct optional digest access. Their behavior children, exact TypeScript
  and scoped ESLint pass.

### AUDIT-BUSINESS-COPY-PROJECT-CONTEXT-TENANT-CACHE-001

- **Affected structure/producer/consumer/trigger:** the browser-global cache
  stored project ID/name/description plus up to 12 categories and 24 items.
  Its key contained store ID and project selectors but omitted tenant ID.
  Two tenants with the same numeric store ID and selectors could therefore
  reuse the first tenant's context for 60 seconds after a tenant switch.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** scope-aware UI settlement prevented stale
  output from updating the wrong component, but it ran after the shared cache
  had already supplied menu context and did not make the cache tenant-safe.
  The cached values could enter a provider-bound request for the second
  tenant. Every cache and read must bind the exact tenant/store pair before
  private menu context is read, retained or transmitted.
- **Fix/legacy/security impact:** a pure boundary now requires exact positive
  canonical tenant and store IDs, rejects malformed/missing scope, and builds
  the key from tenant, store and bounded selectors. Both summary and detail
  reads receive that immutable expected scope and fail if the active session
  changed. No persisted schema or migration is needed; old state was
  browser-memory-only and disappears on reload.
- **Regression/validation:** the focused behavior test proves same-store IDs
  across different tenants generate different keys and malformed/missing
  scope fails closed. The auth/security source gate locks tenant keying,
  expected-scope reads and removal of store-only caching. Exact TypeScript,

### AUDIT-AUTH-LOGOUT-SESSION-CACHE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P0 / Closed locally /

  downstream rules usually deny it.

  the raw session cache first and increments a generation. Request creators
  and joiners reject settlement when their generation or exact promise
  ownership changed; cleanup is exact-request-owned. Valid current-session
  cache hits and route/product/store projection remain unchanged.

## Restart 1183 addendum — monotonic public screen revalidation

Restart 1183 continued cache/publication-first review from browser public-truth
mutations through the per-store in-flight revalidation helper and authenticated
menu revalidation route. One P1 publication freshness defect was confirmed and
closed; `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains `0`.

### AUDIT-PUBLIC-CLIENT-CACHE-SCREEN-MERGE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/cache/publicClientCache.ts`
  (`revalidatePublicClientCache`, `mergePendingPublicCacheRevalidation`);
  overlapping owner public-truth mutations → one per-store browser revalidation
  slot → `/api/revalidate/menu` → public tags and optional Digital Screen
  content-version touch.
- **Observed/root cause:** while one store revalidation was in flight, every
  later call overwrote the single queued context/options record. A
  project-publication call could queue `touchScreen: true`, then a later
  cache-only store call could replace it with `touchScreen: false` before the
  trailing iteration. The public route tags were still refreshed, but the
  required store-level Digital Screen content-version touch was lost.
- **Expected/data/public/cache impact:** same-store route-cache work may
  coalesce because its tags and screen version are store-scoped, but queued
  side effects must merge monotonically. Once any trailing mutation requires a
  screen touch, later weaker requests cannot erase it. Otherwise a successful
  owner mutation can leave a live Digital Screen stale until another qualifying
  write or refresh.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** the pending request merge now retains an
  already queued screen-refresh request when a later cache-only request arrives,
  upgrades cache-only work when a later screen request arrives, and still
  coalesces equally strong requests to the latest bounded context. The existing
  per-store request count, timeout, route tags, authentication, rate limit and
  server screen-touch implementation are unchanged.
- **Regression/validation:** `npm run
  test:public-client-cache-revalidation-merge` covers both request orders,
  equal-strength coalescing and cache-only coalescing. Pricing Integrity and
  Public Business Truth source gates require the monotonic merge. Exact
  TypeScript, focused ESLint and diff hygiene pass. No Firestore rules, indexes,
  Storage rules, Cloud Functions, provider calls, Firebase deployment or
  Vercel deployment changed.

## Restart 1184 addendum — Answerlattice trailing publication invalidation

Restart 1184 restarted cache/publication review from Answerlattice owner KB,
FAQ and predictive mutations through the shared browser invalidation helper and

closed; `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains `0`.

### AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-PUBLIC-CACHE-INFLIGHT-WRITE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/cache/answerlatticePublicClientCache.ts`; committed workspace
  mutation → browser public-cache invalidation → `/api/revalidate/answerlattice`
  → KB/FAQ/context/predictive public consumers.
- **Observed/root cause:** the helper mapped each exact workspace,
  segment-set and failure mode directly to one promise. A second mutation that
  committed while the first HTTP invalidation remained in flight returned that
  promise without requesting a trailing revalidation. When the server had
  already observed the first mutation, the second committed truth could remain
  stale until the 60-second recovery TTL or another write.
- **Expected/security/data/public/cache impact:** same-scope callers may share
  active network work, but every mutation that joins it must guarantee one
  trailing invalidation after that mutation committed. Tenant/store and segment
  keys were already separated and remain unchanged; the defect affected
  same-workspace publication freshness rather than cross-tenant disclosure.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** each key now owns a request entry with a
  rerun marker and latest bounded context. The runner performs trailing work
  until no mutation joined the active attempt, and cleanup deletes only its
  exact entry. Best-effort calls retain nonthrowing behavior. Strict calls
  retain the first failure for their final rejection while still attempting
  any already queued trailing invalidation.
- **Regression/validation:** the predictive cache behavior suite holds the
  first fetch open, joins a second committed mutation, and requires exactly one
  shared active request plus one trailing request. It also retains bad-status
  best-effort, strict rejection and strict-success coverage. The Answerlattice
  runtime source gate requires the rerun and exact-owned cleanup contracts;
  exact TypeScript, focused ESLint and diff hygiene pass. This changes no
  Firestore operation, rule, index, Storage rule, Cloud Function, Firebase
  deployment or Vercel deployment.

## Restart 1195 addendum — public plan-type scalar boundary

Restart 1195 reversed the repaired plan mirror into the public menu/OBP client
DTO and attribution policy. One P1 public-output defect was confirmed and

### AUDIT-PUBLIC-CLIENT-PLAN-TYPE-SCALAR-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/publicTruth/clientStoreProjection.ts` and
  `src/lib/platform/menuListBranding.ts`; persisted
  `stores.activePlanType` → server public-store projection → React client props
  → menu/OBP attribution and downloadable public surfaces.
- **Affected structure/producer/consumer/trigger:** billing and reseller
  entitlement synchronization produce the denormalized plan string. Public
  menu, OBP, feedback, PWA/export and attribution consumers use the projected
  store DTO. The trigger was malformed legacy/corrupt plan state represented
  as a map, array, non-string scalar or oversized string.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** `projectPublicClientStore()` allowlisted the
  field name but copied its value verbatim through `Record<string, any>`. A
  supposedly scalar plan map could therefore cross the public server/client
  boundary with arbitrary nested values; nonserializable/malformed state could
  also destabilize rendering. Public allowlists must validate each sensitive
  scalar, not only its key.
- **Security/tenant/data/public/cache impact:** tenant/store identity was still
  exact and unrelated top-level private fields remained excluded, but
  unexpected nested data under `activePlanType` could be disclosed publicly.
  Malformed strings could also produce incorrect attribution truth. No write,
  cache key or cross-tenant lookup changed.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** the public DTO removes `activePlanType` from
  the generic picker and adds it only after the shared normalizer proves a
  nonempty string of at most 160 characters, trimming/lowercasing it. The
  attribution policy uses the same bound. Valid plan IDs retain their existing
  semantics; invalid state fails safe with MenuList attribution visible.
- **Regression/validation:** the public projection suite proves valid Premium
  normalization plus object/161-character omission. Public Customer Delivery,
  the full Public Business Truth aggregate, exact TypeScript, focused ESLint
  and diff hygiene pass. This is a read/projection-only repair; no Firebase
  infrastructure or deployment applies.

### AUDIT-PUBLIC-CLIENT-STORE-VALUE-PROJECTION-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /

  descriptor-safe plain-record boundary and independently projects bounded
  strings, booleans, finite numbers, string arrays/maps, localized text,
  analytics, PWA state, public presence and exact custom-attribute fields.

  values retain the same DTO shape; invalid individual fields are omitted.

### AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-PUBLIC-CITATION-IPV6-LOCAL-RANGE-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/answerlattice/publicAnswerContracts.ts` and
  `functions-answerlattice/src/answerlattice/publicCitationBoundary.ts`;
  governed citation → runtime/history/trace or compiled public context bundle
  → customer/owner clickable link.
- **Affected structure/producer/consumer/trigger:** canonical answers,
  retrieval results and repaired compiled bundles use the same public
  `{ id, title, url }` citation contract. A literal IPv6 URL in `fe90::/16`,
  `fea0::/16` or `feb0::/16` triggered the gap.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** both projectors intended to reject
  link-local destinations but checked only the textual `fe80:` prefix. The
  actual link-local range is `fe80::/10`, so three additional high-prefix
  bands passed as public citation URLs. Deprecated `fec0::/10` site-local
  destinations were also admitted. Public citations must not direct an owner
  or customer into local/private network address space.
- **Security/tenant/data/public/cache impact:** this was not an automatic
  server fetch or cross-tenant read. It could expose a clickable local-network
  target through public/customer answers, owner traces, exports or a compiled
  bundle. Persistence and cache identities were unchanged.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** both dependency-separated boundaries parse
  the first IPv6 hextet and apply exact masks for unique-local,
  `fe80::/10`, `fec0::/10` and multicast destinations while retaining the
  existing mapped-IPv4, documentation, credential and sensitive-query checks.
  Ordinary public DNS names and globally routable URLs retain behavior.
- **Regression/validation:** app and Functions suites cover `fe80`, `fe90`,
  `fea0`, `febf`, `fec0` and `feff` representatives. Retrieval contracts,
  context-bundle boundaries, the Answerlattice runtime verifier, Founder
  Support Controls, real Answer Trace emulator, dedicated Functions build,
  exact TypeScript, focused ESLint and diff hygiene pass. The final manifest
  regeneration contains 8,491 files (2,159 reviewed, 1,845 in progress, 4,487
  inventory-only) and the 282-family collection catalog/audit tooling pass.

  `env -u GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS firebase deploy --project answerlattice-qa --config firebase-answerlattice.json --only functions:answerlatticeNightly,functions:triggerAnswerlatticeNightly --non-interactive`

### AUDIT-LEGACY-MENU-PDF-OPTIONAL-QR-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/export/menuPdfGenerator.ts`; legacy desktop/mobile/printable-asset
  input → compatibility project/store → auto print design → canonical print
  source → QR/PDF renderer → browser download.
- **Affected structure/trigger:** `MenuPdfOptions.menuUrl` is optional, while
  `showQrCode` is optional and auto design may default `includeQr` to true.
  Omitted, malformed, credential-bearing, relative or non-web URLs triggered
  the mismatch.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** the bridge forwarded an empty destination
  but retained auto-design QR inclusion, causing the canonical renderer to
  reject the entire otherwise-renderable PDF. An optional URL must omit QR
  when it cannot pass the renderer's established destination boundary.
- **Security/tenant/data/public/cache impact:** tenant scope and persistence
  were not involved. The defect caused owner export failure, not unsafe QR
  encoding, because the downstream renderer already failed closed. No cache
  was read or mutated.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** exported
  `resolveLegacyMenuPdfIncludeQr()` now requires a valid normalized
  credential-free HTTP(S) URL before applying explicit owner choice or the
  auto-design default. Valid existing HTTP(S) local/production destinations
  retain current behavior; invalid/absent destinations produce a PDF without
  QR.
- **Regression/validation:** focused cases cover explicit/default true/false
  plus absent, empty, relative, JavaScript, credential-bearing and non-scalar
  inputs. Menu Card Export and its QR/print/shared suites, exact TypeScript,
  focused ESLint and diff hygiene pass.

  Portuguese aliases and precedence, malformed values, the complete seven-key

## Restart 1219 addendum — Menu Card PDF resource and pagination boundaries

Restart 1219 continued reverse public-output review through the complete
`renderPdf.ts` pipeline: source/hash/settings, logo and QR acquisition, style
selection, page/column placement, item measurement/drawing, footer metadata,
blob production, controller, print-shop packet and legacy compatibility
consumers. Two P2 defects were confirmed and closed;
`consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains `0`.

### AUDIT-MENU-CARD-PDF-LOGO-RESOURCE-BOUNDARY-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/menu-card-export/source/buildPrintSource.ts` and
  `src/lib/menu-card-export/render/renderPdf.ts`; persisted store logo fields
  → print-source projection → browser `Image` → canvas PNG → PDF header and
  route-session raster cache.
- **Affected structure/producer/consumer/trigger:** store/OBP logo metadata
  produced `MenuCardPrintSource.business.logoUrl`; desktop, mobile,
  print-shop and legacy PDF callers consumed it. A malformed/credentialed URL,
  very large decoded raster, or many distinct valid logos triggered the
  defect.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** the renderer assigned the raw value to
  `Image`, trusted decoded dimensions before canvas allocation, and retained
  every successful PNG data URL in an unbounded map. Logo rendering must be
  optional and bounded without aborting the artifact.
- **Security/tenant/data/public/cache impact:** no tenant authority or
  persistence changed and no private field was emitted. Malformed legacy
  metadata could cause browser resource exhaustion; successful raster cache
  growth persisted for the route lifetime.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** source projection and final rendering now
  require a credential-free HTTP(S) URL capped at 4,096 characters. Canvas
  allocation requires positive integer dimensions no greater than 2,048 and
  4,194,304 total pixels. Successful raster cache entries are capped at 16
  with oldest-first eviction. Valid remote and local-emulator HTTP(S) logos
  retain current behavior; rejected logos fall back to the business initial.
- **Regression/validation:** shared contract tests cover URL protocols,
  credentials, coercion, length and raster limits; the source gate pins URL,
  dimension and cache admission. `npm run verify:menu-card-export`, focused
  ESLint and exact TypeScript pass. Closure confirmed in restart 1219.

### AUDIT-MENU-CARD-PDF-PAGINATION-TEXT-BOUNDARY-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/lib/menu-card-export/source/sanitizeMenuForPrint.ts` and
  `src/lib/menu-card-export/render/renderPdf.ts`; persisted localized menu
  text → print projection → jsPDF wrapping/height estimation → page placement
  → visible PDF.
- **Affected structure/producer/consumer/trigger:** category/item/attribute/tag
  documents produced print rows. Oversized legacy text or an item with more
  than the drawn description/attribute rows triggered disproportionate
  wrapping or estimator/render divergence.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** localized strings were not length-bounded
  before jsPDF wrapping. `itemHeight()` counted every description line and
  eight sanitized attributes while `drawItem()` emitted at most two/four
  description lines and six attributes, creating false page/column breaks.
- **Security/tenant/data/public/cache impact:** no tenant, persistence, cache
  or private-field boundary changed. Owner/customer PDFs could paginate
  incorrectly and malformed legacy content could consume disproportionate
  browser CPU/memory.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** scalar IDs, category/item names,
  descriptions, attributes and tags now have explicit print limits before
  unsupported-character filtering or wrapping. Height estimation uses the
  exact drawing caps. Normal current menu content is unchanged; excessive
  legacy text is deterministically truncated only for the print artifact.
- **Regression/validation:** the sanitizer suite proves every length cap and
  the Menu Card Export source gate requires estimator/drawer parity.
  `npm run test:menu-card-print-sanitizer-boundary`,
  `npm run verify:menu-card-export`, focused ESLint and exact TypeScript pass.

## Restart 1168 addendum — manual analytics current platform authority

Restart 1168 continued the parent `analytics` reverse trace through the complete
customer analytics aggregation producer, including its previously pending AI
payload builders and manual callable. One P0 defect was confirmed and closed
locally; `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains `0`.

### AUDIT-MANUAL-ANALYTICS-STALE-PLATFORM-AUTHORITY-001

- **Severity/status/file/function/flow:** P0 / Closed locally /
  `functions/src/aggregateCustomerAnalytics.ts`
  (`assertCurrentPlatformAnalyticsAuthority`,
  `triggerCustomerAnalyticsManually`); authenticated callable → platform
  authorization → store-summary target proof → daily/summary/weekly/monthly
  analytics reads, writes and cleanup.
- **Affected structure/producer/consumer/trigger:** a platform operator invokes
  the deployed manual aggregation callable with tenant/store/project input.
  The callable performs Admin SDK analytics settlement and deletion work whose
  results feed owner dashboards, Business Health and Menu Intelligence. The
  trigger was a still-valid Firebase token after the persisted platform user
  had been demoted, blocked, disabled, deleted, unverified or removed.
- **Observed behavior:** authorization checked only the signed
  `platformRole`/`role` custom claim. It did not re-read the exact current user
  before accepting an arbitrary valid store target. A stale platform claim
  therefore retained privileged Admin aggregation and cleanup authority until
  token expiry/refresh.
- **Expected/root cause:** a high-authority callable must require both the
  signed platform claim and current persisted user authority/lifecycle state
  before any target read or write. The callable predated the repository's
  current-authority pattern and relied on the claim alone.
- **Security/tenant/data/public/cache impact:** this was an authorization
  bypass across tenant targets. It could mutate owner-visible analytics
  summaries/rollups or delete expired daily analytics for another tenant.
  Public menu rendering and public cache keys were not directly changed, but
  downstream private owner truth and intelligence could be affected.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** the callable now normalizes the exact
  authenticated UID, reads `users/{uid}`, and requires both token and current
  role to be `PLATFORM` while rejecting inactive, deleted, auth-disabled,
  blocked or unverified rows. This happens before request target processing,
  store-summary reads or analytics effects. Active current platform owners keep
  existing behavior at one additional security read per manual invocation.
- **Regression:** the real Firestore emulator admits a current active platform
  owner and rejects demoted, inactive, auth-disabled, blocked, deleted,
  unverified and missing current users. The auth source gate proves the
  current-user read and its ordering are owned by the callable.
- **Validation/deployment:** Functions build, `npm run
  test:analytics:settlement`, `npm run verify:analytics-write-boundary`, `npm
  run verify:auth-security-failure-matrix`, and focused ESLint pass. The
  required narrow QA deployment was attempted with `firebase deploy --only
  functions:triggerCustomerAnalyticsManually --project menulist-qa` and stopped
  before upload because Firebase CLI authentication is unavailable
  (`Failed to authenticate, have you run firebase login?`). No remote revision
  changed. Closure was confirmed locally in restart 1168.

The complete aggregation source is now reviewed: exact daily/summary/dashboard
contracts, store/date project discovery, idempotent settlement, late
correction, cache/range rollups, replacement writes, cleanup batching, bounded
AI payload construction/fallbacks and manual failure behavior were reconciled.

## Restart 1166 addendum — analytics delivery receipt reverse trace

Restart 1166 changed direction to datastore-first and reversed
`analyticsDeliveryReceipts` through its sole Admin writer, public route,
browser queue, current target authority, transaction, TTL override, deny-all
rule and focused emulators. One P1 defect was confirmed and closed;
`consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains `0`.

### AUDIT-ANALYTICS-INFLIGHT-ACK-LOSS-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P1 / Closed locally /
  `src/database/analytics/index.ts`,
  `src/lib/analytics/queueBoundary.ts`; public menu/OBP/Customer App event →
  browser coalescing queue → public analytics route → Admin daily increment +
  `analyticsDeliveryReceipts` transaction → owner analytics consumers.
- **Affected structure/producer/consumer/trigger:** one queue row held a single
  delivery ID, mutable counters and event count. The browser produced it and
  the receipt-backed Admin writer consumed it. The trigger was a server-applied
  request whose acknowledgement was lost while newer events entered the same
  scope queue.
- **Observed behavior:** the first request snapshotted the old counters but
  left them in the mutable queue under the same delivery ID. New counters were
  merged during flight. On retry, the client sent the combined counters with
  the old ID; the server correctly returned `duplicate` from the first
  receipt, and the client then drained the combined payload. The newer counters
  were never persisted.
- **Expected/root cause:** retries for one delivery ID must be byte-for-byte
  equivalent to the payload guarded by its receipt. Pending work created after
  delivery begins must have a distinct ID and lifecycle.
- **Security/tenant/data/public/cache impact:** tenant isolation and private
  fields were unaffected, but owner-visible analytics could undercount menu,
  OBP or Customer App events after an acknowledgement loss. The defect did not
  alter public menu truth or cache identity.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** immediately before network work, the queue
  persists an exact `activeDelivery` snapshot, clears pending counters and
  rotates the pending delivery ID. Retries replay only the active snapshot.
  New events remain pending under the new ID; acknowledgement clears only the
  active snapshot. Persisted legacy rows retain deterministic migration, while
  malformed active/pending envelopes fail closed.
- **Collection contract:** receipt IDs hash exact tenant/store/project/date and
  delivery identity. The sole Admin transaction reads the receipt, increments
  the exact daily document and creates a 72-hour TTL receipt. The public route
  admits only current active tenant/store/project truth and the current or
  previous business date. Firestore rules deny all browser receipt access; the
  TTL field override disables unused indexing. Remote TTL activation remains
  operator-controlled and was not claimed verified.
- **Files changed/tests/validation:** queue runtime and projector, browser
  regression, aggregate source gate, implementation/Firebase docs, ledger and
  collection ownership record. The regression proves active and pending
  payloads restore with distinct IDs and rejects malformed active state.
  `npm run verify:analytics-write-boundary` passes its browser, normalizer,
  Admin transaction, owner-action receipt and real rules emulators. Exact
  TypeScript and focused ESLint pass. Closure was confirmed in restart 1166.

### AUDIT-ANALYTICS-LIVE-QUEUE-FIELD-CAP-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /
  `src/database/analytics/index.ts`,
  `src/lib/analytics/queueBoundary.ts`; live browser event merge → persisted
  queue → 100-field public route schema.
- **Observed/root cause/data impact:** the live queue attempted a flush above
  100 fields but, while another delivery was active, continued accepting as
  many as 200 distinct fields. Persisted restore and the public route both cap
  one payload at 100, so the accepted pending state could only produce a 400
  response and eventual drop.
- **Fix/compatibility:** one shared pure field-cap predicate now governs live
  merge admission with the same `ANALYTICS_QUEUE_MAX_FIELDS` constant used by
  persisted normalization. A would-be over-wide event returns `false` and does
  not consume analytics session milestones; existing deliverable queued data
  remains intact and can flush.
- **Regression/validation:** the browser suite proves 100 existing fields plus
  one new field is refused while normal merges remain accepted. The source
  gate forbids the prior 200-field allowance. Browser regression, exact
  TypeScript and focused ESLint pass; closure was confirmed in restart 1166.

- **Observed/root cause/security impact:** tenant/store Admin read failures
  were logged and converted to `null`, which is indistinguishable from an

  a missing email, but the new-user branch called `email.split()` and other

### AUDIT-AUTH-SIGNOUT-COMPLETION-001

- **Severity/status/file/flow:** P2 / Closed locally /

- **Observed/root cause/reliability impact:** the helper resolved `true`

### AUDIT-ANALYTICS-CACHE-SERIALIZATION-BOUNDARY-001 — owner analytics cache trusted a non-serializable compile-time shape

  owner analytics dashboard read model → JSON local-storage cache → SWR/UI.

  as JavaScript `Date` values, while the same `AnalyticsData` object was
  JSON-stringified into local storage and generically returned as

  keys remained correctly tenant/store/project partitioned and no
  cross-tenant exposure was found.

  ISO strings from Firestore timestamps, Dates or exact ISO cache values.
  Both cache paths validate the complete summary/daily container and evict a
  malformed entry before fetching authoritative data. Valid existing

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** `AUDIT-GROWTHOS-PERSISTED-RESPONSE-CONTRACT-001`

### AUDIT-LEGACY-COMPRESSED-IMAGE-VALIDATION-001 — compressed images were validated against stale source metadata

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** `AUDIT-LEGACY-COMPRESSED-IMAGE-VALIDATION-001`
  / P1 / Closed in restart 1350.
- **File/function/flow/structure:**
  `src/components/atoms/imageUploadInput/index.tsx` and
  `src/lib/media/legacyImageUploadBoundary.ts`; browser file input →
  optional compression → magic-byte validation → parent owner/platform image
  draft; `UserUploadedFileType`.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** for a legacy image larger than the
  500 KB compression threshold, Compressor emitted a new data URL. Validation
  still supplied the original file size and MIME. `validateImageFile`
  deliberately requires decoded bytes to equal the declared size and magic
  bytes to match the MIME, so compressed output was rejected whenever its size
  changed and could also be rejected when PNG conversion emitted JPEG.
- **Expected/root cause:** security validation must inspect the exact bytes
  handed to downstream consumers. The legacy pipeline correctly added strict
  byte validation later, but retained pre-compression metadata from the older
  flow.
- **Security/tenant/data/public/cache impact:** validation remained fail-closed,
  so no unsafe bytes, tenant crossover or cache leak occurred. Valid tenant
  logos, owner images or prompt images above the threshold could not traverse
  this active pipeline, producing a serious owner image-workflow failure.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** a pure boundary derives decoded size and
  actual MIME from the emitted data URL. Validation, returned type/size and any
  changed extension now agree with those bytes. Optional compression metadata
  is omitted rather than emitted as `undefined`; single/multiple callbacks are
  exact and awaited before success. Existing uncompressed and prepared-media
  behavior remains compatible.
- **Files changed/regression:** image input, pure legacy boundary, media-source
  regression, and typed input refs in the tenant editor and AI edit modal.
  The regression proves a source PNG represented by compressed JPEG bytes is
  admitted using emitted metadata and malformed base64 is denied.
- **Validation/result:** `npm run test:media-image-source-boundary`,
  `npm run verify:auth-security-failure-matrix`, ordinary TypeScript, focused
  ESLint and `git diff --check` pass.
- **Closure:** confirmed closed by restart 1350; no persisted-data migration is
  required.

### AUDIT-TIPTAP-SLASH-COMMAND-EMPTY-LIFECYCLE-001 — empty suggestions corrupted selection and dereferenced an absent popup

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**
  `AUDIT-TIPTAP-SLASH-COMMAND-EMPTY-LIFECYCLE-001` / P2 / Closed in restart
  1351.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** Tiptap slash-command list and extension;
  owner/editor keyboard input → filtered suggestion items → Tiptap command →
  document mutation; `SlashCommandItem` and suggestion lifecycle.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** an empty filtered result handled
  Arrow keys with modulo zero, moving selection to `NaN`, and still swallowed
  Enter. If Tiptap supplied no usable client rectangle, no Tippy instance was
  created, yet Escape/update/exit dereferenced `popup[0]`. The extension hid
  these and all other contract gaps behind `@ts-nocheck`.
- **Expected/root cause:** empty suggestions must decline navigation, and every
  popup/renderer callback must tolerate partial lifecycle creation. The legacy
  integration predated the current Tiptap types and used broad `any` plus a
  file-wide suppression.
- **Security/tenant/data/public/cache impact:** no tenant, persistence or public
  cache boundary was bypassed. The defect could corrupt local selection state
  or throw during rich-text editing, interrupting an owner mutation before
  persistence.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** exact editor/range/item/list and suggestion
  generics replace all broad inputs; a pure navigator rejects empty/invalid
  counts and wraps valid indices; Enter only consumes a real item; popup and
  renderer lifecycle calls are nullable; `@ts-nocheck` is removed. Existing
  headings, lists, tasks and blockquote commands are unchanged.
- **Files changed/regression:** list, extension, typed extension registry, pure
  navigator, registered regression and `package.json`. The regression covers
  empty/invalid counts, wrapping, suppression absence and popup lifecycle
  guards.
- **Validation/result:** `npm run test:tiptap-slash-command-boundary`,
  `npm run verify:dependency-freeze`, ordinary TypeScript, focused ESLint and
  `git diff --check` pass. An initial source-assertion regex was over-escaped;

  required.

### AUDIT-MOBILE-UPLOAD-LATE-STORE-CONTEXT-001 — late identity acknowledgement crossed the active tenant/store context

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** `AUDIT-MOBILE-UPLOAD-LATE-STORE-CONTEXT-001`

  IDs; the pure `mergeBusinessIdentityUpdatesForCurrentStore` projector returns

### AUDIT-MOBILE-UPLOAD-PREVIEW-URL-LIFECYCLE-001 — retained selections lost their object URLs on every state change

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** `AUDIT-MOBILE-UPLOAD-PREVIEW-URL-LIFECYCLE-001`
  / P2 / Closed locally.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** `MenuUploadSheet` selected-file state,
  cleanup effect and review renderer.
- **Trigger/observed:** the effect depended on `selectedFiles`, so React ran its
  cleanup before every new selection render and revoked every preview URL from
  the previous array, including files that remained selected. Adding or
  removing another file could therefore break still-active menu previews.
- **Expected/root cause/impact:** removed files must be revoked immediately and
  remaining files only on unmount. The cleanup was written as an unmount
  handler but had mutable state in its dependency list. Storage/persistence and
  tenant scope were unaffected; owner review correctness was not.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** a current selection ref owns all live URLs;
  the updater revokes only removed members and updates ownership; the
  dependency-free unmount cleanup revokes the final live set.
- **Regression/validation:** the Menu Extraction source gate requires that
  ownership lifecycle and rejects the old dependency; the complete aggregate,
  TypeScript, ESLint and diff hygiene pass.
- **Closure:** confirmed closed by restart 1353.

### AUDIT-SERVICE-WORKER-CLIENT-NAVIGATION-RECONCILIATION-001 — route-dependent worker selection ran only once

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** `AUDIT-SERVICE-WORKER-CLIENT-NAVIGATION-RECONCILIATION-001`
  / P2 / Closed locally.

  reconciliations also had no ordering authority.

  observe pathname changes and the latest route decision must settle last.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** `usePathname()` now triggers reconciliation,

  work is skipped. Origin/product fail-closed selection is unchanged.

  dependency and queue ownership; Customer App, owner lifecycle, MyCodex and
  auth/security aggregates pass.

### AUDIT-SERVICE-WORKER-SCOPE-IDENTITY-001 — same script at a narrowed scope was accepted as the root worker

### AUDIT-SHARED-DEEP-EQUALITY-TEMPORAL-CYCLE-001 — menu comparison mishandled temporal and cyclic values

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** `AUDIT-SHARED-DEEP-EQUALITY-TEMPORAL-CYCLE-001`

  or mobile edit comparison -> save/no-op decision.
- **Trigger/observed:** the legacy recursive comparator treated nested `Date`

  equality across persisted/browser temporal values and must terminate for

### AUDIT-STAFF-STORE-DETAILS-LATE-TENANT-SETTLEMENT-001 — lazy role load could contaminate a later tenant context

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** `AUDIT-STAFF-STORE-DETAILS-LATE-TENANT-SETTLEMENT-001`
  / P0 / Closed locally.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** desktop staff form `StoresMapping` ->
  `readStoreById` -> shared `tenantDetails` role cache -> later staff-role
  selectors.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** selecting an unloaded store started an
  untracked client read and captured only an array index. If the owner switched
  tenant/store before settlement, the callback mutated whichever tenant object
  was current and could install the prior tenant's store details and roles.
- **Expected/root cause/impact:** asynchronous tenant cache settlement must
  prove exact tenant/store identity and current membership. A mutable captured
  object/index is not authority; this could cross-contaminate owner-visible
  tenant context and subsequent role decisions.
- **Fix/backward compatibility/cache impact:** settlement is functional and
  immutable, requires exact expected/current/loaded tenant and store identity,
  and becomes a no-op after a context switch or removal. Read failures emit
  bounded tenant/store diagnostics.
- **Regression/validation:** `test:staff-form-mapping-boundary` covers exact and
  wrong-tenant/store settlement; staff scope/route/concurrency, emulator,
  auth/security and tenant-safety aggregates pass.
- **Closure:** confirmed closed by restart 1357.

### AUDIT-DESKTOP-ROLE-LATE-STORE-SETTLEMENT-001 — awaited role mutations could replace the newly active store

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** `AUDIT-DESKTOP-ROLE-LATE-STORE-SETTLEMENT-001`
  / P0 / Closed locally.

  staff-role API -> `PlatformGlobalDataContext.setStoreDetails` -> role and
  permission consumers.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** both desktop mutations spread the
  store object captured before `await` and wrote it after settlement. Switching
  stores or tenants while the request was pending could replace the new
  context with the old store plus response roles.
- **Expected/root cause/impact:** late mutation acknowledgement must update only
  the exact source store context and revision. Otherwise owner state can cross
  store/tenant boundaries even though the server mutation itself is authorized.
- **Fix/backward compatibility/cache impact:** `mergeStaffRolesForCurrentStore`
  admits response roles only when tenant ID, store ID and source-role reference
  still match. Role selection derives again from the admitted current store;
  modals close on scope changes.
- **Regression/validation:** the focused behavior test covers store and source
  revision mismatch; the route-parity verifier locks both desktop call sites.
  Staff emulator, auth/security and tenant-safety aggregates pass.
- **Closure:** confirmed closed by restart 1357.

### AUDIT-STAFF-STORE-SELECTION-ROLE-CARRYOVER-001 — changing a store retained authority from the prior store

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** `AUDIT-STAFF-STORE-SELECTION-ROLE-CARRYOVER-001`

  proves role reset and immutable input.

### AUDIT-PLATFORM-ASSET-LOCAL-UPLOAD-NETWORK-001 — local image selection depended on an unintended upload request

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** `AUDIT-PLATFORM-ASSET-LOCAL-UPLOAD-NETWORK-001`
  / P2 / Closed locally.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** platform Assets -> `DetailsModal.ImageUploader`
  -> Ant Upload -> local preview -> static asset DAL.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** selecting a local file used the Upload
  component without `beforeUpload` or a custom request, while the handler only
  consumed files whose network-upload status became `done`. The browser could
  POST the selected file to the current route and a rejected/missing upload
  action left the intended local preview unset.
- **Expected/root cause/impact:** local preview intake must be browser-local,
  bounded, and independent of an unrelated route response. The component
  accidentally used network-upload lifecycle semantics for a local FileReader
  flow.
- **Fix/security/data/cache/backward compatibility:** `beforeUpload` now starts
  the local reader and synchronously returns `false`, so no upload request is
  created. Persistence still occurs only through the existing static asset DAL;
  no collection, cache or public DTO changed.
- **Regression/validation/closure:** the Storage hardening source gate requires
  the local-only admission and rejects restoration of the old `onChange`
  contract; exact TypeScript, focused lint and auth/security gates pass.
  Confirmed closed by restart 1359.

### AUDIT-PLATFORM-ASSET-LATE-FILE-SETTLEMENT-001 — a late file read could populate a different asset modal

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** `AUDIT-PLATFORM-ASSET-LATE-FILE-SETTLEMENT-001`
  / P2 / Closed locally.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** platform Assets modal identity -> async
  base64/SVG read -> selected preview -> category/subcategory/item write.
- **Trigger/observed:** the FileReader/base64 callback had no modal or selection
  ownership token. Closing or switching the drawer while it ran allowed the
  old file to settle into the newly selected entity.

  selection that initiated it; otherwise an administrator can persist the
  wrong image on another asset.
- **Fix/security/data/cache/backward compatibility:** a monotonic read epoch is
  invalidated on every modal change and new selection; late success, failure
  and loading settlement are ignored. Persisted shapes and public rendering
  remain unchanged.
- **Regression/validation/closure:** the Storage gate requires epoch capture
  and stale-settlement rejection; exact TypeScript and focused lint pass.
  Confirmed closed by restart 1359.

### AUDIT-PLATFORM-ASSET-DUPLICATE-MUTATION-001 — save and delete admitted overlapping writes

### AUDIT-PLATFORM-USER-TENANT-STORE-CROSS-SCOPE-001 — user tenant changes retained prior-tenant store authority

  mappings/default -> direct users write.

  store option list, `stores`, `storeIds`, and default `storeId` remained from

  create/metadata/active/special-menu calls, extraction upload handoffs and

## Restart 1302 addendum — special-hours end-to-end publication reconciliation

Restart 1302 reconciled concurrently added exact-date special-hours truth from
the canonical store type and DAL normalizer through desktop/mobile mutation,
the timezone-aware hours evaluator, public menu/OBP output, action analytics,
Public Business API, browser projection and Schema.org output. Two public-truth
P1 defects, three P2 boundary defects and one P3 evidence-gate defect were

collection, provider or deployment source changed, and the clean-pass counter
