### AUDIT-SPECIAL-HOURS-OVERNIGHT-PUBLIC-TRUTH-001 — previous-date special overnight service disappeared at midnight

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** `AUDIT-SPECIAL-HOURS-OVERNIGHT-PUBLIC-TRUTH-001`
  / P1 / Closed locally in restart 1302.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** `src/lib/hours/hoursEngine.ts`;
  exact-date store override → current/next status engine → public menu, OBP,
  owner Today and analytics consumers.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** when weekly hours were absent and a
  prior-date special range crossed midnight, `getStoreStatus` and
  `getMinutesUntilStoreStatusChange` returned unavailable/null before
  evaluating that active range. When weekly hours existed, the active range
  could still be labeled as regular because provenance came from the current
  date rather than the interval that actually kept the store open.
- **Expected/root cause/impact:** a range belongs to the store-local date on
  which it starts, including an exact-date override. The early availability
  guard ignored prior-date override truth and active intervals discarded
  their source metadata, causing incorrect public open/closed truth and
  occasion labeling around midnight.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** the availability guard recognizes only a
  valid previous-date overnight override; active intervals retain exact
  regular/special provenance and label through overlap extension. A
  current-date override still owns the complete date and correctly suppresses
  prior carry.
- **Regression/validation:** deterministic UTC cases cover special-only
  overnight carry, remaining minutes, label/provenance and current-date closed
  suppression. `npm run verify:working-hours-boundary`, exact TypeScript and
  focused ESLint pass.
- **Re-audit pass in which confirmed closed:** restart 1302; clean counter
  reset.

### AUDIT-SPECIAL-HOURS-CONSUMER-PROPAGATION-001 — public consumers retained weekly-only assumptions

- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** footer action analytics called the
  legacy four-argument evaluator and classified a special closure as open.
  The OBP hours list explicitly admitted a special-hours-only store but then
  dereferenced missing weekly hours; its Today projection could also call an
  absent current schedule “Closed today” when only a future exception existed.
- **Expected/root cause/impact:** every materially distinct consumer must use
  effective store-local truth, and partial legacy schedules must remain
  fail-safe. These weekly-only assumptions could corrupt action segmentation,
  crash a public page or publish a false current closure. Tenant/cache scope
  and private-field projection were unaffected.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** footer analytics delegates to the canonical
  special-aware evaluator and maps unavailable truth to `unknown`. OBP uses
  optional weekly access and distinguishes no current schedule from an
  explicit closed override. Existing complete weekly documents render
  unchanged.
- **Regression/validation:** the maintained source gate pins both consumer
  paths; the runtime suite covers special open/closed/unavailable evaluation.
  Working-hours verification, exact TypeScript and focused ESLint pass.
- **Re-audit pass in which confirmed closed:** restart 1302; clean counter
  reset.

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** `AUDIT-SPECIAL-HOURS-SCHEMA-COMPOSITION-001`
  / P1 / Closed locally in restart 1302.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** `src/lib/schema/index.ts`;

  persisted special hours plus active Temporary Status → LocalBusiness

### AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-ONTOLOGY-CLIENT-SETTLEMENT-OWNERSHIP-001 — an older response could retire a newer retry token

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**
  `AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-ONTOLOGY-CLIENT-SETTLEMENT-OWNERSHIP-001` / P2 / Closed
  locally in restart 1305.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** `src/lib/answerlattice/ontologyClient.ts`;
  `src/database/answerlattice/canonicalAnswers.ts`;
  `src/lib/answerlattice/pendingMutationRequests.ts`; owner ontology or
  canonical proposal action → validated request with browser-held idempotency
  ID → authenticated governance route → exact result acknowledgement →
  pending retry-map settlement.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** a second, materially different action
  could replace the pending entry under the same UI retry key while the first
  request remained in flight. When the first response later succeeded, it
  unconditionally deleted the retry key now owned by the second action. If the
  second acknowledgement was then lost, retry generated a new request ID and
  could repeat the mutation instead of replaying it. Canonical proposals had
  the parallel same-action form: concurrent identical submissions shared one
  request ID, but the first acknowledgement deleted it while another attempt
  remained unresolved.
- **Expected/root cause/security/data impact:** only the request that owns the
  current action fingerprint and request ID may retire pending retry state.
  The defect did not cross tenant scope, but response reordering could defeat
  client-side mutation idempotency and duplicate a valid ontology action.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** one shared boundary now gives every in-flight
  call an unforgeable attempt token. Settlement compares fingerprint, request
  ID and attempt ownership, and deletes the registry entry only after every
  active attempt has acknowledged. Older responses cannot clear newer
  ownership; ordinary single-action success still releases its entry.
- **Regression/validation:** the new behavior suite starts two different
  actions under one retry key, settles the older response first, then proves a
  retry of the newer action retains its exact request ID, and separately proves
  the first of two identical acknowledgements cannot retire the second claim.
  `npm run test:answerlattice-ontology-client`, ontology contracts, the runtime
  truth verifier, exact TypeScript and focused ESLint pass.
- **Re-audit pass in which confirmed closed:** restart 1305; clean counter
  reset.

### AUDIT-DIGITAL-SCREEN-MANAGEMENT-RESPONSE-BOUNDARY-001 — owner client trusted an unbounded cast management response

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**
  `AUDIT-DIGITAL-SCREEN-MANAGEMENT-RESPONSE-BOUNDARY-001` / P2 / Closed locally
  in restart 1313.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** `src/database/campaigns/index.ts`;
  `callDigitalScreenManagementApi` and `hydrateDigitalScreenOwnerState`;
  `src/lib/screen/screenManagementContracts.ts`; protected
  `/api/digital-screens` response → owner screen state → desktop/mobile owner
  consumers.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** the authenticated route returned a
  typed owner transport, but the browser consumed it with unbounded
  `response.json()` and asserted `Partial<DigitalScreenManagementResponse>`.
  It checked only `success`, then called `.map` on an unchecked nested value
  and constructed Firestore timestamps from unchecked milliseconds. A
  malformed or unexpectedly large same-origin response could therefore cause
  uncontrolled allocation or non-contract exceptions before the existing
  hydrated-state guard.
- **Expected/root cause/security/data/public/cache impact:** every network
  response remains runtime input even when it originates from a protected
  first-party route. The browser must cap bytes and validate the complete
  success/null/state/slide/token/timestamp contract before hydration. This was
  an owner-surface reliability and runtime type-integrity defect; the route's
  authentication, store permission, tenant scope, persistence transaction,
  public mirror and cache invalidation were already correct and unchanged.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** the DAL uses the shared bounded-response
  reader with a 64 KiB cap and parses as `unknown`. The shared screen contract
  now validates positive in-range Firestore milliseconds, current token
  syntax, finite confidence/version values, the configured three-slide cap,
  real arrays and every persisted slide field before hydration. Valid current
  and legacy empty-screen responses retain their wire shape. The stale Today
  summary branch also omits an optional field instead of materializing an
  implicit-any `undefined` property; runtime output is JSON-equivalent.
- **Regression test:** the lifecycle suite accepts the exact valid transport
  and rejects an array-like slide collection and an out-of-range timestamp.
  The source boundary gate requires the byte cap, `unknown` parse and runtime
  guard and forbids the former unbounded cast parser.
- **Validation commands/results:** `npm run verify:digital-screens-boundary`
  passed the source gate, seen/timestamp/lifecycle tests, Firestore rules
  emulator and Admin management emulator; expected rules-denial diagnostics
  were observed. `npm run verify:public-business-truth`, exact TypeScript,
  focused ESLint and `git diff --check` passed. The staged strict replay
  decreased from 653 to 652 diagnostics and has zero diagnostics in all four
  changed runtime/test files. A separate full nullability override reports
  1,781 diagnostics and remains evidence for the open root strict-mode
  migration rather than closure evidence for this finding.
- **Re-audit pass in which confirmed closed:** restart 1313; clean counter
  reset.

### AUDIT-RAZORPAY-WEBHOOK-CLAIM-DISCRIMINANT-001 — terminal claim outcomes prevented safe acquired-attempt narrowing

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**
  `AUDIT-RAZORPAY-WEBHOOK-CLAIM-DISCRIMINANT-001` / P3 / Closed locally in
  restart 1314.
- **File/function/flow/structure:**
  `src/lib/billing/razorpayWebhookLease.ts`; `RazorpayWebhookClaim`;
  `src/app/api/razorpay/webhook/route.ts`; signed provider event → durable
  claim → financial/subscription/top-up effects → attempt-fenced terminal
  ledger state.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** the claim type represented
  `"processed" | "processing"` inside one union member rather than two
  variants. After the route returned for each terminal outcome, TypeScript
  still could not prove that the remaining claim was acquired and reported
  three unsafe `attemptId` accesses. The non-strict root compiler hid the
  disagreement even though runtime producers returned the intended objects.
- **Expected/root cause/security/data/public/cache impact:** an idempotency
  claim is a three-state protocol and each state must be independently
  discriminated. Attempt ownership must be available only on `acquired`.
  Runtime lease fencing was already correct, so no duplicate payment or
  entitlement effect was observed; the defect was a concrete type-governance
  and future-maintenance risk in a payment-critical path.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** `acquired`, `processed` and `processing`
  are separate union variants. Runtime object shapes and ledger persistence
  are unchanged. After terminal/concurrent early returns, the route copies
  the acquired UUID to one immutable local used by success, no-op and failure
  completion paths.
- **Regression test:** the real lease emulator includes a compile-time
  `Extract<RazorpayWebhookClaim, { outcome: "processing" }>` contract. It
  resolves to `never` under the former declaration and now proves the distinct
  variant before exercising concurrent, retry, stale-owner, malformed-state
  and terminal-pruning behavior. The aggregate billing source gate pins both
  literal variants.
- **Validation commands/results:** `npm run
  test:razorpay-webhook-lease:emulator`, `npm run
  verify:billing-entitlement-boundary`, exact TypeScript, focused ESLint and
  `git diff --check` passed. The staged strict replay fell from 652 to 649
  diagnostics and has zero diagnostics in the claim contract, webhook route
  and regression files.
- **Re-audit pass in which confirmed closed:** restart 1314; clean counter
  reset.

### AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-SUPPORT-BOARD-PERSISTED-CARD-001 — Firestore cards were partially checked then broadly cast

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**
  `AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-SUPPORT-BOARD-PERSISTED-CARD-001` / P2 / Closed locally
  in restart 1315.
- **File/function/flow/structure:**
  `src/database/answerlattice/supportBoard.ts`;
  `src/lib/answerlattice/supportBoardReadBoundary.ts`;
  `answerlattice_supportBoardCards`; ticket/signal/manual/nightly producer →
  persisted private work card → list, deduplication, status, note and redaction
  consumers.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** bounded list reads checked only
  `pId`, numeric equality, title and status before asserting the entire
  Firestore object as `AnswerlatticeSupportBoardCard`. Transactional readers
  asserted the same type without runtime checks and then spread notes/status
  histories or returned an existing card. A malformed legacy/Admin row could
  therefore reach owner state or make a later client mutation preserve or
  amplify malformed arrays, timestamps, source identity or resolution state.
- **Expected/root cause/security/data/public/cache impact:** Firestore rules
  protect current browser writes but do not validate historical data or Admin
  writers at read time. Every consumer must reconcile product, numeric tenant
  and workspace scope, document ID, required scalars, source contract,
  bounded optional fields, real arrays, note/status entries, newest-status
  agreement, timestamp fields and redaction/resolution coupling. The board is
  private and no cross-tenant read was observed; the risk was owner-state and
  subsequent-mutation integrity.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** one pure projector now enforces those
  invariants and preserves valid current client and nightly writer shapes.
  The list drops invalid rows; transactional paths reject invalid state
  explicitly. Card creation normalization also has an exact contextual return
  type, removing six implicit-any defaults without casts or suppressions.
  Query limits, indexes, permissions, product separation and write counts are
  unchanged.
- **Regression test:** a new runtime suite accepts the exact current card and
  rejects coercive scope, array-like notes, divergent newest status, missing
  non-manual source identity and half-written source redaction. The existing
  source contract forbids the prior persisted-card cast and pins projector use
  in list and mutations.
- **Validation commands/results:** `npm run
  verify:answerlattice-support-board` passed the source/runtime/evidence
  contracts, real dedicated summary emulator and both dedicated/shared rules
  emulators; expected denial diagnostics and the invalid-scope warning were
  observed. Dependency freeze, exact TypeScript, focused ESLint and
  `git diff --check` passed. The staged strict replay fell from 649 to 643
  diagnostics with zero diagnostics in the DAL, projector and tests.
- **Re-audit pass in which confirmed closed:** restart 1315; clean counter
  reset.

workflow reference constructed directly from an action input.

### AUDIT-SIGNALDESK-DOCUMENT-ID-BOUNDARY-001 — direct action IDs could alter Firestore reference shape

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**
  `AUDIT-SIGNALDESK-DOCUMENT-ID-BOUNDARY-001` / P2 / Closed locally in
  restart 1367.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** `src/app/api/signaldesk/actions/route.ts`
  action schemas; `src/lib/signaldesk/workflowServer.ts` protected workflow
  mutations; caller action DTO → runtime validation → product-private Admin
  transaction → SignalDesk collection document.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** authenticated platform actions could
  supply leading/trailing whitespace, slash-delimited paths, reserved
  Firestore identifiers, or unbounded IDs to multiple schemas. The workflow
  server then passed materially different direct input strings to `.doc()`.
  Some client response projectors rejected slash forms, but that was after
  mutation admission and was neither universal nor a server authority check.
- **Expected/root cause/security/data/public/cache impact:** all
  caller-supplied document identity must retain its exact submitted value and
  remain one valid Firestore document segment before any Admin reference is
  constructed. The defect did not cross a MenuList tenant boundary because
  SignalDesk is a separate global product-private project and action access
  remained platform-gated, but malformed identities could address an
  unintended document path or create unreachable duplicate truth. No public
  DTO, cache, Redux, SWR, local storage, billing or external-send behavior is
  involved.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** one shared boundary now rejects empty,
  whitespace-mutated, slash/path-shaped, reserved and overlong IDs while
  preserving exact valid values. Protected action schemas, the signed outcome
  bridge and exported workflow entry points apply it before every direct
  non-enum input reference across content, revenue, partner, approval, AI,
  outbound, outcome, demand and route-token flows. The reverse persisted-data
  trace applies the same rule to target/research DTOs, replay pointers and
  workspace projectors; malformed optional references invalidate their
  containing row instead of being trimmed into different authority.
  Closed-enum channel control IDs remain internally derived. Valid persisted
  IDs and deterministic server-generated IDs are unchanged.
- **Regression test:** `test-signaldesk-document-id-boundary.ts` covers exact
  values, whitespace mutation, slash paths, reserved values and length caps.
  The local emulator exercises malformed content-source, pod, offer,
  experiment and review identities while retaining valid idempotent and
  signed-outcome behavior. The aggregate source verifier pins both the action
  and server boundary.
- **Validation commands/results:** `npm run verify:signaldesk` passed 4,148
  source checks and all focused runtime contracts; `npm run
  test:signaldesk:e2e:local` passed on a fresh emulator after the fixture
  repair; the signed bridge, operating, revenue, provider-accounting and
  outcome/content focused emulator slices also passed. Exact TypeScript,
  focused ESLint and `git diff --check` passed. The collection families remain
  conservatively `in-progress` because their large shared workflow, route,
  rules, index, E2E and verifier sources retain ranged rather than complete
  whole-file evidence.
- **Re-audit pass in which confirmed closed:** restart 1367; clean counter
  reset.

### AUDIT-SIGNALDESK-PERSISTED-DOCUMENT-ID-PROJECTION-001 — stored references could be trimmed into different authority

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**
  `AUDIT-SIGNALDESK-PERSISTED-DOCUMENT-ID-PROJECTION-001` / P2 / Closed

  `src/lib/signaldesk/outcomeBridgeServer.ts` and the persisted projectors,

  → Admin document reference → private SignalDesk workspace or mutation.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** several stored document-reference
  fields used ordinary text normalization. A whitespace-mutated reference
  could therefore project as a different exact ID, while a path-shaped
  optional reference could survive until a later `.doc()` consumer. The same
  gap existed in operating-envelope ID arrays, signed outcome target IDs and
  a subset of exported server helpers that can be invoked without the HTTP
  action schema.
- **Expected/root cause/security/data/public/cache impact:** persisted and
  caller document identities must preserve exact bytes and remain one valid

  operations retain current access checks, so no MenuList tenant or public DTO
  exposure was demonstrated. The failure path could nevertheless omit,
  misaddress or replay private SignalDesk truth under a different document.
  There is no MenuList public-cache, Redux, SWR, browser-storage or billing
  effect.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** target/research/demand contracts, signed
  bridge payloads, operating-envelope arrays, exported helpers, replay claims
  and custom workspace projectors now use the shared exact
  `normalizeSignalDeskDocumentId` / `requireSignalDeskDocumentId` boundary.
  Invalid optional stored references reject the complete containing record;
  they are not silently removed from an otherwise authoritative projection.
  Exact valid IDs and deterministic server-generated identities retain their
  existing values and document paths.
- **Files changed:** `src/lib/signaldesk/documentIdBoundary.ts`,
  `src/lib/signaldesk/targetContracts.ts`,
  `src/lib/signaldesk/demandSignalContracts.ts`,
  `src/lib/signaldesk/outcomeBridgeServer.ts`,
  `src/lib/signaldesk/workflowServer.ts`,
  `src/app/api/signaldesk/actions/route.ts`, focused tests, the full local E2E
  fixture, runtime verifier and governed SignalDesk/audit documentation.
- **Regression test:** focused document-ID and demand-contract suites reject
  whitespace-mutated and path-shaped values. The emulator proves malformed
  operating-envelope arrays, trust partner/niche IDs, reply conversations,
  route-token target/action/CTA/template IDs, signed target IDs and persisted
  content source/asset references fail closed or are omitted from the private
  workspace without changing valid idempotent behavior.
- **Validation commands/results:** full `npm run
  test:signaldesk:e2e:local`, `npm run verify:signaldesk` (4,148 checks plus
  child suites), `npm run test:signaldesk:rules`, exact non-incremental
  TypeScript, focused ESLint, SecurityOS SignalDesk registry/plan and

  replay-set membership expression; the guard was moved before membership and
  the clean exact rerun passed. Expected emulator `PERMISSION_DENIED` and
  hostile-fixture runtime diagnostics occurred only in passing negative tests.
- **Backward-compatibility/legacy-data impact:** exact historical IDs remain

### AUDIT-PUBLIC-ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-TYPE-001 — malformed lifecycle values were treated as public-eligible

  fields remain a supported legacy shape, but present fields must be exact

  itself write data or alter cache keys.

  validates optional `active`, `deleted`, `blocked`, `tenantBlocked` and nested

### AUDIT-TENANT-NAME-STALE-PLATFORM-AUTHORITY-001 — stale platform session could rename arbitrary tenants

## Restart 1477 addendum — public contact, referral capture and business DTO admission

The public-route cohort was traced from anonymous/contact and referral inputs
through CORS/origin admission, rate limits, Turnstile or encrypted-token
validation, cookies and enquiry persistence, and from API-key admission through

### AUDIT-PUBLIC-RATE-LIMIT-FAIL-CLOSED-PROPAGATION-001 — contact outage policy was not passed to the limiter

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**
  `AUDIT-PUBLIC-RATE-LIMIT-FAIL-CLOSED-PROPAGATION-001` / P2 / Closed locally
  in restart 1477.
- **Flow/root cause/impact:** MenuList and Answerlattice contact callers set
  `failClosed: true`, but `checkPublicRateLimit` did not pass that policy to
  `checkRateLimit`. The shared limiter returns an allowed fallback rather than
  throwing when its provider is unavailable unless explicitly told to fail
  closed, so the wrapper's catch branch never enforced the declared policy.
  During a provider outage, anonymous writes could therefore bypass the
  intended abuse ceiling. Tenant data was not involved and Turnstile remained
  independent.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** the caller policy now reaches
  `failClosedOnProviderError`; provider outages produce retryable 503 while
  actual exhaustion remains 429. Callers that intentionally omit
  `failClosed` retain their existing fail-open availability policy.

### AUDIT-OWNER-REFERRAL-LIMITER-STATUS-001 — provider outage was reported as traffic exhaustion

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** `AUDIT-OWNER-REFERRAL-LIMITER-STATUS-001` /
  P2 / Closed locally in restart 1477.
- **Observed/fix/impact:** referral capture already failed closed in production
  but returned 429 for both provider failure and real exhaustion. It now maps
  `provider_unavailable` to 503 and retains 429 for limit exhaustion, with the
  existing private/no-store and retry headers. Token, pilot-store and cookie
  semantics are unchanged.

### AUDIT-PLATFORM-PULL-NESTED-PROJECTION-001 — raw persisted values crossed the public DTO boundary

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**

  1477.

  allowlisted top-level field names but passed many Firestore values through
  without runtime shape admission. Malformed legacy scalars could become
  arrays/objects, `workingHours`, `socialMedia` and `geo` could carry invalid
  or unexpected nested values, and hostile timestamp-like values could fail
  response construction. That violated the versioned public contract and
  created a concrete unintended-field exposure path to external consumers;
  current credential and tenant isolation were otherwise correct.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** one shared projection now bounds and types
  every scalar, admits only canonical seven-day working-hours values, retains
  bounded legitimate custom social string entries, requires exact finite geo,
  normalizes special hours and serializes only canonical ISO Date/Firestore
  timestamps. Missing or malformed legacy values become `null`; valid v1
  values remain compatible.
- **Regression/validation:** the Platform Pull behavior suite covers nested

## Restart 1372 addendum — Shared KB concurrency-test type convergence

The restarted production-readiness matrix passed the repaired Platform Pull

### AUDIT-SHARED-KB-GENERATION-GATE-RESOLVER-001 — nullable deferred resolver narrowed to `never`

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**
  `AUDIT-SHARED-KB-GENERATION-GATE-RESOLVER-001` / P3 / Closed locally in
  restart 1372.
- **File/function/flow/structure:**
  `scripts/verification/test-shared-kb-generation-emulator.ts`; cancellation
  race fixture → processing-state observation → owner cancellation →
  generation release → terminal-state preservation.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** the fixture declared the Promise
  resolver as `(() => void) | null` and assigned it inside the Promise
  executor. TypeScript does not use callback-local assignment as definite
  control-flow evidence, so after the later assertion the call expression was
  narrowed to `never` and `ts-node` failed with TS2349.
- **Expected/root cause/security/data/public/cache impact:** the concurrency
  regression must compile and execute without a cast or non-null assertion.
  The defect affected test admission only; production Shared KB generation,
  Firestore documents, tenant boundaries, publication, caches and billing were
  unchanged.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** the resolver now has an explicit callable
  initializer that fails fast if the synchronous Promise executor ever fails
  to replace it. The normal executor replaces it immediately, preserving the
  same deterministic cancellation interleaving and eliminating nullable
  control flow without weakening types.
- **Regression/validation:** complete `npm run
  verify:shared-kb-generation-boundary` passes, including the source contract,
  generation Firestore emulator and publishing Firestore emulator; focused
  ESLint and `git diff --check` pass. The generation emulator proves a single
  concurrent claim/write, tenant/store-scoped duplicate evidence,
  cancellation preservation with no orphan article and fail-closed malformed
  scope.
- **Re-audit pass in which confirmed closed:** restart 1372.

## Restart 1503 addendum — public menu claim authority convergence

The authenticated claim route was re-read from bounded request admission through
draft/source validation, current account authority, tenant/store/project writes,
the durable receipt, cache effects and browser URL handoff. Six findings were
closed. `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains `0`.

### AUDIT-PUBLIC-MENU-CLAIM-CURRENT-AUTHORITY-001 — existing-account publish trusted stale session role

- **Severity/status/flow:** P1 / Closed locally in restart 1503; signed claim →
  session-selected tenant/store → store roles → project/public truth write.
- **Observed/root cause:** the transaction re-read store and tenant truth but
  derived the role from the signed session. A disabled, revoked, remapped or
  role-changed user could retain stale publish authority until session refresh.
- **Fix/impact:** the transaction now locks exact `users/{userId}`, applies the
  shared current identity/lifecycle/revocation predicate, requires its current
  tenant/store mapping and an unambiguous persisted store role, then passes that
  fresh role projection to publish permission evaluation. Missing or conflicting
  current authority fails before project/store/summary writes. This closes an
  authorization and tenant-scope race; no public cache identity changed.

### AUDIT-PUBLIC-MENU-CLAIM-NEW-ACCOUNT-CONCURRENCY-001 — allocation omitted the current-user lock

- **Severity/status/flow:** P1 / Closed locally in restart 1503; empty-scope
  authenticated user → starter tenant/store allocation → user mapping/project.
- **Observed/root cause:** unlike website onboarding, claim allocated counters
  and account documents without transactionally proving the current user was
  still active, verified, unblocked, unrevoked and empty-scope. Concurrent
  onboarding paths could both proceed from the same stale session.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** the shared onboarding current-user assertion
  now runs after draft validation and before allocation. Firestore conflict retry
  makes one mapping authoritative; the losing/stale attempt returns bounded 409.
  Valid first claims add one user-document transaction read.

### AUDIT-PUBLIC-MENU-CLAIM-PERSISTED-DEFAULTS-001 — malformed store fields crossed into public truth

- **Severity/status:** P2 / Closed locally in restart 1503.
- **Observed/root cause:** existing `publicPresence`, business attributes/type/
  category and subdomain were read as `DocumentData`, spread or coerced directly,
  and could create numeric keys, invalid public URLs or malformed project/store

### AUDIT-PHONE-OTP-RESEND-COOLDOWN-BOUNDARY-001 — start response coerced an unvalidated resend cooldown

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**

  action, purpose and challenge ID but left `resendAfterSeconds` as `unknown`.

  that control an auth action must be runtime-admitted before use. The server

  public output and caches are unaffected.

  a safe integer cooldown from 1 through 300 seconds, logs only the validation
  boolean on malformed responses and assigns the already narrowed number with
  no coercion. The valid server response behaves identically.

  validation and direct narrowed assignment and forbids the old coercion. The

## Restart 1559 addendum — exact category-review and self-fingerprint convergence

After documentation and assets passed their current category gates, the strict

### AUDIT-AUDIT-REVIEW-STATE-SELF-FINGERPRINT-001 — review-state could never attest its raw hash

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**
  `AUDIT-AUDIT-REVIEW-STATE-SELF-FINGERPRINT-001` / P3 / Closed locally in
  restart 1559.
- **File/function/flow:** manifest generator `fileDigest`, guarded category
  recorder and their source verifier; review evidence -> review-state JSON ->
  manifest fingerprint/status -> exit-criterion coverage.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** writing the review-state file's own raw SHA
  changes that file, so its exact review immediately reopened and could never
  converge. Category defaults did not weaken this, but the self-referential
  artifact had no stable semantic digest. Reapplying category evidence could
  also repeat its note text.
- **Fix/impact:** both producer and consumer now compute the same canonical
  self-fingerprint by replacing only the self entry's `reviewedSha256` value
  with a sentinel before hashing every other semantic field. Category recording
  is dry-run by default, requires explicit category/pass/date/note/tests,
  rejects stale or missing files, preserves findings/evidence and is idempotent.
  Runtime, tenant, persistence, public output, cache and billing behavior are
  unchanged.
- **Regression/validation:** syntax and focused lint pass; the audit source gate
  asserts explicit category selection, stale-hash rejection, dry-run default,
  evidence preservation, canonical self-fingerprint parity and idempotent notes.
  Dependency freeze passes. The regenerated manifest reports all 3,291 docs and
  all 544 assets reviewed, including the review-state artifact itself.
- **Re-audit pass in which confirmed closed:** restart 1559.

### AUDIT-SD-PROVIDER-ADAPTER-REQUEST-CAPTURE-TYPE-001 — request fixture narrowed to `never`

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**
  `AUDIT-SD-PROVIDER-ADAPTER-REQUEST-CAPTURE-TYPE-001` / P3 / Closed locally in
  restart 1550.
- **File/function/flow/structure:**
  `scripts/verification/test-signaldesk-provider-adapter-contracts.ts`,
  `assertMetaTransportContracts()`; provider-send input -> canonical recipient
  -> Meta fetch request -> bounded acknowledgement -> send result.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** a nullable `lastRequest` was assigned only
  inside the mocked fetch closure. TypeScript did not treat that callback
  mutation as guaranteed after the send and narrowed every request-field
  assertion to `never` (five TS2339 errors). The maintained suite must compile
  and inspect the actual captured request without a cast or suppression.

  an array, asserts the final entry exists, then inspects it. Production
  transport, provider calls, tenant data, persistence, billing, public truth and
  caches are unchanged.

  passes recipient injection rejection, SMTP/Meta acknowledgement exactness,

### AUDIT-AL-REVIEW-UPDATE-RETURN-TYPE-001 — transaction result escaped through an unobservable callback assignment

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** `AUDIT-AL-REVIEW-UPDATE-RETURN-TYPE-001` / P2
  / Closed locally in restart 1548.

  `src/lib/answerlattice/knowledgeIntake.ts`,
  `updateKnowledgeIntakeReviewItem()`; scoped review mutation -> Firestore
  transaction -> updated review DTO -> source-governance tests and callers.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** the transaction callback assigned an
  outer `AnswerlatticeIntakeReviewItem | null`, followed by a null guard and
  return outside the callback. TypeScript does not treat closure mutation as a
  guaranteed assignment, narrowed the post-guard value to `never`, and the
  maintained emulator failed TS2339 at both accepted-status assertions before
  executing.

  producer and must return the precise updated DTO. Runtime Firestore writes,
  tenant scope, public truth, caches and billing were unchanged, but the
  exported API contract was unusable to strict TypeScript consumers and
  blocked transactional regression evidence.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** the callback now explicitly returns
  `Promise<AnswerlatticeIntakeReviewItem>` from `runTransaction`; procedure
  deletion is applied to that local result before return. No cast, suppression,
  persistence-shape or behavior change was introduced.
- **Regression/validation:** `npm run test:answerlattice-source-governance`
  passes the rollout flag, exact job scope, reciprocal conflict/cap/rollback,

## Restart 1510 addendum — origin-pinned product redirects

### AUDIT-PROXY-CROSS-ORIGIN-PATH-REDIRECT-001 — protocol-relative request paths changed redirect origin

- **Severity/status:** P1 / Closed locally in restart 1510.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** `src/proxy.ts` cross-origin MenuList
  redirect-domain, legacy Answerlattice and inactive-product redirect branches;
  request Host/path/query → product deployment target → 301/308 response.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed behavior:** an admitted redirect host with
  a pathname such as `//attacker.example/phish` reached
  `new URL(requestPath, trustedTarget)`. URL resolution interpreted the path as
  a protocol-relative URL, so the browser could be redirected away from the
  configured product origin. The final consumer was an unauthenticated public
  browser, enabling trusted-domain phishing redirects.

  must preserve the configured destination origin while carrying only the
  request path/query. Treating an untrusted pathname as a URL reference caused
  the origin escape. No tenant data, persistence, cache, public DTO or legacy
  document shape changed, but the public routing/security boundary was wrong.
- **Fix/files/backward compatibility:** one origin-pinned projector constructs
  the configured target first, then assigns pathname and search. All three
  affected branches use it. Normal paths and query strings are preserved;
  hostile double-slash paths remain paths on the product origin.
- **Regression/validation/closure:** the URL-routing verifier now rejects the
  unsafe constructor pattern and executes the hostile double-slash projection.
  `npm run verify:url-routing-boundary`, the complete MenuList API tenant-safety
  aggregate, Next build-compatibility contract and focused ESLint pass. The
  current proxy fingerprint is closed in restart 1510. This is not a full
  repository pass; `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains `0`.

## Restart 1507 addendum — reseller onboarding authority and recovery convergence

The reseller onboarding route, operation/provider boundaries, atomic billing
writer and focused regressions were traced from current actor admission through
owner Auth, tenant/store/user creation, Razorpay setup, persistence, cache
repair and handoff. Five findings were closed. This is not a full repository
pass; \`consecutiveCleanFullPasses\` remains \`0\`.

### AUDIT-RESELLER-ONBOARD-CURRENT-AUTHORITY-001 — stale actor admission

- **Severity/status/flow:** P1 / Closed locally in restart 1507; signed
  reseller/platform session → current actor/profile → tenant/store provisioning.
- **Observed/root cause:** reseller admission checked the profile but did not
  re-read the MenuList user represented by the session, so a disabled/deleted
  actor with a still-valid session could reach destructive onboarding.
- **Fix/security impact:** non-platform requests now require
  \`getCurrentUser(session)\` plus the exact active reseller profile; platform
  requests retain \`getCurrentPlatformUser(session)\`. Authorization completes
  before owner, tenant, provider or billing side effects.

### AUDIT-RESELLER-ONBOARD-AUTH-SAGA-001 — Auth and business truth could diverge

- **Severity/status/flow:** P1 / Closed locally in restart 1507; owner login →
  Firebase Auth → tenant/store/user transaction → claims/profile.
- **Observed/root cause:** an existing Auth account was mutated before the
  Firestore transaction, while post-transaction claim/profile failure had no
  durable retry checkpoint.
- **Fix/data/backward compatibility:** existing Auth mutation is deferred until
  Firestore creates an exact fingerprinted \`provider_provisioning\` operation
  with tenant/store/user truth. Auth failure returns 503 and keeps this
  credential-free checkpoint. Retry revalidates operation, current store/user
  and reseller ownership before completion; active/disabled state is
  preserved. A newly created Auth user is deleted only when Firestore is proven
  not to have committed.

### AUDIT-RESELLER-ONBOARD-PROVIDER-AMBIGUITY-001 — timeout could orphan or duplicate provider state

- **Severity/status/flow:** P1 / Closed locally in restart 1507; provisional
  operation → Razorpay subscription → checkout → billing commit.
- **Observed/root cause:** ambiguous provider creation could enter local
  compensation, and bounded recovery could not distinguish proven absence from

## Restart 1501 addendum — website onboarding provider-effect convergence

The remaining website onboarding subscription route was re-read end to end
from authenticated current-user admission through allocation, referral binding,
server plan pricing, Razorpay creation/recovery, local subscription persistence,
provider cancellation, workspace compensation, cache invalidation and browser
handoff. Five findings were closed. The adjacent billing source gate exposed
and closed the same limiter-outage diagnostic drift in subscription/top-up
creation and payment verification. `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains `0`.

### AUDIT-ONBOARD-PROVIDER-RESPONSE-BINDING-001 — known provider effects could escape cancellation

- **Severity/status/flow:** P1 / Closed locally in restart 1501; allocated
  workspace → Razorpay create/recovery → provider response admission → local
  subscription or compensation.
- **Observed/root cause:** direct creation required only a syntactically valid
  subscription ID. Provider plan, quantity, total count and exact attempt-bound
  notes were not reconciled. Rejecting a response with an exact owned attempt
  but invalid commercial fields could then compensate tenant/store/user truth
  without cancelling the known live subscription.
- **Security/data/public/cache impact:** no cross-tenant read was confirmed,
  but a malformed or drifted provider response could detach a chargeable
  provider effect from local billing/workspace truth. Compensation cache
  invalidation could publish the removed workspace while billing remained live.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** one runtime boundary now requires exact
  provider plan, quantity, total count, attempt, source, plan, user, tenant and
  store. A separate exact-owned-attempt predicate permits cancellation only
  for an effect provably created by this request, even when its commercial
  fields are wrong; unrelated IDs are never cancelled. Existing correct
  Razorpay responses and numeric/string note encoding remain compatible.
- **Regression/validation:** focused tests reject every mismatched dimension
  and prove that wrong commercial fields retain only the bounded ownership
  needed for safe cancellation. The source verifier locks both predicates and
  cancel-first compensation.

### AUDIT-ONBOARD-CHECKOUT-URL-PERSISTENCE-001 — invalid recovery links entered billing truth

- **Severity/status/flow:** P1 / Closed locally in restart 1501; admitted
  provider subscription → checkout URL normalization → `subscriptions` write →
  returning-owner Pricing/Billing recovery.
- **Observed/root cause:** missing or hostile provider `short_url` normalized to
  an empty string and was persisted as a successful pending subscription. The
  owner could be left with durable payment-pending state that had no usable
  recovery path.
- **Fix/side-effect order:** the allowlisted HTTPS Razorpay URL is mandatory
  before persistence. Direct or recovered exact effects with an invalid URL
  are cancelled first; local workspace compensation runs only after confirmed
  cancellation. Cancellation failure preserves local truth and is observable,
  preventing a live provider effect from becoming ownerless.
- **Regression/validation:** the source gate requires URL failure, exact effect
  cancellation and the checkout-specific diagnostic reason. Existing valid
  links and dismissed-checkout recovery are unchanged.

### AUDIT-ONBOARD-LIMITER-OUTAGE-METADATA-001 — infrastructure failure was reported as quota state

- **Severity/status/flow:** P2 / Closed locally in restart 1501; onboarding and
  adjacent billing request → distributed limiter → security log/HTTP response.
- **Observed/root cause:** onboarding and four billing routes distinguished
  503 from 429 but still logged quota counts, reset times or wait windows during
  provider uncertainty; the aggregate billing verifier also required the old
  fixed quota-exhaustion log literal and failed after the runtime distinction.
- **Fix/regression:** provider outage now has a distinct diagnostic and omits
  quota/reset metadata; real exhaustion retains bounded quota evidence and
  retry headers. The aggregate verifier accepts the explicit ternary and
  requires conditional diagnostic omission. Admission policy and quotas are
  unchanged.

### AUDIT-ONBOARD-PRIVATE-RESPONSE-001 — protected billing handoff lacked uniform cache controls

- **Severity/status:** P3 / Closed locally in restart 1501.
- **Observed/root cause:** tenant/store IDs and billing state relied on ambient
  route defaults; auth, validation and handler failures did not share one
  explicit protected-response policy.
- **Fix/regression:** a route-owned wrapper applies `private, no-store,
  max-age=0` and `nosniff` to the complete authenticated response. Bodies,
  statuses, referral-cookie behavior and browser consumers remain unchanged.

### AUDIT-ONBOARD-BOUNDARY-ANY-001 — request and timestamp boundaries bypassed strict types

- **Severity/status:** P3 / Closed locally in restart 1501.
- **Observed/root cause:** a bounded JSON result was cast to `any`, validation
  diagnostics dereferenced it permissively, and a Firestore client timestamp
  crossed the subscription type through `as any`.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** the request remains `unknown` until strict
  validation; diagnostic projection reads only checked records. The existing
  client Firestore `Timestamp` type is used directly, preserving the stored
  representation accepted by the subscription writer without a cast.

The new Video Projects route was traced through shared auth/scope/rate/body
admission, strict mutation schemas, workspace/campaign/output authority,
idempotency claims, optimistic versions, trust/approval gates, compact project,
event and receipt persistence, owner compositor calls, and Firestore/Storage
rules. Its shared admission dependencies revealed product-wide defects across
all 18 CampaignCue API routes. Four findings were closed;

### AUDIT-CAMPAIGNCUE-RATE-LIMIT-FAILOPEN-001 — every API route bypassed limiter-provider failure

- **Severity/status/flow:** P2 / Closed locally in restart 1499; authenticated
  CampaignCue API request → shared distributed limiter → reads, writes, export
  generation, or response.
- **Observed/root cause:** all routes used one shared helper, but it omitted
  `failClosedOnProviderError`. Missing, timed-out, bypassed, or malformed
  Upstash state therefore admitted requests, including mutation, upload,
  export and AI-operation routes. Provider failure was indistinguishable from
  a successful allowance.
- **Fix/impact/regression:** the shared helper now fails closed. Provider
  uncertainty returns fixed 503 without quota fields/headers and receives a
  distinct bounded diagnostic; real quota exhaustion retains 429 and retry
  metadata. Valid request limits, hashed actor/tenant/store partitioning, data
  contracts, Firebase cost and provider-disabled delivery posture are
  unchanged. The complete CampaignCue verifier source-gates the invariant.

### AUDIT-CAMPAIGNCUE-PRIVATE-RESPONSE-CACHE-001 — protected tenant responses were storable by default

- **Severity/status:** P3 / Closed locally in restart 1499.
- **Observed/root cause:** 18 authenticated API routes created tenant-scoped
  JSON, binary exports and errors without one response-side storage policy;
  helper auth/scope/rate/body branches diverged further. Browser/proxy caches
  could retain private workspace material under ambient defaults.
- **Fix/impact/regression:** one product-owned wrapper now encloses the complete
  existing `withAuth` result and non-overridably stamps private/no-store,
  max-age zero and nosniff headers. Every CampaignCue route uses it, covering
  auth, CORS, scope, validation, limiter, success and exception paths without
  changing bodies or statuses.

### AUDIT-CAMPAIGNCUE-VIDEO-RECEIPT-RESTART-001 — a second key could overwrite an existing render attempt

- **Severity/status/flow:** P2 / Closed locally in restart 1499; approved
  project → browser render start → completed/failed settlement → compact
  project receipt history.
- **Observed/root cause:** terminal receipts required a matching started
  attempt, but `started` was accepted unconditionally. Reusing a receipt ID
  with another idempotency key replaced a completed, failed, or active receipt
  because render settlement intentionally does not increment project version.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** a pure transition boundary admits `started`
  only when the ID is absent and admits terminal state only from the same
  started attempt. Existing normal start/complete/fail flows remain unchanged;
  conflicting retries fail before persistence. Unit tests cover start,
  duplicate start, matching completion and mismatched failure.

### AUDIT-CAMPAIGNCUE-API-GUARD-ANY-BOUNDARIES-001 — shared session helpers erased runtime input types

- **Severity/status:** P3 / Closed locally in restart 1499.
- **Observed/fix:** shared CampaignCue scope, logging, rate and body helpers
  accepted `session: any`, allowing unchecked nested email/name access and
  hiding malformed runtime sessions. Boundaries now accept `unknown`, project
  only record-shaped fields for diagnostics, and leave exact identity to the
  existing session-scope resolver. No new cast or suppression was introduced.

### AUDIT-CAMPAIGNCUE-PERSISTED-RECEIPT-SCHEMA-001 — stored receipt states were weaker than request validation

- **Severity/status:** P2 / Closed locally in restart 1499.
- **Observed/root cause:** after the request boundary was made
  status-specific, the project decoder still allowed completed receipts without
  MIME/size, failed receipts without an error code, and started receipts with
  terminal fields. Malformed Admin/legacy rows could therefore enter owner
  output and subsequent state decisions despite being impossible through the
  current request schema.
- **Fix/regression:** persisted receipt decoding now uses the same discriminated
  state contract plus server timestamps. Unit tests prove malformed completion
  and started-terminal rows fail closed; the bounded list continues omitting
  invalid project records and mutation reads reject them.

Render mutation validation was also tightened to a discriminated status union:

  `answerlattice_entityCandidates` document ID → governance review.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** extraction correctly retained
  distinct multilingual names, but the server upsert removed every character
  outside ASCII `a-z0-9` before hashing. Two Arabic, Indic, CJK, or other
  non-Latin names of the same entity type therefore produced the same empty-name
  ID and were merged into one candidate record.
- **Expected/root cause/security/data/public/cache impact:** deterministic
  identity must remain stable for existing ASCII candidates and distinguish
  supported Unicode scripts. The defect was workspace-scoped, so no
  cross-tenant exposure was found, but it destructively combined review truth,
  descriptions, confidence, frequency, and article provenance. Article public
  output and cache keys were not directly affected.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** the new pure identity boundary applies NFKC,
  locale-independent lowercase normalization and Unicode letter/mark/number
  preservation. Existing ASCII keys are byte-for-byte compatible; distinct
  non-Latin names now hash separately, and all-symbol legacy input cannot share
  an empty identity key.
- **Regression/validation:** pure contract assertions preserve the ASCII key
  and distinguish Arabic names. The Firestore ontology emulator creates two
  same-type Arabic candidates and proves distinct IDs and documents. Runtime
  truth, entity-extraction contracts, and ontology emulator pass.

### AUDIT-AL-ENTITY-EXTRACTION-REQUEST-FALLBACK-001 — request fields could enter persisted extraction truth

- **Severity/status:** P2 / Closed locally in restart 1498.
- **Observed/root cause:** although the maintained browser caller sends only an
  article ID and persisted content was authoritative, the route schema still
  admitted client `title`, `categoryTitle`, and arbitrary `content`. Missing
  legacy persisted title/category values fell back to those request fields in
  the provider prompt and AI accounting response.
- **Fix/impact/regression:** the strict body contract now accepts only the
  normalized article ID. Provider and accounting context use persisted fields
  exclusively. Existing maintained callers are unchanged; regression gates
  reject the old fields and fallback expressions. Firestore shape, valid
  extraction output, article link invalidation, and billing mode remain
  unchanged.

### AUDIT-AL-ENTITY-EXTRACTION-LIMITER-OUTAGE-METADATA-001 — limiter outages emitted quota state

- **Severity/status:** P2 / Closed locally in restart 1498.
- **Observed/root cause:** fail-closed limiter-provider uncertainty correctly

## Restart 1481 addendum — authenticated Razorpay limiter outage convergence

  → subscription checkout, top-up checkout, cancel, pause, resume, upgrade,
  subscription verification or top-up verification → Razorpay and Firestore

  limiter without `failClosedOnProviderError`. Its general fail-open fallback

  uncertainty returns generic retryable 503 copy and omits quota reset/retry
  metadata; actual exhaustion remains 429. Checkout and verification security
  diagnostics distinguish provider outage from quota exhaustion. The billing
  verifier covers all eight routes, while tenant-safety additionally locks the
  four subscription-mutation paths. Valid provider, transaction, idempotency,
  response, entitlement and cache behavior is unchanged.

## Restart 1480 addendum — owner AI reservation, project authority, output, and limiter convergence

This forward paid-provider trace re-read Business Copy, SEO, Campaign Caption,
and the dormant Review Suggest route from authenticated request through rate
admission, permission, tenant/project authority, capacity, provider output,
accounting and final response. Four defects were confirmed and closed. This is
not a full clean pass; `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains `0`.

### AUDIT-AI-PUBLIC-COPY-RESERVATION-001 — Business Copy and SEO paid work could never settle

- **Severity/status/flow:** P1 / Closed in restart 1480; authenticated owner
  request → permission/capacity check → Gemini → exact output projection → AI
  operation settlement → owner response.
- **Observed/root cause:** both routes called `checkAICapacity()` and paid
  Gemini, but never called `reserveAiCapacity()`. The shared accounting
  finalizer intentionally rejects every positive-unit operation without its
  pre-provider reservation, so otherwise valid output ended as HTTP 500 after
  provider cost and without a consumed operation row.
- **Security/data/billing impact:** this did not debit another tenant or
  corrupt a payment, but it defeated concurrency-safe credit admission,
  stranded provider cost outside a successful owner operation, and made the
  two generation flows deterministically fail at settlement.
- **Fix/compatibility:** each route now reserves the effective subscription
  after capacity admission and before Gemini, passes that reservation to the
  finalizer, clears it only after successful settlement, and safely refunds it
  from `finally` on provider, parse, projection, or settlement failure. Request
  and successful response DTOs are unchanged. The accounting verifier now
  includes both routes in the paid-provider reservation ordering matrix.

### AUDIT-CAMPAIGN-CAPTION-PROJECT-AUTHORITY-001 — project attribution checked the session against itself

- **Severity/status/flow:** P1 / Closed in restart 1480; optional request
  `projectId` → project association in prompt/accounting context → generated
  owner caption.
- **Observed/root cause:** when `projectId` was supplied, the route called
  `verifyTenantAccess(session, session.tId, session.sId, request)`. That proves
  only that the authenticated session matches itself; it did not validate the
  project ID's encoded tenant/store scope or document existence. A caller with
  otherwise valid store permission could attribute paid work to a foreign,
  deleted, blocked, or fabricated project ID.
- **Fix/security/data impact:** `getSessionProjectAccessBlockReason()` now
  exact-normalizes session and project scope, rejects mismatched tenant/store
  identities, reads only the canonical scoped project path, and rejects
  missing, deleted, or platform-blocked documents before capacity/provider
  work. No persisted schema changed. The optional project path adds one Admin
  read; requests without a project add none.

### AUDIT-CAMPAIGN-CAPTION-PROVIDER-DTO-001 — arbitrary provider fields reached the owner response

- **Severity/status/flow:** P2 / Closed in restart 1480; Gemini JSON → phrase
  guard → operation summary → owner response/copy consumer.
- **Observed/root cause:** the parser returned `Record<string, any>` and the
  route checked only that the top level was an object. Unknown fields, mixed
  hashtag values, overlong strings, or missing declared fields could pass into
  the response; only truthy caption fields were phrase-guarded.
- **Fix/public-truth/backward compatibility:** the shared
  `campaignCaptionOutput` boundary accepts only usable string `caption` and
  `shortCaption` plus a string hashtag array, normalizes/caps the fields,
  deduplicates and caps hashtags at five, and returns exactly those three
  fields. Malformed output follows the existing generic failure/refund path.
  Focused behavior tests cover malformed types, required fields, caps,
  normalization, deduplication and unknown-field omission.

### AUDIT-REVIEW-SUGGEST-LIMITER-FAIL-CLOSED-001 — limiter outage admitted dormant paid work

- **Severity/status/flow:** P2 / Closed in restart 1480; enabled review reply
  request → per-user distributed limiter → permission/capacity reservation →
  Gemini/fallback → accounting.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** the direct limiter used its default provider-
  error bypass, so an Upstash outage could admit paid provider work and was
  indistinguishable from quota exhaustion. The feature remains disabled, but
  activation would have inherited the fail-open cost boundary.
- **Fix:** limiter infrastructure uncertainty now fails closed and returns 503;
  actual exhaustion remains 429. The accounting source gate locks both the
  fail-closed option and status distinction. No feature flag was enabled.

## Restart 1479 addendum — Customer App public dynamic asset convergence

This forward public-output trace re-read the dynamic icon, startup-image and
screenshot routes, the complete shared renderer/URL contract, public store
lookup, anonymous limiter semantics, manifest consumers, owner-upload
authority, Customer App docs and the owning aggregate. Four runtime defects

### AUDIT-CUSTOMER-APP-DYNAMIC-ASSET-LIMITER-FAILOPEN-001 — provider outage still admitted expensive public work

- **Severity/status/flow:** P2 / Closed in restart 1479; anonymous asset request
  → hashed IP limiter → public store read → server image render.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** all three routes used the limiter's default
  provider-error bypass. During an Upstash outage, random store-ID probes could
  continue causing Firestore reads and image generation even though the route
  already had a safe generic fallback. Tenant identity was not confused, but
  cost and availability protection failed open.

  `failClosedOnProviderError: true` before store lookup. The Customer App source
  gate requires this on every route; the full aggregate passes.

### AUDIT-CUSTOMER-APP-DYNAMIC-ASSET-CACHE-POISON-001 — transient generic fallbacks were shared-cacheable

- **Severity/status/flow:** P1 / Closed in restart 1479; rate-limit/provider or
  render failure → generic image → browser/CDN cache → later install consumers.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** generic fallback responses reused the
  stable branded asset policy (`s-maxage=86400`, one-week stale window). A
  rate-limited miss or transient renderer failure could therefore replace the
  branded shared response for unrelated users. Transient failure output must
  never become public truth.
- **Fix/cache/backward compatibility:** a shared `private, no-store,
  max-age=0` policy now covers invalid/rate-limited/provider-failure and caught
  render-failure assets. Successful public-safe and stable missing-store output
  retains the existing CDN policy and URL/version contract.

- **Severity/status/flow:** P1 / Closed in restart 1479; persisted public store
  logo/override → icon-source projection → `ImageResponse` server fetch.
- **Observed/root cause/security impact:** `resolveCustomerAppIconSource`
  accepted any string ending in a raster extension, including HTTP,
  credential-bearing, localhost, IP-literal, arbitrary-host and foreign-bucket
  values. A malformed or legacy owner-controlled store record could induce a
  server-side fetch outside MenuList-owned storage.
- **Fix/legacy behavior:** server-rendered images now require bounded HTTPS,
  no credentials or port, an exact Firebase/Google Storage host, the configured
  MenuList bucket, and a raster path. Invalid legacy values deterministically
  render the generated mark; stored data is not rewritten. Tests cover every
  rejected class and trusted configured-bucket admission.

- **Severity/status/flow:** P2 / Closed in restart 1479; path/persisted display
  identity → render dimensions/text → generated PNG.

  noncanonical paths could select a supported size unexpectedly.

  rendered business names normalize whitespace and cap at 120 characters.
  Screenshot taglines retain their existing 120-character cap. Focused tests

## Restart 1478 addendum — Answerlattice analytics authorization, range, limiter, and write convergence

The forward and reverse analytics trace re-read the ROI and weekly-insight
routes, their shared contracts, the analytics DAL, owning UI permission, docs,
and source gates. Four new defects were confirmed and closed. This was a
targeted restart, not a full clean pass; `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains

### AUDIT-AL-ROI-PERMISSION-001 — ROI aggregates lacked the owning support permission

- **Severity/status/flow:** P1 / Closed in restart 1478; authenticated request
  → exact Answerlattice workspace → aggregate DAL → private ROI response.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** the ROI route resolved the exact
  workspace but omitted the `MANAGE_SUPPORT` permission required by the owning
  Conversations surface, allowing a direct authenticated workspace member to
  read conversation and feedback aggregates.
- **Root cause/impact:** route authorization drifted from its consumer. Tenant
  identity remained exact, but role confidentiality and private analytics were
  not enforced consistently; no public cache or persisted shape changed.
- **Fix/regression:** the route now checks `MANAGE_SUPPORT` before the DAL read
  and attaches private response headers on success and failure. Tenant-safety
  and Answerlattice runtime gates require permission, ordering, and private
  caching behavior.

### AUDIT-AL-ROI-RANGE-OFF-BY-ONE-001 — N-day ROI included N+1 UTC buckets

- **Severity/status/flow:** P2 / Closed in restart 1478; day query → completed
  daily documents → current live bucket → ROI totals.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** a request for N days read N completed days
  plus today, and historical date arithmetic used local time. The contract is
  exactly N UTC buckets: N-1 completed days plus today; one day means today
  only.
- **Impact/fix/compatibility:** counts, rates, and ROI could be overstated and
  month boundaries could drift by runtime timezone. A shared UTC trailing
  window helper now drives the DAL and skips historical reads for `days=1`.
  The response shape is unchanged; month-boundary and one-day cases protect
  legacy callers.

- **Severity/status/flow:** P2 / Closed in restart 1478; weekly refresh request
  → scoped limiter → analytics reads → weekly insight write.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** provider failure used the generic allowed
  fallback and was indistinguishable from quota exhaustion. The mutation could
  proceed during limiter outage and an outage was reported as 429.
- **Fix/regression:** the route now requests fail-closed provider behavior,
  maps provider outage to 503 and genuine exhaustion to 429, and retains the
  exact workspace scope. Runtime and tenant source gates assert the boundary.

### AUDIT-AL-WEEKLY-INSIGHT-TRANSACTION-001 — concurrent or stale refresh could overwrite weekly truth

- **Severity/status/flow:** P2 / Closed in restart 1478; completed-week inputs
  → deterministic source hash → weekly insight document.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** a nontransactional get-then-set allowed
  duplicate concurrent writes and let a slower request for an older week
  replace the newer weekly document. This affected derived owner truth and
  write cost, not billing or public MenuList data.
- **Fix/compatibility:** a pure decision contract classifies the attempted
  write as `write`, `current`, `superseded`, or `invalid`; an Admin transaction
  now applies that decision atomically. Newer weeks win and identical
  week/hash refreshes avoid a write. Persisted schema and readers remain
  compatible.
- **Regression:** contract tests cover identical refresh, changed source,
  older-week arrival, newer-week arrival, and invalid persisted state; runtime
  verification requires the transaction fence.

The current shared Creative Editor, Fabric adapter, element builders, smoke

full pass and `consecutiveCleanFullPasses` remains `0`.

### AUDIT-CREATIVE-EDITOR-NETWORK-IMAGE-SCHEME-001 — imported documents admitted ephemeral and non-web image schemes

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**
  `AUDIT-CREATIVE-EDITOR-NETWORK-IMAGE-SCHEME-001` / P2 / Closed locally in
  restart 1466.
- **File/function/flow/structure:**
  `src/modules/creative-editor/CreativeEditor.tsx::{isSafeCurrentImageSource,
  isSafeImportedImageSource}`, `imageSourceBoundary.ts`; owner JSON/Fabric
  import or current document → image-source classification → Fabric load →
  autosave/template/export.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** the earlier hardening rejected only
  `data`, `file`, `javascript` and `vbscript` schemes before accepting any
  other non-SVG string. A persisted import could therefore admit an ephemeral
  `blob:` URL or schemes such as `ftp:` and later save/export a document whose
  image could not be reliably or safely reloaded.
- **Expected/root cause/security/data/public/cache impact:** persisted/editor

### AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-SEARCH-HISTORY-OPTIONAL-REPLAY-ADMISSION-001 — malformed optional cache fields were silently coerced

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**
  `AUDIT-ANSWERLATTICE-SEARCH-HISTORY-OPTIONAL-REPLAY-ADMISSION-001` / P2 /
  Closed locally in restart 1405.
- **File/function/flow/structure:**
  `src/database/aiSearchHistory/server.ts`,
  `compactAiSearchHistoryPayload` and
  `findCachedSearchByCacheKeyServer`; authenticated help/widget/API search →
  canonical/FAQ/RAG result → compact `aiSearchHistory` write → tenant/store
  and hashed-key lookup → response replay into `searchCore`.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** the writer spread the complete input
  before selectively normalizing optional fields. Invalid clarification,
  matched-entity and source-version values could therefore remain persisted.
  On read, malformed clarification was reduced to its valid subset, malformed
  entity arrays were filtered/truncated, arbitrary source-version objects were
  returned, document IDs were accepted without the authoritative ID
  boundaries, and persisted scope aliases were compared through `Number`.
  The remaining answer could be returned as a valid cache hit despite no
  longer representing the stored response contract.
- **Expected/root cause/security/data/public/cache impact:** cached answers
  must replay only when the complete persisted response is canonical and
  belongs to the exact numeric product/tenant/store scope. The Firestore query
  already constrained numeric scope, so no demonstrated cross-tenant read was
  found. Silent coercion could nevertheless replay an incomplete or
  misattributed governed answer, omit required clarification, lose evidence
  identity and bypass source-version freshness semantics.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** the writer now deletes each controlled
  optional field before adding its canonical projection. Canonical/FAQ/entity
  IDs use their authoritative document-ID boundaries; fallback reason,
  clarification and source versions are bounded; entity IDs are normalized
  and deduplicated. The reader requires exact numeric scope and exact canonical
  optional shapes, failing closed rather than transforming corrupted rows.
  Existing valid version-2 rows remain replayable; malformed rows remain
  analytics records but are no longer response-cache truth.
- **Regression/validation:** the real Firestore emulator now seeds malformed
  clarification, duplicate/whitespace entity IDs, string-coerced source
  versions and whitespace-mutated canonical IDs and proves each returns a
  cache miss. `npm run test:answerlattice-search-cache:emulator`,
  `node scripts/verification/verify-answerlattice-runtime-truth.js`, exact
  root `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false`, focused ESLint and
  `git diff --check` pass.
- **Re-audit pass in which confirmed closed:** restart 1405; convergence reset
  to zero.

### AUDIT-CUSTOM-DOMAIN-AVAILABILITY-HTTP-STATUS-001 — service failures looked like claimed domains

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**
  `AUDIT-CUSTOM-DOMAIN-AVAILABILITY-HTTP-STATUS-001` / P2 / Closed locally in
  restart 1432.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** `src/database/stores/index.tsx`,
  `checkCustomDomainAvailability`; desktop/mobile custom-domain input →
  authenticated availability GET → bounded response projection → owner
  availability state.
- **Observed/root cause:** the route deliberately returns a bounded
  `{ available: false, reason }` body with HTTP 429 or 503 when rate limiting
  or its provider is unavailable. The DAL validated the body but ignored
  `response.ok`, so both owner surfaces displayed that operational failure as
  a successful “domain unavailable” answer instead of entering their existing
  error/retry path.
- **Expected/security/data/public/cache impact:** only a successful 2xx
  availability response may update domain-availability state. Authorization,
  tenant/store scope and claim writes were unaffected; no persistence or cache
  mutation occurs on this advisory read. The defect produced incorrect owner
  decision truth and hid a retryable failure.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** the DAL now rejects every non-2xx response
  before admitting the bounded availability DTO. Valid available/unavailable
  2xx responses are unchanged.
- **Regression/validation:** the custom-domain source gate now requires the
  HTTP-status admission check. `node

### AUDIT-AL-KB-RETRY-SENTINEL-PAYLOAD-001 — retry handed Firestore delete sentinels to the development callable

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**
  `AUDIT-AL-KB-RETRY-SENTINEL-PAYLOAD-001` / P2 / Closed locally in restart
  1429.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** `src/database/kb-generation/jobs.ts`,
  `retryJob`; failed job → transaction-current retry mode → Firestore reset →
  development generation/publishing callable → owner acknowledgement.
- **Observed/root cause:** generation retry used the correct `deleteField()`
  update values, then spread that Firestore update object into `resetJob`.
  Outside production, `resetJob` is sent to a callable, so its payload contained
  sentinel objects rather than the authoritative post-commit job shape.
- **Expected/security/data/public/cache impact:** Firestore update sentinels
  belong only in the transaction update. Queue/callable and response DTOs must
  contain ordinary serializable job data with deleted fields absent. Scope and
  platform authorization were correct; no cross-tenant access or public/cache
  impact was found. The defect could break local/QA retry dispatch or supply
  invalid lifecycle state to the development trigger.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** retry now keeps a precise Firestore update
  object and a separate serializable response projection. Generation-only
  deleted fields are explicitly removed from the response/callable job, while
  the transaction continues using `deleteField()` and `update()`.
- **Regression/validation:** the Answerlattice runtime source verifier now
  requires the split projection and forbids spreading the Firestore update
  into `resetJob`. Category-mutation and ingestion-deletion boundaries,
  dedicated KB publishing emulator, runtime source verifier, exact TypeScript,
  focused ESLint and `git diff --check` pass.
- **Re-audit pass in which confirmed closed:** restart 1429; convergence reset
  to zero.

### AUDIT-IMAGE-BATCH-TERMINAL-UNSTAGED-CLEANUP-001 — terminal jobs falsely reported an unstaged upload as retained

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**
  `AUDIT-IMAGE-BATCH-TERMINAL-UNSTAGED-CLEANUP-001` / P2 / Closed locally in
  restart 1428.
- **File/function/flow/structure:**
  `src/database/imageBatchProcessing/server.ts`,
  `markImageBatchItemAttemptFailedAdmin`; claimed worker item → provider
  generation → tenant/store Storage upload → attempted staged result → terminal
  job transition → failure settlement → Storage cleanup.
- **Observed/root cause:** the terminal branch unconditionally returned
  `retainsStagedResult: true` before examining the item execution. If
  cancellation committed after upload but before staging, the worker therefore
  treated its unreferenced files as authoritative and skipped deletion.
- **Expected/security/data/public/cache impact:** an exact still-processing
  claim with no staged item/accounting must report that nothing was retained,
  allowing the worker to delete only its own locally known uploaded paths.
  Stale claims and genuinely staged executions must remain protected to avoid
  deleting another delivery's or authoritative media. The defect caused
  orphaned tenant-scoped Storage objects and cost/retention drift; no public
  URL was persisted and no cross-tenant access was found.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** terminal settlement now inspects the exact
  execution. It reports no retained result only for the matching processing
  claim with no staged data; every ambiguous, stale or staged case remains
  retention-safe.
- **Regression/validation:** the real concurrency emulator now proves the
  cancellation-before-stage result is not reported as retained. Image-batch
  server/retention boundaries, the full AI accounting aggregate, Firestore
  rules, the real concurrency emulator, exact TypeScript, focused ESLint and
  `git diff --check` pass.

  to zero.

## Restart 1425 addendum — Answerlattice conversation pagination after runtime filtering

### AUDIT-AL-CHAT-ANALYTICS-PAGINATION-FILTER-001 — malformed rows could terminate or duplicate conversation pagination

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**
  `AUDIT-AL-CHAT-ANALYTICS-PAGINATION-FILTER-001` / P2 / Closed locally in
  restart 1425.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** `src/database/chatAnalytics/index.ts`
  `getConversationsPaginated`; exact workspace query ordered by `modifiedOn`
  → `pageSize + 1` raw snapshots → strict session projection → browser page and
  continuation cursor.
- **Observed/root cause:** continuation was calculated from the post-projection
  array. A malformed or legacy row filtered by the runtime parser reduced that
  array below the page threshold, so `hasNextPage` became false even when the
  raw query proved later data existed. A vanished cursor silently restarted at
  page one. Naively mixing a raw cursor with all projected `pageSize + 1` rows
  would also duplicate the lookahead record.
- **Expected/security/data/public/cache impact:** pagination state must follow
  raw ordered Firestore truth while response entries remain strictly
  projected. Missing or cross-scope cursors must fail closed. Query product,
  tenant and workspace predicates were correct, so no cross-tenant exposure
  was found. The defect could hide or duplicate private support conversations;
  it does not affect persistence, public output or cache keys.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** only the first `pageSize` raw documents are
  projected for the returned page; `hasNextPage` comes from the raw
  `pageSize + 1` snapshot, and the continuation cursor is the last raw document
  in that page. A missing cursor now rejects instead of restarting. Valid
  datasets retain the same page contract.
- **Regression/validation:** the owning runtime source gate requires the raw
  page slice, raw continuation test, raw cursor and missing-cursor rejection.
  Chat analytics contracts, the complete Answerlattice runtime source gate,
  dedicated/shared Firestore rules, exact TypeScript, focused ESLint and
  `git diff --check` pass.
- **Re-audit pass in which confirmed closed:** restart 1425; convergence reset
  to zero.

### AUDIT-PWA-ICON-PERSISTED-CLEANUP-RACE-001 — prior icon deletion could race a concurrent restore

- **Finding ID/severity/status:**
  `AUDIT-PWA-ICON-PERSISTED-CLEANUP-RACE-001` / P1 / Closed locally in restart
  1413.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** `src/database/pwa/index.ts`,
  replacement/removal → `cleanupSupersededPWAIconUrl`; committed
  `stores.publicPresence.pwaIconOverrideUrl` → server-only read guard →
  Firebase Storage delete → public manifest/icon consumer.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** after a replacement or removal
  committed, the client re-read current Firestore truth and deleted the prior
  owned object if it was no longer referenced. A concurrent save could restore
  that prior URL after the read but before deletion, leaving current public
  truth pointing at deleted bytes.

## Restart 1410 addendum — font-preset sort collection and batch ceiling

### AUDIT-FONT-SORT-BOUNDED-BATCH-001 — sort read and write cardinality was unbounded

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** `AUDIT-FONT-SORT-BOUNDED-BATCH-001` / P2 /
  Closed locally in restart 1410.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** `src/database/static/fontPresets.ts`,
  `sortFontsPresets`; platform drag order → ID/index map → full
  `common/assets/fontPreset` read → batched index updates.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** ordinary font reads probe at 501 and
  reject collection overflow, but sorting used an unlimited collection read
  and did not cap the caller list. At 501 matching rows it constructed 501
  writes, exceeding Firestore's 500-operation batch limit; larger corrupted
  collections also created an unbounded platform read before failure.
- **Expected/root cause/security/data/public/cache impact:** this finite shared
  registry must enforce its 500-row invariant before write construction and
  probe only one row beyond the ceiling. The defect caused avoidable reads and
  a guaranteed failed sort at overflow, leaving public font ordering stale. It
  did not weaken platform-only write rules, tenant isolation, billing or cache
  partitioning.
- **Fix/backward compatibility:** sort now rejects non-array/over-500 input,
  reads at most 501 persisted rows, rejects persisted overflow, then verifies
  exact set equality before building the batch. Valid registries and ordering
  behavior are unchanged.
- **Regression/validation:** the Storage source gate pins both input and query
  bounds. Complete `npm run verify:storage-paths`, font sort behavior,
  immutable-media Storage rules, `npm run test:common-assets:rules`, exact
  TypeScript, focused ESLint and `git diff --check` pass.

## Restart 1409 addendum — MenuList subscription scope and paid AI lifecycle
